N12 In requirements: BR-002 · BR-007 · FR-008 · FR-011 · FR-058 · FR-065 · FR-091 · NFR-P-003and 6 more
Replay horizon
How long past decisions can be re-run, and what serves as the record after that.
In requirements: DR-008
Reportable circumstance
A fatality, critical injury or serious incident involving a child or youth that meets the tests policy sets, and so must be reported within the time limit policy sets to the people and bodies entitled to the report (FR-337 to FR-339).
Retention schedule
The official list of how long each kind of government record must be kept.
Government records are kept for set periods and then destroyed or archived. A schedule might say case files are kept for a set number of years after the case closes. Deleting a whole kind of record when its time comes is the default method in N12, and most kinds of record end this way.
Used in:
[aria-label] N12: How records are destroyed is decided before anything is stored
N12
Rules engine
The software that applies the entitlement rules to a client’s facts to reach a decision.
The rules for each benefit are written down in a form a computer can follow. The rules engine takes those rules and a client’s facts, and works out the result. Each version of the rules, and each version of the engine, is kept, so an old decision can be replayed exactly as it was made.
N07 asks that the engine is sealed off: it may use only what it is handed, never the clock, a database or another service.
Used in:
[aria-label] N07: The calculation uses only what it is given
N07 ·
[aria-label] N08: The decision record is complete on its own
N08 In requirements: FR-001 · FR-102 · FR-061 · FR-090 · FR-095
Rules register
The list of every policy rule with its source page, effective dates and status, held apart from the requirements so that dollar amounts and day counts live in one place.
In requirements: BR-014 · FR-010 · FR-016 · FR-037 · FR-048 · FR-101
Safety plan agreement
An agreement made under Division 1.1 of Part 3 of the CFCSA. Policy describes it as a voluntary plan to keep the child or youth safe until the assessment or investigation has concluded, or when a court order has been applied for but not yet granted.
SBOM, penetration test
A software bill of materials lists every component in a system; a penetration test is an authorised attack to find weaknesses.
In requirements: NFR-SEC-007 · NFR-C-006
Secure Data Exchange
The Province's gateway for sharing personal information between ministries. All cross-ministry traffic goes through it.
In requirements: INT-013
Separation of duties
Making sure no one person controls every step, so each step checks the one before.
Policy sets three separations. The person who reviews a decision cannot be the one who made it. The person who speaks for the ministry at an appeal cannot be either of them. And working out a payment, approving it and releasing it are done by different people. N17 asks the system to enforce these, rather than leaving it to rosters.
Used in:
[aria-label] N17: Different people decide, review and pay
N17 In requirements: BR-004 · FR-047
Service line
One of the eight areas of the ministry's work that each requirement is tagged with: child protection and family services, guardianship, adoption and permanency, youth transitions, children and youth with support needs, early years and inclusion, children and youth mental health, and youth justice. A requirement that applies to all of them is tagged ministry-wide.
In requirements: NFR-SEC-013
Set-off
Recovering a debt by deducting it from another amount the ministry owes the same person.
In requirements: FR-048 · FR-052 · FR-060 · INT-007
Severing
Removing protected details from a record before it is released.
A record given to a client can contain information they are not entitled to see, such as details about another person. FOIPPA says which details must be removed first. Doing this by hand on a large record is slow and easy to get wrong. N08 asks that the decision record can be severed on demand.
Used in:
[aria-label] N08: The decision record is complete on its own
N08
Shadow comparison
Running the new system's calculation on the same inputs as the old one and classifying every difference before switching over.
In requirements: BR-001 · INT-023 · DR-003 · DR-014
Shadow root, shadow DOM
A browser feature that hides a component's inner structure. It can break links assistive technology relies on.
In requirements: NFR-U-004
Shred-survivor set
The fixed list of facts that stay readable after a person's records are destroyed, such as payment totals and disclosure records.
In requirements: FR-008 · FR-077 · NFR-C-003 · DR-004
Significant measure
A measure for an Indigenous child that needs prior notice to the parent, the care provider and the Indigenous governing body. The federal Act does not define the term; policy lists the measures under the CFCSA that count, and the system holds that list as dated reference data (FR-136).
In requirements: INT-028
SLO, SLA, error budget
A service level objective or agreement is a stated performance target; the error budget is how much failure the target allows.
In requirements: NFR-SEC-004 · NFR-M-001
SOP (standard operating procedure)
A ministry procedure telling staff how to do a task. SOPs are evidence of current practice, not the authority for a requirement.
Source (provenance)
Where a fact came from: who said it, and which record it was taken from.
Architects call this provenance. It is what lets you judge how far to trust a fact, and what lets a correction find every copy that needs fixing. Once a fact is passed on without it, it cannot be added back later.
Used in:
[aria-label] N02: Parts of the system share facts and decisions, not raw data
N02 ·
[aria-label] N06: Every copy can be traced, and every correction reaches it
N06 In requirements: DR-010
Source hierarchy (Tier 1, 2, 3)
The ranking of sources used to decide what the system must do: Tier 1 is legislation, Tier 2 is the policy manual, Tier 3 is practice (procedures, job aids, spreadsheets). A higher tier wins any conflict.
Special needs agreement
A written agreement under section 7 of the CFCSA by which a parent keeps custody and gives the director care of a child with a special need. Policy defines a special need as a documented significant impairment that requires specialized care and support.
Specified adult
A person at or over the age the CFCSA sets for whom services under the Act, or Indigenous child and family services, were provided while the person was a child (CFCSA section 1). A director may make an agreement with a specified adult who meets the regulation's criteria (FR-224).
In requirements: DR-028
Statutory administrative decision
A decision made under a law about a person's rights or benefits. It carries a duty to give reasons and a right to challenge.
Statutory basis
The section of a law or regulation that grants an entitlement.
In requirements: BR-003 · FR-092 · FR-099
Statutory decision-maker
The person the law gives authority to make a program's decisions. Only they can approve a class of decisions to be issued without human review.
In requirements: FR-093
Store
A place where data is kept, such as a database.
The new system has many stores. Some are built to answer questions quickly and are refreshed from the main history a moment after it changes. That short delay is normal, but it means a store can be briefly behind. N09 is about what a decision must do about that.
Used in:
[aria-label] N09: A decision records the moment its facts were read
N09
Subsidiary ledger
The ministry's own record of what it owes, pays and recovers, reconciled to the corporate financial system.
In requirements: FR-045 · FR-053 · FR-102 · FR-103 · NFR-U-002
Supervision order
A court order under the CFCSA that the director supervise a child's care, with the terms and conditions the court attaches. The director may apply for one without removing the child (FR-184, FR-193).
Support services agreement
A written agreement under section 5 of the CFCSA between a director and the parent of a child, for services or support to help the family care for the child.
Synchronous, asynchronous
Synchronous means the user waits for the answer; asynchronous means the work is queued and the answer comes later.
In requirements: NFR-A-003
System of record
The one system in charge of a record, whose version counts when there is a disagreement.
While the old and new systems run side by side, the same record may exist in both. N05 says only one of them may change it at a time, for each group of clients. The other system can read it, but cannot write to it.
Used in:
[aria-label] N05: Only one system can change a record at a time
N05 In requirements: FR-047 · NFR-A-009 · NFR-SEC-003
Target architecture
The architecture document (version 2) describing the system that replaces ICM and MIS.
In requirements: FR-099
Telemetry, observability, OpenTelemetry
Data a system emits about its own behaviour (logs, metrics, traces) so problems can be found; OpenTelemetry is the open standard for it.
In requirements: NFR-P-001 · NFR-C-004 · NFR-M-001
TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED, INDETERMINATE
TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED marks a determination answering a valid-time question from migrated facts whose old-system dates are unknown: it can show an amount but not what the ministry knew at the time. INDETERMINATE is what a knowledge-state question (what did the ministry know, and when?) returns on such a fact; it never substitutes the import date (DR-013; ADR-002).
In requirements: DR-013
Temporary custody order
A court order under the CFCSA that places a child in the custody of a director or of a person other than the parent for a term. The Act limits each term and the total time a child may spend in temporary custody (FR-192).
The old system (ICM and MIS)
The two systems that do the ministry’s case work today, and that the new system will replace.
ICM, short for Integrated Case Management, is a customer relationship management product adapted for government. MIS is a mainframe built in 1982. The two run side by side and share the core programs between them, so the site calls them together “the old system”.
For years the old and new systems will run side by side while groups of clients move across. The Current State page explains how the work is done today.

Threat model, runbook
A threat model lists how a part of the system could be attacked; a runbook is a written step-by-step procedure for operations staff.
In requirements: NFR-SEC-008 · NFR-C-006 · NFR-M-006
Three dates (tri-temporal)
Each fact records when it was true, when this system learned it, and, for migrated facts, when the old system recorded it.
Three-way reconciliation
Daily checking that the ministry's ledger, the bank's settlement files and the corporate financial system agree.
In requirements: NFR-P-002
Tier-1 component
A service whose failure stops payments or decisions, covered by 24-hour on-call.
In requirements: BR-013 · NFR-A-002 · NFR-M-006
TLS, mutual TLS, SFTP
Encryption for data in transit. Mutual TLS has both sides prove who they are; SFTP is secure file transfer.
In requirements: NFR-SEC-005 · INT-001
Tombstone
A marker left in place of destroyed data, so replay knows something was there and was lawfully destroyed.
In requirements: NFR-C-003 · DR-004 · DR-026
Transaction time
When the system learned a fact.
This is the date the fact was recorded, which is often later than when it became true. Together with valid time, it lets the ministry answer two separate questions a tribunal will ask: what was true, and what did the ministry know at the time? For records moved from the old system, this is the date they were moved. A third date, legacy assertion time, holds when the old system recorded them.

N01
Transition
The years when the old and new systems run side by side while clients move across.
Replacing a system this size is done in stages. During the transition, some clients are in the new system and some are still in the old one. Most of the risk in a replacement sits here, and several parameters are written for it.
Used in:
[aria-label] N05: Only one system can change a record at a time
N05
Translation layer
Temporary software that lets the new interfaces talk to the old system.
The new interfaces use the ministry’s words. The old system uses its own. The translation layer sits between them and converts one into the other. Architects call it an anti-corruption layer, because it stops the old system’s way of doing things leaking into the new design.
It is meant to be thrown away once the old system is gone. N10 asks that nobody mistakes it for something permanent.

N16 In requirements: NFR-P-001 · NFR-A-008 · NFR-I-001 · INT-023
Tribunal
An independent body that hears appeals against ministry decisions.
For most income and disability assistance decisions, this is the Employment and Assistance Appeal Tribunal. Some entitlements go to a different body, which is why N20 records the body for each one.
A tribunal will ask how a decision was reached and what the ministry knew at the time. Several parameters exist so the ministry can answer from the record rather than from memory.

N20 In requirements: INT-011
True-up
Working out, once the real decision is made, the difference between what an emergency payment paid and what was owed.
Valid time
The period during which a fact was true in the world.
A client’s income of $1,100 might be true from March to June. That period is its valid time. It is separate from when the ministry found out, which is transaction time, and from when the old system recorded it, which is legacy assertion time. Keeping all three lets the ministry recalculate the past correctly when it learns something late.

N01 In requirements: DR-001 · DR-010
Variant
A version of an entitlement with its own conditions, such as a supplement for one group of clients.
Some entitlements come in several forms. A variant can differ from its parent in who hears an appeal, or even in whether it can be reconsidered at all. N20 records these details for each variant, and never copies them from the parent.
Used in:
[aria-label] N20: Each benefit records whether and how a decision can be challenged
N20 In requirements: BR-003 · FR-033 · FR-092
Voluntary care agreement
A written agreement under section 6 of the CFCSA by which a parent keeps custody, gives care of the child to the director and delegates as much guardianship authority as the agreement needs. The child is in care while it runs.
Watermark
A marker recording exactly how far through the system’s history a decision read.
A decision reads its facts from a store that is filled from several streams of events, each updating on its own schedule. The watermark is the point in time up to which that store has applied every event from every one of those streams. It is set by the stream furthest behind. It is not the last event the decision happened to see, because a later event can arrive while an earlier one is still missing.
Writing the watermark into the decision record shows exactly which version of the facts the decision was based on. Setting a limit on how far behind a store may be stops a decision being made from an out-of-date view.

[aria-label] N09: A decision records the moment its facts were read

A task assigned to a person or team, with a due date, priority and history.

Copying changes from the new system back into the old one so its reports and interfaces keep working during the move.
In requirements: NFR-SEC-011 · NFR-M-003 · INT-023 · DR-014
Youth agreement
A written agreement under section 12.2 of the CFCSA between a director and a youth, who signs in their own right and is not a child in care. It includes a plan for independence, and the Act limits its term (FR-220 to FR-222).

A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.

Glossary
A PWD* designation granted in July.
It takes effect from March.
Four months of payments were right when the ministry made them. They are now an underpayment: four months a client went without money they turn out to have been owed. The current system keeps only today's answer. It rewrites history instead of recording it. What did we know, when did we know it, and how do we prove it? This design keeps all three.

Asked in Jun about May, the system reports a monthly entitlement of $1,060.
Current version of the record: At application in March, no disability designation is in place.
Today the system reports $1,535.50 for May. The payment actually made that month was correct when it was issued, and is now an underpayment of $475.50.
Move either slider. The left one changes the month you ask about. The right one changes the month you ask in. The hard edge across the grid is the July decision reaching back over every earlier month. That is what a backdated decision looks like when the system keeps both axes.
Current State
Two ministries run case management: Children and Family Development, and Social Development and Poverty Reduction. The work covers assistance payments, service requests, social work, loss recovery and client support. All of it depends on a worker seeing the full picture. The work is life-critical. A wrong answer means someone might not eat this month, or a child misses a check-in.
Two systems do the work. One is an Oracle Siebel customer relationship management product, adapted for government. The other is a mainframe built in 1982. They run side by side and share the core programs between them. Every attempt to retire the mainframe has stalled or failed.
The New Design is Built on Three Pillars
Evidence, not 'facts'
The system will not store "this person is an adult." It stores this: on 14 July, AI agent ID-33422 read the uploaded image of identification, matched it to the case, and read the date of birth as 22 April 1988. Business rules then decide the person is an adult. Who or what decided, when, and on what basis all sit in the record. They do not sit in an attached PDF, or outside the system altogether.
Evidence
Apt boundaries
Two ministries with broad mandates carry a very mixed portfolio. The current system forces all of it into one rigid model. That is how a design turns brittle. Here each program family gets its own model.
Domains
A decision you can re-run
Every entitlement decision stores the rules, the engine, the facts it saw, its own reasoning, the template of the letter the client was sent, how up to date its facts were, and what kind of decision it was. A manager four days later, or a tribunal years later, can re-run it instead of piecing it together from memory.
Determinations
Why do backdates matter?
Much of case management is building one clear timeline as information arrives. It does not arrive in order, and what turns up later can change what earlier events meant. In the backdated designation above, the client spent four months short of what they were owed. Someone on assistance has no savings to absorb that. The same machinery runs the other way too. It lands on the same person, who then has to pay the money back.
When someone is paid too much, the money falls into one of two classes. If the client's circumstances changed and they told the ministry late, it is a recoverable overpayment. The ministry takes it back at $10 a month, out of a payment that was already only just enough. If the ministry held the information all along and did not act on it, that is administrative error, and the client should not carry it.
Telling those two apart means knowing when the ministry knew. That is a transaction-time question. A system that records only when a fact was true cannot answer it. Nor can one that stamps every moved record with the date it moved. Almost the whole overpayment backlog sits in records from before any cutover.
Mispayment is one example of many. Evidence has to back nearly every claim a client makes. That cycle of claim, evidence and proof is the core loop of the whole service.
How this is modelled
Every evidence assertion carries three time dimensions: valid_time (the period in the world for which the fact holds), recorded_at (when this system learned it), and legacy_asserted_at (when the old system asserted it, where the old record still shows that).
The third axis is nullable. It carries a confidence value of DECODED, INFERRED or UNKNOWN. On UNKNOWN, any consumer working out a knowledge-state answer must return INDETERMINATE. It must not quietly substitute the migration timestamp.
None of this can be added later. Events are immutable: you can add a field with a default, but you cannot fill it in afterwards. The axis has to exist before the first production event.
What this site covers
These pages set out the domain model, and the thinking behind the least conventional choices. Each one leads in plain English and keeps the technical statement behind a disclosure.
The design comes from the law, from policy and from the nature of the work, not from the old system. Current State gives the context: how the work is done today, and what the design must not repeat. Parameters lists the twenty-one rules the design has to hold to, each with the check that catches a breach.

Parameters
The following parameters are the twenty-one proposed rules the design has to follow. Each one is written so a reviewer can point at something and judge whether it complies. Six of the parameters must be built in from the start; they cannot be added once the work has started.
What a parameter is
A parameter is something a system must comply with. A parameter must be check-able; it must be possible to check whether the system complies to it. To make sure that these rules are parameters, every entry below ends in a question you can put to a running system and get a wrong answer to.
The set makes three claims:
Every parameter is necessary: take one away and the design loses something nothing else supplies.
No two overlap: nothing is said twice.
And together they carry what the architecture is trying to do.
Each entry below demonstrates the first two claims. The third rests on an argument against a list of intents, and it is the weakest of the three, because another architect could reasonably draw some of these lines elsewhere.
The set

N07
The calculation uses only what it is given
While the system works out a decision, it doesn’t check the clock, look anything up in a database or call any other service. Everything it needs is handed to it at the start. The decision record is written from the result, and never feeds back into the calculation.
Why it is needed
This is what makes it possible to re-run a decision and get exactly the same answer, in practice and not just in theory. A rules service that fetches its own information ties every decision to systems that must still be running. That is the first thing a tribunal will look at.
How to check it
Give it the same rules, the same version of the engine and the same inputs. Do you get exactly the same result, down to the last character? Does it read the clock, its settings or any other service along the way?
Where it came from
Principle 8, narrowed to the calculation
Cannot be added later
The rules engine has to be sealed off before anyone writes the first rule
Words explained in the glossary
Decision (determination)
Rules engine
Replay
Decision record
Tribunal
Grouped by the part of the design each one covers. Select any parameter to see how to check it. A heavy left edge marks the six you cannot add later. Words with a special meaning are explained in the glossary, and each parameter links to the ones it uses.
Six cannot be added later
You can satisfy most of these late, at a price. Six you cannot. Each one has to be in place before a particular first event. Once that event has happened, the fix is a rebuild rather than a repair.
Before the first rule is written N07
The engine is sealed off from live data. A rule authored against a service it can call has already fixed the shape of every rule after it.
Before the first event is written N12, and the third date in N01
How records are destroyed is decided per class of fact. Events are immutable, so a date can be added with a default but never filled in afterwards.
As the first copy is made N06, N21
Where a copy came from, and what its source bars it from, are written at the moment of copying. Neither can be reconstructed later.
From the first decision N09
The point in the event sequence a decision read from goes into its record. Earlier decisions cannot be tied to a consistent view of the world.
Before the first group of clients moves N14
Moving them back is proven rather than claimed, and what the return trip loses is written down and approved.
The gates in the order delivery reaches them. This says what order the work has to happen in. It does not say which rules matter most.
Do first only what cannot be done later.
Where the twenty-one came from
Every principle in the architecture is accounted for. Seven carried across, with their wording narrowed or widened. Three split, because each held two ideas that could stand apart. One took in a clause from another, and one became more general. So twelve principles turned into fourteen parameters, and seven more joined them.
P1 split N01 · N02
P2 narrowed N08
P3 split N03 · N06
P4 absorbs P3(a) N03
P5 carried N04
P6 extended N11
P7 carried N10
P8 narrowed N07
P9 carried N05
P10 generalised N18
P11 split N12 · N13
P12 carried N14
Added N09 · N15 · N16 · N17 · N19 · N20 · N21
N09 closes a gap the architecture names in its own text. N15 and N16 close two more it had already recorded against itself. The last four came out of the policy manual, which turned out to state rules the architecture had never reached.
Those last four are the interesting ones, because nobody found them by thinking harder about the architecture. They came from reading what the ministry already tells its own staff to do. Policy sets time limits, and missing one changes what a client is owed. It names which entitlements a client can appeal, and to whom. It keeps the person who decides apart from the person who reviews. And it bars certain uses of information the ministry may lawfully hold. The twelve could not express any of that.
Where a parameter restates one of the architecture’s twelve principles, the architecture’s own wording wins if the two ever differ. The seven new ones are recorded as amendments to the architecture, each with a decision record. N16 is still a proposal.
A rule nobody can check is not a rule
One parameter is not about the system at all. N18 ranges over the other twenty. It makes each of them name how you catch a breach, and it says that anything you could write as a lint rule or a compatibility check has to be written as one.
It stands on its own rather than folded into the others. File a rule about enforcement among the rules about behaviour, and enforcement stops being anybody's job without anyone deciding that it should.

Business requirements 25
BR-001 Must
Entitlement is decided correctly, as policy states it
Every decision applies the statute and the policy rules in force for the period it covers, as policy states them. Show detail
Description
Every decision applies the statute and the policy rules in force for the period it covers, as policy states them. No worker should have to adjust a result by hand to reach the entitlement policy sets.
Rationale
A benefits system that calculates something other than the stated entitlement pays people wrongly, at scale. Policy states at least one entitlement the current system does not calculate. Today the gap is closed only when a worker notices it and adjusts the amount by hand OBLG-C1. A specification copied from the legacy system would carry that underpayment forward. The rules also have no single current date: the supplement rules alone carry 54 different effective dates OBLG-C3. Being correct means applying the right version of each rule to each period.
Success Criteria
Shadow comparison meets its exit criteria for every class of difference, across three monthly payment cycles in a row, on a group of clients whose cases are as complex as the real caseload. There are zero unresolved defects in the new system before any group of clients moves (FR-095).
Every rule a decision applies is named in its record by rule identifier and version, and every rule in the register carries a policy citation and effective date (FR-090, FR-091).
The entitlements that need manual adjustment today are calculated by the rules with no manual step. Test cases in the rules test suite prove it.
Drivers
DRV-01, DRV-09, DRV-10
Parameters
N01, N04, N07
Delivered by
FR-005, FR-007, FR-010, FR-033, FR-090, FR-091, FR-095
Stakeholder
Assistant Deputy Minister, Policy and Program Design
BR-002 Must
Every decision can be defended years after it is made
Any decision can be reproduced, explained and disclosed for as long as it can be reconsidered, appealed, reviewed or requested under access legislation. Show detail
Description
Any decision can be reproduced, explained and disclosed for as long as it can be reconsidered, appealed, reviewed or requested under access legislation. That means what was decided, on what facts, under which rules, and what the client was told.
Rationale
A tribunal asks what the ministry decided, on what basis, and what the client was told, and it often asks years later. A decision can only be reproduced if the calculation depends on nothing but its inputs, and if those inputs and outputs are stored in full when the decision is made TA-C3. A record that points to a running system is not evidence.
Success Criteria
For a randomly chosen adverse decision, the rule, the fact and where it came from, the reasons as issued, and the deadline to challenge that was stated can all be rebuilt from stored records alone, with no running system and no person involved (TA §C.8.5 test).
The replay horizon, and how decisions older than it will be evidenced, are set out in writing before the first live decision (FR-008).
The appeal record for any decision can be put together, and severed, on demand (FR-058, FR-078).
Drivers
DRV-02, DRV-03, DRV-11 (aim 1)
Parameters
N07, N08, N09
Delivered by

Stakeholder
Chief Architect, with the Reconsideration and Administrative Fairness Unit
BR-003 Must
Clients can always challenge a decision, and are told truthfully how
A client may ask for reconsideration of any communication, at any time, and the request is always recorded. Show detail
Description
A client may ask for reconsideration of any communication, at any time, and the request is always recorded. The client is told accurately whether a decision can be reconsidered or appealed, and where. Statutory deadlines are tracked by the system, and the ministry's own lateness never costs the client.
Rationale
Policy gives an unconditional right to ask for reconsideration. An independent unit decides whether reconsideration is available; the worker who sent the communication does not OBLG-C4. Whether a decision can be challenged differs by entitlement and by variant, and cannot be worked out from the parent program PRIN-C2. A missed statutory deadline changes what the client is owed PRIN-C1.
Success Criteria
No reconsideration request is refused at the point of contact on any channel, and every one is recorded with the date and channel it arrived on (FR-055).
Every entitlement and variant records its statutory basis, whether it can be reconsidered, whether it can be appealed, and to which body. The rights text in every notice is generated from those values (FR-092, FR-063).
Every breach of a statutory deadline is detected and recorded automatically, and its effect on entitlement is applied without anyone asking (FR-061).

BR-004 Must
Public money moves only under control, and people are paid even when the system fails
Every payment passes through one defined issuance point. Show detail
Description
Every payment passes through one defined issuance point. Separation of duties is enforced in the software. Payment runs never pay twice and can resume after a failure. Payments are reconciled daily against the corporate financial system in a three-way check. A planned, rehearsed emergency payment route exists before the first payment.
Rationale
A benefits system that calculates correctly but does not pay has failed completely. A single issuance point that is described but never specified cannot be built. If each program family builds its own link to the payment system, the controls exist once per program and are audited once per program TA-C4. Rolling back to the old system does not keep payments flowing: a client's rent is due on a date TA-C5.
Success Criteria
The five acceptance criteria for the issuance point in TA §C.6.8 pass before the first live payment (FR-042).
No payment is made outside a run, and there are no unexplained reconciliation breaks at month-end (FR-043, FR-045).
Emergency payment is exercised, at a load-tested share of a program's caseload, before M6 ends (FR-047).

BR-005 Must
Debt is raised fairly, and can be reversed in bulk
An overpayment is calculated as the difference between two decision records. Show detail
Description
An overpayment is calculated as the difference between two decision records. It is classified by what changed in the evidence, and raised only after a person decides it. Automatic raising is capped per cycle. Overpayments that share one cause are reviewed together as a group. A batch of overpayments can be reversed in one step, and any money already recovered is returned automatically.
Rationale
Another jurisdiction ran a debt-raising program that was found unlawful. It raised debts automatically from averaged income data and made recipients prove they did not owe. The controls against that failure are cheap to build only before any debts exist TA-C6. Whether a debt can be recovered depends on what the ministry knew and when, and only the evidence record captures that.
Success Criteria
No overpayment is raised without a recorded human decision-maker for each component (FR-052).
Every overpayment component is classified from the type of evidence change and the party at fault that caused it (FR-051).
A raised batch can be reversed in one step, with recovery reversed and corrected notices issued. This is shown in testing before the first live decision (FR-052).

BR-006 Must
Information is collected, used and disclosed lawfully by design
The system collects only what it needs. Show detail
Description
The system collects only what it needs. It discloses only where a legal basis is recorded. It enforces limits on how information may be used, wherever the information goes. It severs records before release, handles correction requests across every place the information is held, and can answer "whose information was accessed, by whom, and when" with a query.
Rationale
The original design had no part responsible for how the ministry manages the information it holds. About 15% of obligations had no part of the system to own them MAP-C1, and every unowned intake obligation was about managing information NOTE3-C1. Policy bars information the ministry holds lawfully from particular uses, in five different ways PRIN-C3. Severing works phrase by phrase inside free-text notes OBLG-C5.
Success Criteria
Every disclosure record names the recipient, the legal basis and the agreement. No access decision is made from any source other than the agreement registry (FR-077, FR-085).
Every barred use is blocked by default at the point of use, and each blocked attempt is recorded as an event (FR-080).
The people affected by a privacy breach can be listed by a query (NFR-C-001).

BR-007 Must
Records can be disposed of lawfully in a store that never overwrites
Before the first live event is written, the ministry decides for each kind of fact how long it is kept and how it is disposed of. Show detail
Description
Before the first live event is written, the ministry decides for each kind of fact how long it is kept and how it is disposed of. That includes the disposal method, the published list of what survives disposal, who holds the encryption keys, and what happens when a replay reaches a disposed fact. The ministry can then meet its disposal duties without destroying its financial and control records.
Rationale
A store that only ever adds records conflicts with a legal duty to destroy them. Settling that conflict after the first event means rebuilding the store. The authority for disposal comes from the Information Management Act and the ARCS/ORCS schedules, not from the policy manual OBLG-C2.
Success Criteria
Every kind of fact has a disposal method before the first live event (DR-004).
After a test disposal, financial control totals still reconcile to the same values as before (NFR-C-003).

BR-008 Must
Indigenous jurisdiction and custodianship are recorded accurately
The system records who is custodian of each fact for each person. Show detail
Description
The system records who is custodian of each fact for each person. It treats Indigenous governing bodies as their own class of participant outside the Crown, with their own legal bases. It supports transferring records to another sovereign government as a way of disposing of them. And it recognises designations made by another jurisdiction, while showing how current that recognition is.
Rationale
The Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act commits the Province to bringing its laws into line with the UN Declaration. A Nation's authority over its own data cannot be expressed as a retention rule or an access list. The participant class and the custodianship attribute have to be built in from the start, because they cannot be added once the registry and evidence types exist TA-C7.
Success Criteria
The system can read the custodian of every evidence type for every person, and every access decision traces to the agreement registry alone (FR-084, FR-085).
A transfer package can be produced, and the receiving body can check it without using ministry systems (FR-084).

Policy changes are fast, safe and dated

Policy staff can write, test and release a rule or rate change without a software release. Each change is versioned and takes effect on its own date, after review and legal sign-off. BR-011 Must
The legacy systems are replaced step by step, reversibly, and completely
Work moves from the legacy systems to the new system one part and one group of clients at a time. Show detail
Description
Work moves from the legacy systems to the new system one part and one group of clients at a time. There is exactly one writer per aggregate at every moment, per context and per cohort (N05). A published statement says what moving back would lose. The published interface outlives the legacy system behind it. Each legacy capability is shut down as its replacement goes live.

The vendor supports the legacy platform past 2037, so no outside deadline forces the replacement to finish TA-C10. The previous programme replaced about a third of the legacy systems and left the most important one running. Responsibility for records moves one part of the system at a time, never one field at a time TA-C11.

BR-015 Must

Description
For every child, the system records whether the child is an Indigenous child, each community, whether an Indigenous law or an agreement applies, and which Indigenous authority is responsible. It applies the terms of an applicable agreement to the work, supports referral of a report to an Indigenous authority and withdrawal from a proceeding at its request, and records every notice, consultation and placement decision the Acts require.
Rationale
The federal Act and the provincial Acts make these duties conditions of acting lawfully for an Indigenous child, and an agreement with a governing body binds every director in the province. BR-008 already requires custodianship and a class of participant outside the Crown; this requirement covers what the director must do case by case.
Success Criteria
No protection response, agreement, court step or placement for an Indigenous child proceeds without the recorded identity and applicable-law check (FR-110 to FR-142).
An agreement's terms are held once and applied to each child it covers; the registry of agreements (FR-085) and the register of agreements with governing bodies are one record.
Drivers
DRV-06, DRV-12, DRV-14
Parameters
N13, N17, N21
Delivered by
FR-110 to FR-142, FR-084, FR-085
Stakeholder
The Indigenous Child Welfare Director and the Provincial Director of Child Welfare, designated under the CFCSA
BR-017 Must
Every agreement and court step runs on its statutory time, with the record the court and the parties are owed
Agreements with families and each step of a court proceeding are recorded with their parties, required content, term and cumulative limits. Show detail
Description
Agreements with families and each step of a court proceeding are recorded with their parties, required content, term and cumulative limits. Notices are served on everyone entitled, hearings are tracked against their limits, and the prescribed reports to court are produced from the record.
Rationale
The Act fixes how long an agreement or order may run, who must be told of a hearing and what the court must be given. A term that passes unnoticed leaves a child in care with no legal basis.
Success Criteria
Every agreement and order has a recorded start, term and cumulative total, tested against the limit the Act sets for the child's age (FR-161 to FR-176, FR-177 to FR-195).
Every hearing has a recorded list of persons entitled to notice, with proof of service for each.
Drivers
DRV-12
Parameters
N08, N19, N20
Delivered by
FR-161 to FR-176, FR-177 to FR-195, FR-061
Stakeholder
The child protection practice authority, with legal counsel to the director
BR-018 Must
A child in care or in an out-of-care arrangement has a plan, a guardian's decisions and their rights on record
For each child in care, and each child placed with a care provider outside care, the system holds the plan of care and its reviews, the visits made, the health and consent decisions taken as guardian, the rights the child was told of, the checks made on the pe Show detail
Description
For each child in care, and each child placed with a care provider outside care, the system holds the plan of care and its reviews, the visits made, the health and consent decisions taken as guardian, the rights the child was told of, the checks made on the people caring for the child, and the plan for permanency.
Rationale
The director is the child's guardian or supervises the person who is. The Act sets the rights of children in care and the content of a plan of care, and policy sets how often a child is seen. Much of the policy that governs a child in care is not held (DEP-30), so several of these requirements are provisional.
Success Criteria
Every child in care has a current plan and a record of each review and each private visit (FR-211 to FR-225).
No child is placed with a care provider or caregiver whose required checks are not on record and current (FR-196 to FR-210, FR-226 to FR-234).
Drivers
DRV-12, DRV-17
Parameters
N01, N17, N19
Delivered by
FR-196 to FR-210, FR-211 to FR-225, FR-226 to FR-234
Stakeholder
The child protection practice authority
BR-019 Must
Adoption records hold the consents, notices and identity information the Adoption Act requires
The system supports adoption from planning to the order and after it: Show detail
Description
The system supports adoption from planning to the order and after it: consultation with Indigenous communities, matching, the proposal to adoptive applicants, placement, consents and their revocation, notices, the reports to court, registries, openness agreements and post-adoption assistance.
Rationale
An adoption changes a child's legal identity for life. A consent taken too early, a notice not given or a birth father not searched for can undo an order.
Success Criteria
No placement or application proceeds while a required consent, notice or consultation is not on record (FR-235 to FR-281).
The medical and social history, and an Indigenous child's community information, are preserved and can be given when the Act requires.
Drivers
DRV-13, DRV-14
Parameters
N08, N12, N21
Delivered by
FR-235 to FR-281
Stakeholder
The Provincial Director of Adoption
BR-020 Must
Services for children with support needs rest on recorded eligibility, consent and agreements
Eligibility for each support needs program is decided against the criteria policy sets and recorded with its evidence. Show detail
Description
Eligibility for each support needs program is decided against the criteria policy sets and recorded with its evidence. Services start on recorded consent. Requests are ranked for priority, and each service, agreement and payment is recorded with how it ended.
Rationale
These services are voluntary and rationed. A family is owed a written decision on eligibility and a record of where they stand.
Success Criteria
Every eligibility decision records the criteria met, the evidence and the decision-maker, and is given in writing (FR-282 to FR-296).
No service is recorded as started without the consent policy requires.
Drivers
DRV-12, DRV-17
Parameters
N01, N17, N20
Delivered by
FR-282 to FR-296, FR-297 to FR-298
Stakeholder
The program policy authority for children and youth with support needs
BR-021 Must
Only a person with the delegated authority acts, and every approval is recorded
The system holds every designation of a director and every delegation of a director's powers, with its category, limits and dates. Show detail
Description
The system holds every designation of a director and every delegation of a director's powers, with its category, limits and dates. It tests a worker's delegation before a power is exercised and records each approval policy requires from a supervisor, team leader or director.
Rationale
The Act lets a director delegate powers in writing. A removal or a consent given by a worker without the delegation is unlawful, and policy reserves named decisions to named positions.
Success Criteria
Any exercise of a director's power can be traced to a delegation in force on that date (FR-104 to FR-109).
Every decision that policy reserves to a named position shows who approved it and when.
Drivers
DRV-12
Parameters
N17
Delivered by
FR-104 to FR-109, FR-004, FR-094
Stakeholder
The Provincial Director of Child Welfare
BR-022 Must
Information about children and families is restricted, shared and disclosed as the Acts allow
Collection, use and disclosure follow the child protection statute where it applies and the privacy statute where it does not. Show detail
Description
Collection, use and disclosure follow the child protection statute where it applies and the privacy statute where it does not. Records are restricted where policy requires, kept apart where a statute bars their use by another service line, disclosed to the parties to a proceeding, and transferred complete when a family moves.
Rationale
One family can be served under two statutes at once, with different rules for sharing between them. Staff in one service line may not open another line's records without consent or a written request. BR-006 sets the general duty; this requirement covers the rules particular to children's services.
Success Criteria
Every disclosure names its legal basis under the governing Act (FR-299 to FR-315).
A user in one service line cannot open a record another line holds unless a recorded consent or request allows it.
Drivers
DRV-03, DRV-12
Parameters
N06, N13, N21
Delivered by

Stakeholder
The Ministry Privacy Officer
BR-023 Must
Money paid for a child's care is authorised, traceable and recoverable
Payments to caregivers, care providers, service providers and families are made on a recorded agreement or entitlement, approved by a person with the spending authority, and issued through the controls BR-004 sets. Show detail
Description
Payments to caregivers, care providers, service providers and families are made on a recorded agreement or entitlement, approved by a person with the spending authority, and issued through the controls BR-004 sets. A parent's contribution to a child's care is determined, agreed or ordered, and collected.
Rationale
Finance policy separates the people who request, approve and issue a payment. The Act keeps parents responsible for contributing to the care of a child in care.
Success Criteria
Every payment traces to an agreement or entitlement and to an approver whose authority covered it (FR-316 to FR-334).
Every parental contribution has an agreement or an order behind it.
Drivers
DRV-07, DRV-12
Parameters

Stakeholder
The Executive Financial Officer
BR-024 Must
Deaths, critical injuries, serious incidents and complaints are reported and reviewed on time
A reportable circumstance is recorded, approved and sent to those entitled to it within the limit policy sets, and screened for review. Show detail
Description
A reportable circumstance is recorded, approved and sent to those entitled to it within the limit policy sets, and screened for review. Requests for administrative review and complaints are taken by any means, tracked to an outcome, and never held against the person who made them.
Rationale
The regulation gives a person a right to an administrative review. Policy requires a report on a death or critical injury of a child who received services, and the review that follows depends on that report being made.
Success Criteria
Every reportable circumstance shows when the practitioner learned of it, when the report was approved and to whom it went (FR-335 to FR-348).
Every request for administrative review is recorded with the date it arrived and its outcome.
Drivers
DRV-12, DRV-17
Parameters

Delivered by

Stakeholder
The child protection practice authority
BR-025 Should
Mental health, integrated team and youth justice work is specified and held ready for the scope decisions
The requirements for child and youth mental health, the Integrated Child and Youth teams and youth justice are written from their own law and policy and kept in their own groups, so that each scope decision keeps or removes a whole group without rework. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE (conditional on DEP-26 to DEP-28)
Description
The requirements for child and youth mental health, the Integrated Child and Youth teams and youth justice are written from their own law and policy and kept in their own groups, so that each scope decision keeps or removes a whole group without rework.
Rationale
Each of these areas records its work today in a system other than the one being replaced, and nobody has decided whether the replacement covers them. Their statutes limit who may see their records: a youth justice record may not be seen by other service lines except as the federal Act allows.
Success Criteria
Each of DEP-26, DEP-27 and DEP-28 is decided before the discovery for module M9 closes.
Whatever is decided, a person index shared across service lines does not reveal youth justice or mental health involvement to a user who may not see it (FR-349 to FR-391, FR-406 to FR-434).
Drivers
DRV-15, DRV-16, DRV-17
Parameters
N03, N13, N21
Delivered by
FR-349 to FR-391, FR-392 to FR-405, FR-406 to FR-434, FR-435 to FR-481
Stakeholder

DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document, from 326 service-delivery procedures, and from 308 documents and 14 statutes and regulations on children and family services. Nothing here is a government commitment.

How facts are recorded and kept 21
