How facts are recorded and kept 21
DR-001 Must
Every fact carries three dates, fixed before the first event
Every fact carries three time axes. Show detail
Requirement
Every fact carries three time axes. It records when it was true (valid period) and when this system learned it (transaction time, recorded_at; for a migrated fact, always the import time, ADR-002). Facts from the old systems also record legacy_asserted_at, the date the old system recorded them, with a rating of how confidently that date could be decoded. This structure is fixed before the first production event is written.
Acceptance Criteria
A sample across fact classes, including facts from the old systems, shows for each fact its valid period, its recorded time and its old-system date (or an explicit UNKNOWN), and points to its source record.
Parameters
N01
Rationale
The third date cannot be added later under the rule that new record formats must stay readable alongside all earlier ones (decision D10). Without it, corrections and supersessions made before cutover cannot be told apart PRIN-C10.
DR-002 Must
Fact states and lifecycle
The data model represents four fact states: Show detail
Requirement
The data model represents four fact states: present, asserted negative, considered but not retainable, and disposed. It also represents four lifecycle states: asserted, active, superseded and invalidated. Invalidation is reserved for an assertion that should never have existed. Amended 2026-09-30 (ADR-004 §5): v1.3 read "An outside body, such as the tribunal, can invalidate a fact without a replacement determination." A tribunal rescission is recorded as external-determination evidence; the original determination stands, annotated, and the ministry re-determines.
Acceptance Criteria
Each state can be recorded and told apart at every point where data is captured and in every view built from it.
Parameters
N01, N08
Rationale
A determination record never changes, so even a rescinded decision stays in the record as what was decided (TA §C.8.4; ADR-004). Only an asserted negative can support a determination (PRIN N01, N08).
DR-003 Must
Security classification and storage placement for each fact class
Every fact class carries its security classification and is stored where that classification allows. Show detail
Requirement
Every fact class carries its security classification and is stored where that classification allows. So does everything derived from it, including indexes, extracted text, thumbnails, caches and shadow comparison results (NFR-C-004).
Acceptance Criteria
An inventory of where data is stored shows no Protected C data at rest outside the permitted stores.
Parameters
N12, N13
Rationale
A search index built over Protected C content is itself Protected C (TA §C.11.6).
DR-004 Must
Retention class and disposal method for each fact class
Before the first production event, each fact class is given exactly one disposal method: Show detail
Requirement
Before the first production event, each fact class is given exactly one disposal method:
class-wide disposal on a schedule;
keeping personal details in a separate store that can be deleted (reference-based indirection);
destroying one person's encryption key (per-subject cryptographic erasure);
permanent retention and transfer to the archives.
The shred-survivor list is published as a closed, versioned list. When a replay reaches a disposed fact, it returns a typed placeholder (a tombstone), never an error or a silent gap. Each disposal produces a signed certificate.
Acceptance Criteria
Every registered fact class has a method. A disposal run in test leaves the tamper-evident record chain verifiable and the financial control totals unchanged. The survivor list covers record header fields, the existence and outcome class of each determination, financial and recovery control facts, access-decision records, disclosure records and disposal certificates.
Added v1.6 (OB-LG4-40, RC-LG4-11, CK-LG4-17). Given a fact class that holds personal information used to make a decision that directly affects the individual, when its retention class is registered, then registration fails if the class could be disposed of sooner after that use than the minimum the Act sets (CK-LG4-17).
Parameters
N12, N08
Rationale
This cannot be added after the first event. The authority for it is the ARCS/ORCS records schedules, which the ministry must obtain first (decision D13; DEP-09).
DR-005 Must
Custodianship on every evidence type
Every evidence type records its custodian, governance regime, access conditions and transfer status. Show detail
Requirement
Every evidence type records its custodian, governance regime, access conditions and transfer status. These are worked out for each person at the moment of access.
Acceptance Criteria
For any evidence type and person, the custodian is a value the system reads, and the access policy checks it.
Parameters
N13
Rationale
A fixed value that cannot vary by person is what adding this later would produce (TA §B.8.2).
DR-006 Must
Limits on use recorded on facts
Facts record barred_from and permitted_for for each use. Show detail
Requirement
Facts record barred_from and permitted_for for each use. These limits exist from the moment the fact is first captured, and they travel with every copy.
Acceptance Criteria
A fact barred for one use and allowed for another is stored once. A copy test confirms the limit is still present on the copy.
Parameters
N21
Rationale
A limit missing at capture is missing from every copy made before it was added (PRIN §V).
DR-007 Must
Every copy records its source, and every copy can be found
When one part of the system copies evidence from another, it records the source at the moment of copying. Show detail
Requirement
When one part of the system copies evidence from another, it records the source at the moment of copying. For any fact, the system can list every part holding a copy. A correction at the source requires each of them to act, and a correction that goes unprocessed raises an alarm.
Amended 2026-09-30 (drift B6, B7; TA §B.3.3): every copy carries all five copy stamps, recorded at copy time:
Stamp
Content
source_context
The owning context of the original
source_evidence_id
The identity of the assertion copied
source_evidence_version
Which version of the succession set was copied
source_transaction_time
The owning context's recorded_at at the moment of the copy
copied_at
The consuming context's own transaction time for the copy
EvidenceCorrectionRecorded is a mandatory subscription: any context that holds a transform of an evidence assertion declares a subscription to corrections for that assertion's type in its manifest, and a fitness function checks the declaration at release. A context holding a derivative without a declared subscription fails its own pipeline. The on-premise continuity copy of NFR-A-009 is a registered derivative under this requirement (ADR-009).
Acceptance Criteria
A correction test at the source lists every copy and records what each part did. An unprocessed correction raises an alarm. Given a corrected evidence id, the derivative set is returned by a lookup over the five stamps, not by asking teams. A test context that holds a copy without declaring the subscription fails its release pipeline.
Parameters
N06, N18
Rationale
Copying data without being able to find the copies spreads it with no record of where it went (PRIN N06). Policy says nothing about passing corrections to parties already given the information, so this requirement rests on the architecture (OBLG §6).
DR-008 Must
Policy and rate history captured when first loaded
From the first day, every rule is captured with its policy citation and the effective date shown on its own block of text. Show detail
Requirement
From the first day, every rule is captured with its policy citation and the effective date shown on its own block of text. The archived rate tables are copied in once, not relied on where they sit. Older versions of policy text held by the ministry are kept under records retention for at least the replay horizon.
Acceptance Criteria
Every register row has its citation and effective date. The copied archive is kept under the programme's own retention.
Parameters
N01, N08
Rationale
The published archive has no retention statement and has gaps. Nothing can recover what was never published NOTE2-C1.
DR-009 Must
Data quality at the point of capture
Mandatory questions cannot be left blank, and "no" answers are captured as asserted negatives. Show detail
Requirement
Mandatory questions cannot be left blank, and "no" answers are captured as asserted negatives. Every correction must say who caused the error. Values a machine reads from documents stay unverified until someone verifies them. Every migrated fact carries its confidence rating.
Acceptance Criteria
Validation rejects blank mandatory questions and corrections that do not say who caused the error.
Parameters
N01, N18
Rationale
Gaps in these fields cannot be fixed afterwards, because the information was never captured.
DR-020 Must M0
Evidence & Verification is event-sourced, with the evidence succession set as its aggregate
Added 2026-09-30 (drift B6; Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
Added 2026-09-30 (drift B6; TA §B.2.1, §B.3). Numbered after DR-019 and placed here because it belongs with the evidence model.
Requirement
Evidence & Verification is event-sourced. Its aggregate is the evidence succession set: the stream of versions of one logical fact about one subject. The commands RecordEvidence, CorrectEvidence, SupersedeEvidence, VerifyEvidence and InvalidateEvidence append events to that stream; nothing is updated or deleted in place. Current state is a projection rebuilt from the events. The context publishes EvidenceRecorded, EvidenceActivated, EvidenceSuperseded, EvidenceVerified, EvidenceInvalidated and EvidenceCorrectionRecorded, under the domain-event compatibility class (NFR-I-003) and partitioned by aggregate (NFR-I-004). Every event carries the three time axes (DR-001).
Acceptance Criteria
The Evidence & Verification store has no update or delete path for evidence. Dropping every projection and replaying the streams from origin reproduces the current state exactly. Given any fact, its full succession of versions, with the operation that produced each, can be read back in order. A mutable table with an audit log does not satisfy this requirement.
Parameters
N01, N06, N08
Rationale
The difference between "the world changed" and "we were wrong" lives only in the succession of operations, and it decides whether a debt is recoverable. A store that overwrites current state loses it, and it cannot be rebuilt after the first event is written. No earlier version of this document required event sourcing, so a mutable table with an audit log would have passed.
DR-021 Must M0
Each program family's response to a correction is a versioned policy artefact
Added 2026-09-30 (drift B7; Show detail
First needed in: M0 (mechanism), each capture module (mapping)
Description
Added 2026-09-30 (drift B7; TA §B.3.3).
Requirement
When evidence is corrected after determinations have been made from a pre-correction copy, the consuming context applies one of three responses:
Response
When it applies
Consequence
Re-open
The correction is material to entitlement and the program's rules require reassessment
A fresh determination against the corrected snapshot; any difference flows to payment and to Overpayment & Recovery, classified by the operation that produced it (FR-051)
Annotate-only
The correction does not change the outcome, or the period is closed and the program's rules bar reassessment
The determination record carries a correction annotation naming the corrected evidence id and why no reassessment followed; the original trace is untouched
Flag-for-review
Materiality cannot be decided mechanically, typically where a discretionary determination is among the inputs
A work item with a statutory clock, routed to a delegated decision-maker, never auto-closed
Each program family publishes its mapping from evidence type to response. The mapping is a versioned policy artefact under the same release governance as eligibility rules (FR-090), owned by the family's policy authority and ratified by the determination governance body before that family's first capture. The mapping version in force at the time of the correction is recorded on every correction annotation.
Acceptance Criteria
For each program family entering capture, a released mapping covers every evidence type its case context consumes. Given a correction, the annotation names the response applied and the mapping version. A consuming context that holds a derivative has a declared EvidenceCorrectionRecorded subscription, checked by the fitness function in DR-007.
Parameters
N06, N04, N17
Rationale
This is a policy decision, not an engineering one. Left to each team, five case contexts will reach five answers to the same statutory question, and the client will see a correction that the payment and debt engines never acted on (TA §B.3.3).
DR-022 Must
Youth justice information is kept apart from every other record of the young person
Information that identifies a young person's involvement in a youth justice process is held apart from any other record of that person. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (the parts in groups CF15, CF17 and CF18 are conditional on DEP-26 and DEP-28)
Requirement
Information that identifies a young person's involvement in a youth justice process is held apart from any other record of that person. It is open only to those who need it and is destroyed when no longer required. Each youth justice record carries the date after which it may not be disclosed except to the youth and their counsel, worked out from the outcome and the period the federal Act sets. A copy disclosed to another person or body carries the same separation, restriction and duty to destroy. A record of an extrajudicial sanction and a record of extrajudicial measures are separate classes, each with its own access period. Youth justice record information is never included in a disclosure to an Indigenous authority unless the federal youth justice Act authorises it.
Acceptance Criteria
A test shows that no view, search, copy or disclosure of a child protection, mental health or support needs record returns youth justice information; that a record past its non-disclosure date opens only to the youth and their counsel; and that each disclosed copy is listed with its recipient until its destruction is recorded.
Parameters
N12, N21, N06
Rationale
The federal youth justice Act requires the separation, the non-disclosure date and the destruction of copies, and mental health policy repeats the rule (CL-D5-140, CL-D3-037, CL-D3-042, CK-YJ1-16, CK-YJ1-17, CL-D4-041, CL-D4-042, CL-D7-016, CL-D3-054). The classes and their disposal rules cannot be added after the first record (DR-004). Needed by FR-114, FR-383, FR-414, FR-434 and FR-446 to FR-448. The federal Act's records provisions are not yet extracted (DEP-37).
DR-023 Must
Record classes that carry a bar on disclosure are marked when captured
Each of the following is its own record class, marked at the moment of capture so that the bar travels with every copy (DR-006): Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (test data, the custody health record and court-ordered reports are conditional on DEP-26 and DEP-28)
Requirement
Each of the following is its own record class, marked at the moment of capture so that the bar travels with every copy (DR-006):
information obtained in a family conference, mediation or other alternative dispute resolution process, which the CFCSA bars from disclosure except as it lists;
the identity of a person who reports that a child needs protection;
information under solicitor-client privilege;
raw psychological test data, test scores and completed test protocols, open only to qualified test users;
the custody health record, which is not part of the youth's custody file;
medical, psychological and psychiatric reports ordered by a court, externally written Gladue reports, and any report a court has ordered withheld from the youth or a parent;
information a parent gives the parents' registry, which may be used only to give notice;
what screening shows about a care provider, a caregiver, an applicant or another adult in a home (DR-030).
Acceptance Criteria
For each class, a test shows that the mark is present on the record and on a copy made from it, that a person outside the permitted group cannot open it, and that a disclosure package built from the surrounding record leaves it out unless a recorded basis allows it.
Parameters
N21, N12, N13
Rationale
A mark cannot be added later to copies already made (CL-D8-039, CL-D1-114, CK-LG1-12, CL-D1-013, OB-IN1-24, CL-D7-016, R-MH2-42, RC-MH2-18, OB-MH2-74, CL-D3-051, CL-D3-166, RC-YJ5-03, CL-D4-052, CL-D2-195, CL-D1-153). Needed by FR-114, FR-143, FR-178, FR-196, FR-271, FR-310, FR-313, FR-389, FR-416, FR-450 and FR-471.
DR-024 Must
A restriction reaches every instance of a record, and each physical file has a known holder
Any record class can be restricted, contact and identity records included. Show detail
Requirement
Any record class can be restricted, contact and identity records included. A restriction applies to every instance of the record in every medium the system holds or tracks. The system records, for each physical file, who holds it and where it is, as a fact with its own history. A restricted physical file is not sent to offsite storage while the restriction is active. When responsibility for a file transfers, the physical file goes to the receiving office. Under joint management the lead worker's office holds it.
Acceptance Criteria
Given a restricted record with an electronic part and a physical part, when the restriction is applied or removed, then both parts show the change, and a request to send the physical part offsite is refused while the restriction is active.
Parameters
N12, N06, N13
Rationale
Policy requires a restriction to cover all media and instances and bars offsite storage of a restricted record (CL-D8-001, CL-D8-006, CL-D8-009, CL-D1-218, CL-D8-022, CL-D8-025, CL-D5-137, CL-D5-141). Needed by FR-299, FR-300, FR-302, FR-304, FR-381 and FR-384.
DR-025 Must
Adoption records are kept apart, and what the Act preserves for the child outlasts them
Information about the child, about the birth parents and about an adoptive applicant or prospective adoptive parent is held on three separate records. Show detail
Requirement
Information about the child, about the birth parents and about an adoptive applicant or prospective adoptive parent is held on three separate records. No information about prospective adoptive parents is placed on the birth parents' record, and applicants' names are not kept on the child's record. The medical and social history of the child's biological family, and an Indigenous child's cultural identity and community information, are preserved for the child in a class that survives closure of the adoption records and stays linked to the birth identity. The preserved copy keeps identifying information that is removed from the version given to prospective adoptive parents. Original signed consents and statements of alternatives are kept as unmarked originals. A revoked consent is kept and marked as no longer valid, never removed. A homestudy is kept and disposed of as one record with every update. The signed acknowledgement of Indigenous community information is kept for each placement.
Acceptance Criteria
After an adoption order closes the child's record and the adoptive parent's record, the preserved history and cultural identity information can still be found from the birth identity by a person entitled to it, and a search of the birth parents' record returns nothing about the adoptive parents.
Parameters
N12, N21, N13
Rationale
The Adoption Act requires the history and the cultural identity information to be preserved for the child, and policy requires the three records to be separate (RC-LG2-01, RC-LG2-15, CL-D2-237, CL-D2-073, CL-D2-076, CL-D7-097, CL-D7-100, CL-D7-092, CL-D2-257, CL-D2-253, CL-D2-186, CL-D2-208, CL-D2-143, RC-LG2-13, CL-D2-156). No source held states the retention period or the reopening rule for adoption records, and the period a job aid gives for applicant records is not confirmed (CK-AD4-01, CK-AD4-02; DEP-30). Needed by FR-237, FR-244, FR-256, FR-259, FR-263, FR-265, FR-267, FR-268, FR-273 and FR-276.
DR-026 Must
Records removed on an event, and records that are never kept
The disposal design (DR-004) covers classes whose removal is triggered by an event, not by a period, and classes that policy says are never kept: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (recordings, referrals, communications and scan images are conditional on DEP-26 and DEP-28)
Requirement
The disposal design (DR-004) covers classes whose removal is triggered by an event, not by a period, and classes that policy says are never kept:
adoption registry information, removed promptly when a registration is cancelled or no longer valid;
copies of a proposal package, each registered when issued and tracked until returned, and the package and other identifying information about the child removed from the prospective adoptive parent's record after a disruption;
audio and visual recordings of mental health sessions, which are never stored: the transcribed notes, the approval and the signed permissions are the record;
a referral that is not accepted, and documents received from a guardian's social worker that policy calls transitory;
recorded copies of a youth's communications in custody, kept under the short limit policy sets and extended only item by item on recorded grounds;
body scan images, kept only where the scan led to separate confinement or a consequence, for the period policy sets from the end of that event.
For each, the system records that the removal took place, and what was removed, without keeping the content.
Acceptance Criteria
For each class a test triggers the event and shows the content is gone from every copy the system holds, that a removal record remains, and that a replay returns a tombstone.
Parameters
N12, N06
Rationale
The Adoption Regulation requires prompt removal from the registries, and policy sets the other rules (OB-LG2-61, R-LG2-61, R-LG2-64, CK-LG2-14, RC-AD2-15, OB-AD2-20, OB-AD2-27, OB-AD2-28, CL-D2-127, CL-D2-124, CL-D5-023, CL-D5-038, RC-MH2-29, CL-D3-192, CK-YJ2-22, CL-D3-176, CK-YJ2-10, CK-YJ2-11). The rule for a referral that is not accepted rests on practice material only (CL-D5-037), and whether identification viewed to decide residency is kept waits on a ministry answer (CL-D6-016, MQ-085). Needed by FR-242, FR-245, FR-250, FR-353, FR-356, FR-473 and FR-477.
DR-027 Must
Agreements and consents made verbally are recorded with their later written confirmation
An agreement, a confirmation or a consent that the law or policy lets a person give verbally is recorded when it is given, with who gave it, how, and why it was not in writing where policy asks for the reason. Show detail
Requirement
An agreement, a confirmation or a consent that the law or policy lets a person give verbally is recorded when it is given, with who gave it, how, and why it was not in writing where policy asks for the reason. The written copy, each party's signature or written confirmation (an email or text message included, where the Act allows it) and the date each arrived are added to the same record. The record keeps the terms as agreed and the date all parties agreed, which is the date the agreement takes effect. Each amendment and each renewal is kept as issued and linked in sequence to the first signing. Every version of a suicide risk assessment and of a safety plan is added to the record and none is replaced.
Acceptance Criteria
Given a safety plan agreement made verbally, when the written confirmations arrive later, then the record shows one agreement with its original effective date, each confirmation with its own date, and no confirmation overwrites what was first recorded.
Parameters
N01, N08, N09
Rationale
The Act makes an agreement effective when the parties agree, whether or not anyone has signed, and the total duration of a care agreement is counted from the first signing (CL-D1-048, CL-D1-050, CL-D1-042, CL-D1-051, CL-D1-261, CL-D1-267, CL-D7-020, CL-D1-018, CL-D6-041, CL-D5-006, CL-D8-233). Needed by FR-122, FR-163, FR-166, FR-172, FR-175, FR-289, FR-349, FR-350 and FR-401.
DR-028 Must
Records that move with a child, and records that stay, on a transfer
For each kind of transfer the system records what moves, what is copied and what stays, with the custodian before and after: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (the integrated care plan and custody parts are conditional on DEP-27 and DEP-28)
Requirement
For each kind of transfer the system records what moves, what is copied and what stays, with the custodian before and after:
a transfer of responsibility between offices or agencies, where the record and the physical file move and agreements stay with the child;
a written transfer of records from one director to another, which names the records and its effective date;
a referral or a transition to an Indigenous authority, where the ministry's records close and the confirmations, proofs of notification and notices are kept as filed with the court;
an adoption in another province, where the ministry's record states that the adoption records are held there and keeps a copy of every document forwarded;
an integrated care plan, which moves with a child who leaves the region, with consent;
health information that goes with a youth to another custody centre or to an appointment, which travels sealed;
custody medical and master files, which stay with the ministry when a youth moves to adult custody.
The periods a child spent under each listed agreement, order or guardianship are kept, with exact dates and their source, for as long as the person can ask for an agreement as a specified adult, whatever happens to the rest of the child's record.
Acceptance Criteria
For each kind of transfer a test shows the list of records transferred, the custodian of each afterwards, that every copy the ministry keeps records its source (DR-007), and that a disposal run on a closed child's record leaves the periods that decide later eligibility.
Parameters
N13, N06, N12
Rationale
The Act and policy set what moves on each transfer (CL-D1-218, CL-D8-025, CL-D1-267, CL-D1-164, CL-D7-035, CL-D1-187, CL-D1-183, CL-D7-026, CL-D2-232, CL-D2-229, R-IC1-31, CL-D3-211, CL-D3-022, OB-YJ1-07, CL-D3-051, R-LG2-90, R-LG2-91, CK-LG2-20). No source read says whether the ministry keeps its copy as custodian or transfers custody when information goes to an Indigenous authority; FR-084 needs that answer for each kind of record. Needed by FR-124, FR-126, FR-134, FR-135, FR-224, FR-277, FR-301, FR-302, FR-306, FR-314, FR-397, FR-442, FR-450 and FR-479.
DR-029 Must
A parent's contribution to a child's maintenance is held as a receivable
Where a maintenance agreement or a maintenance order requires a parent to pay, the amount owed is held as a receivable with the document that proves the debt. Show detail
Requirement
Where a maintenance agreement or a maintenance order requires a parent to pay, the amount owed is held as a receivable with the document that proves the debt. One signed agreement is linked to the child's or youth's record and to the parents' record, and its retention follows the longer of the two. Its dates stay in step with the care agreement it accompanies. An in-kind contribution is recorded apart from the financial amount. Arrears owing under a maintenance order that the Act cancels on a withdrawal are kept. Financial support to a guardian after a permanent transfer of custody is held on a record of its own, which stays open after the child's service record closes.
Acceptance Criteria
Given a care agreement with a maintenance agreement, when the care agreement ends, then billing stops, the receivable keeps its history and its proving document, and the signed agreement can be found from both the child's record and the parents' record.
Parameters
N12, N17, N08
Rationale
The Act keeps a parent responsible to contribute, and financial policy requires a copy of the agreement so the receivable can be set up (RC-CP2-25, OB-FI1-74, CL-D1-270, CL-D1-246, CL-D1-164, CL-D1-156, CL-D2-185). Needed by FR-135, FR-171, FR-199, FR-209 and FR-329 to FR-333. This entry states what must be kept. Where the receivable sits among the financial records is for the ledger decision (ADR-010).
DR-030 Must
Records about people who are not clients have their own handling
Information the ministry holds about a person who is not a client is held under its own access, use and retention rules, apart from any child's or youth's record it relates to. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (visitor, staff search and victim records are conditional on DEP-28)
Requirement
Information the ministry holds about a person who is not a client is held under its own access, use and retention rules, apart from any child's or youth's record it relates to. This covers:
adults in a care provider's home, and what record searches, voluntary disclosures and police say about them;
care providers, caregivers and adoptive applicants: screening results, prior contact check consents and results, and the foster caregiver review report, which is filed on the caregiver's record and not released to the caregiver;
visitors to a youth custody centre, in the visitor's registry;
staff members and visitors who are searched, refuse a search or are detained;
victims, whose identity and contact details are kept from the youth and from disclosure of the youth's own record;
complainants and the staff a complaint is about.
What screening shows about a person is not shared with others, the parent and the Indigenous community included, without that person's consent. A prior contact check reads records collected for another purpose, so it starts only on the person's signed consent and its result carries a limit on use.
Acceptance Criteria
For each class a test shows that the record cannot be opened from a child's or youth's record by a person without access to the class, that a search or detention report about a staff member cannot be read by that person's peers, and that release outside the ministry or agency is refused without a recorded consent or legal basis.
Parameters
N21, N12, N13
Rationale
Policy limits the sharing of screening results and requires consent for a prior contact check (CL-D1-064, CL-D1-153, CL-D1-150, CL-D2-006, CL-D2-009, OB-GU1-11, RC-GU1-02, OB-GU1-07, CL-D3-185, CL-D3-169, CL-D3-170, CL-D3-171, CL-D3-172, CL-D4-074, CL-D4-075, OB-QA1-04, CL-D8-155, RC-YJ2-39). No source held states a retention period for any of these classes. Needed by FR-168, FR-196, FR-226, FR-227, FR-230, FR-405, FR-424, FR-462, FR-472, FR-474 and FR-475.
DR-031 Must
Retention classes for children's services records are set before the first record, from schedules not yet held
Each children's services record class is given a retention class and a disposal method before the first record is written (DR-004). Show detail
Requirement
Each children's services record class is given a retention class and a disposal method before the first record is written (DR-004). The classes include the child's service record, agreements and their amendments, court reports and orders kept as presented and as issued, notices of significant measures with proof of delivery, delegation records, reportable circumstance reports, administrative review and complaint records, the mental health client record with its physical part, and youth justice records. A delegation record is kept at least as long as any decision record that cites it. An agreement is kept at least as long as any decision made under it can be reviewed. Where policy keeps a record in both electronic and paper form, the design says which copy is the record.
Acceptance Criteria
Every children's services record class in the registry has a retention class, a start event and a disposal method, each citing the schedule entry it rests on, and none rests on a job aid alone.
Parameters
N12, N18
Rationale
The sources held state few retention periods and several defer to records schedules that are not in the corpus (CL-D1-010, CL-D7-112, CL-D7-129, CL-D8-190, CL-D8-192, RC-IN1-22, CL-D8-171, CL-D8-183, CL-D5-118, CL-D5-100, CL-D5-141, RC-LG3-18, CK-RP1-19; DEP-30). The guideline tells a person formerly in care they may apply for their information for a very long period, which implies a long retention class for the child's record. Needed by FR-104, FR-117, FR-136, FR-190, FR-192, FR-218, FR-338, FR-343, FR-380, FR-381 and FR-406.
Moving data from the legacy systems 7
Migration Scope: History that affects entitlement, current case state, case notes and practice history, and financial history held in ICM, MIS and the stores around them. The old audit trail is included because it is the evidence for when the old system recorded each fact.
Migration Strategy: Phased, by part of the system and by group of clients, with a shadow period before each group moves. Groups move in this order: new applicants; clients in one program with no active protection involvement; clients in several programs; and last, clients with active protection concerns or court involvement. No client is moved in the middle of a determination or an appeal.
Data Transformation: A mixed approach chosen per fact class (DR-010). Migration events use the old system's terms. Business events that claim to record what someone intended are never invented.
Data Validation: Record counts, financial control totals, checks that links between records hold, sample checks by program staff, a pilot on converted data, and the date-accuracy gate (DR-012).
Rollback Plan: Per group of clients, rehearsed, with the published list of what would be lost accepted in writing by the program policy authority (DR-015).
Migration Timeline: Per capture module (M2 onwards). Profiling the old data and the trial of decoding old-system dates both happen before design freeze.
DR-010 Must
A mixed migration approach, chosen per fact class
Facts that affect entitlement (income, assets, household, dependants, shelter, designation, enrolment periods, earlier determinations, overpayment balances) are loaded with all three time axes (DR-001): Show detail
Requirement
Facts that affect entitlement (income, assets, household, dependants, shelter, designation, enrolment periods, earlier determinations, overpayment balances) are loaded with all three time axes (DR-001): valid time, transaction time (the import time, ADR-002) and legacy assertion time with its confidence, marked as coming from the old systems (provenance LEGACY). The case shell and current operational state migrate as current state only. Case notes and practice history are archived and made available through an adapter that marks them as coming from the old systems. Everything else is loaded through named migration events such as LegacyClientWasImported.
Acceptance Criteria
Every fact class appears in the migration register with its approach. No invented business events exist.
Parameters
N01, N06
Rationale
Each fact class has its own right answer, and using one approach for everything is an error (decision D10).
DR-011 Must
Migration records its source, can be re-run, and can be reversed per group
Every migrated fact records its source system, source record identifier, migration batch identifier, migration time and a confidence rating. Show detail
Requirement
Every migrated fact records its source system, source record identifier, migration batch identifier, migration time and a confidence rating. Migration can be re-run without creating duplicates, keyed on the source record identifier, and can be reversed for each group of clients TA-C43.
Acceptance Criteria
Running a migration batch twice creates no duplicates. In test, a group of clients can be un-migrated and migrated again.
Parameters
N01, N14
Rationale
Migration is a product with its own quality gates, not a one-off task.
DR-012 Must
Migration quality gates, including date accuracy
Migration gates check record counts, control totals, links between records, samples checked by people, and a pilot on converted data. Show detail
Requirement
Migration gates check record counts, control totals, links between records, samples checked by people, and a pilot on converted data. They also set two date-accuracy minimums for each fact class: the percentage of facts with a known valid period, and the percentage with a recoverable old-system date. Both minimums are agreed before migration begins.
Acceptance Criteria
No group of clients passes a gate whose minimums were set after the data was measured.
Parameters
N01, N18
Rationale
The standard gates cannot detect that the "when did we learn it" dates have all collapsed to the import date. The comparator ran no pilot on converted data and produced about 114,000 errors in converted legacy records (TA §C.2.8).
DR-013 Must
Unknown old-system dates are visible, and default in the client's favour
For a migrated fact, recorded_at is always the import time, and is never set to legacy_asserted_at; Show detail
Requirement
For a migrated fact, recorded_at is always the import time, and is never set to legacy_asserted_at; a decoded or inferred old-system date is carried only in legacy_asserted_at with its confidence (ADR-002). When a fact's old-system date is UNKNOWN, the two kinds of question behave differently:
Valid-time questions (a recalculation, or a replay reproducing an amount) proceed, order the fact by its recorded_at (the import time), and mark the determination TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED. This marker is carried onto the decision record, notices and appeal packages.
Knowledge-state questions (overpayment classification, tribunal reconstruction, disclosure history) return INDETERMINATE. They never substitute the import time or the migration timestamp, and they direct the reader to the retained legacy audit trail.
An overpayment component whose classification is INDETERMINATE defaults to administrative error and is not recovered, unless a person reclassifies it on recorded evidence. Amended 2026-09-30 (ADR-002; drift B14): v1.3 read "it treats the fact as recorded at migration and marks the determination TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED" for every replay, without separating the two kinds of question. Before design freeze, the old audit trail is profiled across the most important fact classes, with at least 10,000 records for each.
Acceptance Criteria
Profiling results are published for each class. A TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED determination cannot, on its own, show what the ministry knew at a past date. A knowledge-state query over an UNKNOWN fact returns INDETERMINATE and never a date.
Parameters
N01, N08
Rationale
If the ministry cannot show when it knew something, it cannot meet the burden of proof a tribunal places on it TA-C19. The client-favourable default is the architecture's administrative-error default (TA §C.7.5), stated from the client's side (ADR-002 §3; TA §B.3.1).
DR-014 Must
Running old and new systems side by side, and writing back to the old system
Responsibility for a record moves from the old system to the new one per part of the system and per group of clients, never one field at a time. Show detail
Requirement
Responsibility for a record moves from the old system to the new one per part of the system and per group of clients, never one field at a time. When the new system writes changes back to the old one for groups it has taken over, the write-back:
uses only insert and update operations. It never uses a synchronize operation on an object with child records, unless a check before writing confirms the data is complete;
is kept out of the new system's outgoing event queue, so it cannot loop back;
is removed from both sides of every reconciliation and shadow comparison;
keeps the old system's validation, or records a decision for each case where validation is bypassed;
runs one way only for records the new system has taken over;
follows a published mapping, per fact class, that lists every field with nowhere to go in the old system.
Acceptance Criteria
A deliberately incomplete write is refused. A loop test shows no echoed events. The list of what would be lost is published before the new system takes over writing for a group (state S2).
Parameters
N05, N14
Rationale
Writing back to the old system is the most dangerous write path in the old and new systems combined (TA §C.2.6).
DR-015 Must
Rollback rehearsed, with its losses published
Every group of clients moved to the new system can be moved back to the old one without a separate data project. Show detail
Requirement
Every group of clients moved to the new system can be moved back to the old one without a separate data project. The published list of losses names every fact class that would not survive the move back, and the difference between a correction and a supersession is always on it. Rollback is rehearsed before any group moves.
Acceptance Criteria
The rollback rehearsal record and the accepted list of losses are present at the capture gate.
Parameters
N14
Rationale
A rollback plan that does not say what is lost has not been tested (PRIN N14).
DR-016 Must
Retiring the old systems and disposing of their data
Each old system is retired as its replacement goes live. Show detail
Requirement
Each old system is retired as its replacement goes live. Each record class receives one of five outcomes: moved, archived for a period, transferred to the archives, permanently and ethically deleted, or transferred to another government (an Indigenous governing body or other sovereign). The oldest core systems and the old audit trail are kept in a complete archive with controlled access. People who use a core old system, staff and oversight bodies get at least twelve months' notice before it is shut down. Disposal decisions are in place before the new system takes over writing for each part (state S2).
Acceptance Criteria
Old interfaces are closed, with evidence, and counted against the full list of interfaces from Module 0.
Parameters
N12, N13, N14
Rationale
Systems cannot be retired by deleting them, and retention duties run for decades beyond the programme (TA §C.2.9).

DR-017 Must
Analysis without making copies
People and systems analysing data get what they are entitled to, at the level of detail they are entitled to, from one governed store, without a new copy being made. Show detail
Requirement
People and systems analysing data get what they are entitled to, at the level of detail they are entitled to, from one governed store, without a new copy being made. Only de-identified, aggregated, synthetic or differentially private versions leave the trusted environment.

The list of data consumers shows no new extracts. Every dataset in public cloud is a registered de-identified or aggregated version.

A data warehouse that already exists, built on shared reporting dimensions, means this is a migration from what exists (APP §9).

Reports need to stay comparable across the cutover (GAPS P-02). Carrying the old categories forward as the design would tie the new model to the old system's vocabulary (N10).
DR-019 Must
Identity data is read when needed, not stored
The system reads identity details from provincial identity services when it needs them and does not keep them longer than they stay valid. Show detail
Requirement
The system reads identity details from provincial identity services when it needs them and does not keep them longer than they stay valid. The client index holds only identifiers and the personal details needed to match people, and does not become a second directory.

The main information objects
Each object belongs to one part of the system. They are not a shared model that every part must use; each part keeps its own view of what it needs.

Data Volume: The number of determinations a year for each program family has not been measured. The architecture calls it the single most important missing number (NFR-P-003).
Access Patterns: By person and period; replay by identifier; assembly into appeal records.
Data Classification: Protected B or C, taken from the classification of the facts it read.
Data Retention: For the full period during which the decision can be appealed, reviewed or requested under access law, and at least as long as the replay horizon (FR-008). The fields on the shred-survivor list remain after the rest is destroyed (DR-004).

9 Work item

Data quality
Data Accuracy: Shadow comparison proves correctness separately for each type of difference (FR-095). A single overall match rate does not count. Two wrong amounts that cancel each other out to a zero total count as a defect.
Data Completeness: Mandatory questions are answered or recorded as asserted negatives (DR-009). Determination records carry every required field (FR-001). Migrated facts that affect entitlement meet minimum rates, agreed in advance, for having a known valid period and a recoverable old-system date (DR-012).
Data Consistency: There is one writer per aggregate per cohort (N05). (Restored 2026-09-30, drift Δ1.2: v1.1–v1.3 read "Only one system can change each record for each group of clients".) Reference data has one master copy, published as events (FR-094). Money is reconciled three ways every day (FR-045). Read-only views are compared with the old system every day, with rows written back by the new system removed from both sides first (DR-014).
Data Timeliness: The system refuses a determination when its facts are older than the consistency limit allows (FR-009). Delays in processing published events have limits and raise alarms (NFR-P-005).
Data Lineage: Every fact records where it came from, including the extraction tool version and confidence where a machine read it. Every copy records its source (DR-007). Every migrated fact records its source system, source record, migration batch, migration time and confidence (DR-011).
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document, from 326 service-delivery procedures, and from 308 documents and 14 statutes and regulations on children and family services. Nothing here is a government commitment.

Functional requirements
What the system must do. Groups A to P follow a client's matter through the ministry. Groups CF1 to CF18 follow a child's or a family's, and were written from the law and policy of the Ministry of Children and Family Development. Each requirement lists the provisions it meets and the checks that prove it.
Functional requirements are grouped by capability, in the order a client's matter moves through the ministry. Each one lists the policy obligations it meets (Obligations) and the architecture parameters that test it (Parameters). Where a requirement has no obligation, its authority is the architecture section named in its rationale. Appendix E and the companion file ARC-001-REQ-v1.4-traceability.csv map all 270 obligations to requirements, and carry a row for each requirement that traces to the architecture rather than to an obligation.
Module names the delivery module in which the requirement must first be met (target architecture §A.8). Requirements assigned to M0 are foundations. Several of them cannot be added later, once the first event, copy, rule or cohort exists (PRIN §V) PRIN-C5.
Added v1.6. Groups CF1 to CF18 hold the children and family services requirements. They follow a child's or family's matter through the ministry, then the records, money and oversight that cut across it, then the three conditional areas. Each lists its Authority in words, with the tier of the source, and its Provisions: the reconciled provisions (CL-) and further register rows it meets. A time limit, an age or an amount is cited by its row and never stated. Where two requirements written by different authors rest on the same provisions, each names the other under See also. All are first needed in module M9, which the architecture gives its own discovery and its own gate, endorsed by the child protection practice authority (TA §E.5.9).

A Decisions and the decision record 10
FR-001 Must M0 High
Decision types and what the decision record holds
The system records every decision as one of three types: Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M5 (first rule surface)
Description
The system records every decision as one of three types: grant; deny; or reduce or discontinue. Each is a determination in its own right. Its record states the criteria met and not met, the statutory provisions applied, the assumptions made, the evidence lacking, any decision-support report used, and every item of information considered.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-1, UC-2
Obligations
OB-D01, OB-D03, OB-D04, OB-D05, OB-D06, OB-D07, OB-D09, OB-D11
Parameters
N01, N07, N08, N20
Acceptance Criteria
Given any issued determination, when its record is read, then it holds its type, criteria met, criteria not met, provisions applied, assumptions made and evidence lacking as separate fields, none of which can only be recovered by re-running the rules.
Given a determination informed by a decision-support report, when the record is read, then a full copy of the report is stored with it.
Given a request to disclose the information considered, when the record is queried, then every item considered can be listed from the record alone.
Data
Inputs: evidence snapshot, rules artefact, decision-maker input; Outputs: determination record; Validations: the assumptions and evidence-lacking fields cannot be empty (an explicit "none" counts as an answer).
Dependencies
FR-008, FR-011
Rationale
Policy sets out what the record must contain. That includes negative facts, the assumptions made and the evidence lacking, which cannot be rebuilt after the decision (PRIN N08 amendment (a)).
FR-002 Must M5 Medium
Reasons that name the rule applied and the fact behind it
Every decision carries real reasons, generated from the decision trace: Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
Every decision carries real reasons, generated from the decision trace: the specific rule, the specific fact, its source and the period it covers. Each rule has its own reasons text, written with the rule and released with it.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-003, UC-1
Obligations
OB-D02
Parameters
N07, N08, N18
Acceptance Criteria
Given an adverse determination chosen at random, when its notice is inspected, then each adverse element names the rule identifier, the fact relied on, where that fact came from, and its period.
Given a rules artefact release, when any rule that produces an adverse outcome lacks approved reasons text, then the release fails.
Edge case: a category code or a generic "you do not meet the criteria" paragraph is not accepted as reasons.
Data
Inputs: decision trace; reasons text keyed by rule identifier; Outputs: reasons text bound into the notice; Validations: every adverse rule that fired has reasons text.
Dependencies
FR-062, FR-090
Rationale
A person cannot challenge reasons they cannot trace to a rule and a fact. Untraceable reasons were a defining feature of the automated-debt failure the architecture designs against (TA §C.8.7).
FR-003 Must M0 Medium
Decision classes and the human decision-maker
Every output of a rules artefact carries a decision class. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M5
Description
Every output of a rules artefact carries a decision class. The policy author declares it, the program policy authority approves it on legal advice, and the system enforces it when running. There are three classes:
an administrative decision, which needs reasons and a route to challenge it;
a decision that needs a human decision-maker before it issues, held until that person records it;
a computational intermediate, which is never presented as a decision.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-005, UC-1, UC-7
Parameters
N07, N08, N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a rules artefact with an unclassified output, when release is attempted, then release is refused.
Given a determination whose adverse outcome rests on any inferred, estimated, averaged or apportioned input, when it is computed, then it is held for a human decision-maker, whatever class the artefact declares TA-C14.
Given a held determination, when no human decision is recorded, then nothing issues and no timeout issues it automatically.
Given a computational intermediate, when any client-facing screen or notice would present it as a decision, then the output is blocked and a governance defect is raised.
Data
Inputs: class on the artefact; where each input came from; Outputs: class recorded on the determination; DiscretionaryDetermination evidence for human decisions; Validations: a human decision records identity, authority and rationale.
Dependencies
FR-093
Rationale
The duty to give reasons attaches to the decision, not to the software, and operating procedures break down at volume (TA §B.4.4, §D.5). Open item: the architecture names the classes three ways, with different ordering: (i)/(ii)/(iii) at §B.4.4, Class 1/2/3 at §C.8.5 and Class A/B/C at §D.5. This document uses the §D.5 A/B/C names. The Chief Architect is asked to adopt one set throughout.
FR-004 Must M4 Medium
Who may decide, value bands, and reasoning that cannot be handed off
The system routes each decision to the person or body with authority for it, by entitlement and, where policy sets one, by value band. Show detail
First needed in: M4 (routing), M5
Description
The system routes each decision to the person or body with authority for it, by entitlement and, where policy sets one, by value band. It records the person who reasoned the decision as the decision-maker of record. It keeps anything the system or another person proposed separate from what the decision-maker concluded.
Relates To
BR-002, BR-003, UC-1, UC-3
Obligations
OB-D10, OB-EL-23, OB-EL-74, OB-SU-02, OB-SU-32, OB-SU-62, OB-SU-63
Parameters
N17
Acceptance Criteria
Given a decision whose value or type needs a higher authority, when a worker without that authority tries to finalise it, then the system routes it to the required authority and refuses to finalise it.
Given any decision where a recommendation or pre-filled outcome was shown, when the record is read, then the proposal and the decision-maker's conclusion are recorded separately PRIN-C6.
Given a request to close or re-open a type of case that needs a named approver, when no approval is recorded, then the action is refused.
Data
Inputs: the schedule of delegated authority (reference data with effective dates); Outputs: decision-maker identity and authority on the record; Validations: the authority was in force on the decision date.
Dependencies
FR-094
Rationale
Policy says a decision-maker "must not delegate the actual decision or allow advice to take the place of their own reasoning". It also sets decision-makers by dollar band, up to Executive Director and ADM (PRIN N17).
Added v1.6 (CL-D1-059). Given a decision that policy lets take effect before a required approval, with the approval due within a time limit, when the decision is recorded, then the system records it as made, routes it for approval, and shows the approval as outstanding until it is given or refused.
FR-005 Must M5 High
Effective dates worked out by rule, for each part of the benefit
A versioned rule works out the effective date of every determination, including one that replaces an earlier determination, a reconsideration outcome, and a re-determination after the tribunal rescinds a decision. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
A versioned rule works out the effective date of every determination, including one that replaces an earlier determination, a reconsideration outcome, and a re-determination after the tribunal rescinds a decision. The date is worked out separately for each benefit component and recorded as derived. The ministry's own timeliness is one of the inputs.
Relates To
BR-001, BR-003, UC-2, UC-4
Obligations
OB-R11, OB-A08, OB-SU-79
Parameters
N01, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a determination granting several components, when it is recorded, then each component carries its own effective date and the version of the rule that worked it out.
Given a decision issued after its legal time limit expired, when the effective date is worked out, then the earlier date the clock rule sets is applied automatically, without anyone asking.
Given two components policy does not allow in the same month, when both would otherwise be granted, then the determination grants only what the rule allows and records why.
Data
Inputs: benefit type, component, clock state; Outputs: effective dates per component, marked as derived; Validations: no effective date entered by hand without a recorded override authority.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-090
Rationale
A determination that replaces an earlier one does not take effect on the day it is made. Policy sets the date by benefit type. Where the ministry decided late, policy sets it as the date the decision was due (PRIN N01 amendment v3.1).
FR-006 Must M5 Medium
A pre-decision letter, kept separate from a decision
The system supports a pre-decision communication as its own kind of record, separate from a determination and available to any part of the system that makes decisions. Show detail
First needed in: M5
Description
The system supports a pre-decision communication as its own kind of record, separate from a determination and available to any part of the system that makes decisions. It carries reasons, a response deadline, what happens if the client responds or does not, and a plain statement that no decision has been made yet.
Amended 2026-09-30 (ADR-004): PreDecisionCommunication is an aggregate of the Eligibility & Entitlement (Determination) context. It sits in that context's imperative shell, never inside the pure Determine function. The amount and reasons it carries are produced by Determine as a class (iii) computational output and bound into a record like any other evaluation. It carries an explicit no_decision_made marker. Its response window is a clock artefact (FR-061), evaluated in the shell. The client's response is recorded as evidence in Evidence & Verification. The letter is rendered by Notices & Correspondence from a bound template.
Relates To
BR-003, BR-005, UC-1, UC-5
Obligations
OB-EL-27
Parameters
N01, N08, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a pre-decision communication, when its notice is generated, then it states the issues, the response due date and how to respond, and no reconsideration or appeal rights are drawn from it.
Given a client's response within the window, when it arrives, then it is recorded as evidence for the determination that follows.
Given a client asks for reconsideration of a pre-decision communication, when the request is made, then it is recorded (FR-055). The communication's status never causes the request to be refused.
Given any rights-derivation path (notices, adjudicability, appeal periods), when it reads a record carrying no_decision_made, then it cannot treat that record as a determination (ADR-004).
Given the amount shown in a pre-decision communication, when its record is read, then it is a class (iii) output of Determine, bound to its rules artefact digest and input snapshot, and not a value typed or computed outside the function.
Data
Inputs: draft calculation or list of issues, response clock definition; Outputs: PreDecisionCommunication record (owned by Eligibility & Entitlement); Validations: it cannot carry an adjudicability attribute, and no_decision_made is always set.
Dependencies
FR-055, FR-061
Rationale
If this were only a status flag on a determination, one rule change could make the system read it as a decision and attach appeal rights to it. The ministry's own intake practice already runs this pattern correctly (NOTE-001 v2.0). The owning context and the shell placement are set by ADR-004, because Determine is pure and has no clock (N07).

FR-008 Must M0 High
Replay from stored records, and a declared replay horizon
Any determination can be replayed from what was stored with it (the rules artefact, the engine version and its archived copy, a full copy of the input snapshot, the decision trace and the notice template) without depending on any running system. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (declaration), M5
Description
Any determination can be replayed from what was stored with it (the rules artefact, the engine version and its archived copy, a full copy of the input snapshot, the decision trace and the notice template) without depending on any running system. Before the first live determination, the ministry declares in writing how long replay is guaranteed and what serves as evidence after that.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-4
Parameters
N07, N08
Acceptance Criteria
Given a determination issued in a previous year, when it is replayed in an isolated environment from storage alone, then it produces a decision trace identical to the original, byte for byte.
Given the archived engine copies inside the declared window, when the scheduled test runs, then every archived copy runs or an alarm is raised.
Given a determination whose inputs were disposed of, when it is replayed, then the result is marked with the declared limit and points the reader to the trace, the notice as issued, and the shred-survivor set.
Given a determination older than its rule family's policy-availability date in the horizon statement, when authority is asked for, then the result says authority is not producible, and the evidentiary record is the decision trace, the notice as issued and the input snapshot, with the shred-survivor set where disposition has occurred (ADR-007). Amended 2026-09-30: v1.3 combined this case with disposal and omitted the input snapshot.
Given the replay-horizon statement, when it is published before the first production determination, then it is one statement with the layered horizon and, per rule family, the earliest effective date for which the governing policy text or rate can be produced from a retained source (ADR-007).
Data
Inputs: the five stored artefacts; Outputs: replay result with limit markers; Validations: each artefact's digest checks out against the hash chain.
Dependencies
FR-010, NFR-SEC-009
Rationale
A pointer to a running system is not evidence (PRIN N08). The architecture chooses a layered horizon. It keeps a runnable archive for seven years, a written specification with a regression corpus up to twenty years, and the trace after that TA-C15. Superseded policy text that was never published shortens that horizon unless it is captured when the rules are loaded NOTE2-C1. The policy citation and effective-date marker are carried inside the rules artefact (artefact 1) and bound by its digest, so there is no sixth artefact; the horizon statement gains a per-rule-family policy-availability dimension, not a second horizon (ADR-007).
FR-009 Must M0 High
Recording the point in time a decision's facts were read
Every determination records the watermark: Show detail
First needed in: M0
Description
Every determination records the watermark: the point in the system's history up to which its evidence snapshot was read. The watermark is the minimum, across the contributing partitions, of each partition's highest contiguously applied position, expressed as a transaction time. It is not "the last event seen". The system refuses to issue a determination when the gap between now and the watermark is larger than the limit set for its class.
Relates To
BR-002, UC-1, UC-6
Parameters
N09
Acceptance Criteria
Given any determination, when its record is read, then the watermark is present.
Given an interactive determination whose gap is over its limit, when issuance is attempted, then it is refused, the worker sees the reason, and a work item is raised TA-C16.
Given a batch issuance run, when any contributing data stream is over the batch limit at the start of the run, then the run stops and no partial run issues.
Data
Inputs: how far each data stream has been applied; limit per determination class; Outputs: watermark on the record; Validations: limits set from measured lag before the first live determination.
Dependencies
NFR-P-004
Rationale
Two determinations made moments apart can each legitimately see a different set of facts, and without the watermark nothing detects it. This is a required addition to the architecture's parameter set, and in practice it cannot be added later (PRIN N09).

FR-012 Must M0 High

FR-041 Must M6 Medium
Money paid out now that may have to be repaid
Some money is paid out against a signed promise to repay: Show detail
First needed in: M6, M7
Description
Some money is paid out against a signed promise to repay: reconsideration and appeal supplements, security and pet deposits, co-op share purchases, warrant-related supplements, and hardship promises to pay. The system records each as a repayable issuance. It holds the signed promise, the decision it is waiting on and the outcome. It becomes a debt only on the outcome policy sets.
Amended 2026-09-30 (ADR-005): RepayableIssuance is an aggregate of Financial Components, its sole writer. It carries the undertaking (modelled with its signature requirement, not held as a scanned attachment), the determination it awaits, the covered period as a compound clock, and the resolution. Financial Components decides nothing: resolution is triggered by the awaited determination's DeterminationIssued event, and the amounts come from the determination records. Interim assistance pending reconsideration or appeal is its principal instance; the "true-up obligation" is this aggregate, and its payment still passes the issuance chokepoint with its own purpose code. A repayable issuance is a debt undertaken at issuance, not a retroactive recalculation, so it enters Overpayment & Recovery only when it resolves on denial, as a component whose classification is set by policy.
Relates To
BR-004, BR-005, UC-4, UC-5
Obligations
OB-R18, OB-A11, OB-EL-38, OB-SU-04, OB-SU-06, OB-SU-07, OB-SU-08, OB-SU-67
Parameters
N01, N05, N19
Acceptance Criteria
Given a repayable issuance, when the promise to repay is not signed, then no payment instruction issues.
Given the decision it is waiting on, when that decision issues, then the repayable issuance settles automatically as closed, partly repayable or fully repayable, with no manual reconciliation.
Given deposit rules that depend on earlier deposits still owing, when a new deposit is requested, then the rule is applied using the recorded repayable issuances.
Given interim assistance instructed pending a reconsideration or appeal, when it is issued, then it is recorded as a repayable issuance awaiting that reconsideration or appeal determination (ADR-005).
Given a repayable issuance resolved on denial, when it enters Overpayment & Recovery, then its component carries the classification policy sets for that instance, not a classification derived from a Supersede or Correct operation.
Data
Inputs: signed promise, reference to the awaited decision; Outputs: settlement events; Validations: settled only by the linked decision; no amount originates in Financial Components.
Dependencies
FR-042, FR-053
Rationale
Money paid now, whose repayment depends on a later decision, fits neither the payment model nor the overpayment model NOTE5-C1. Whether an appeal supplement must be repaid when the appeal is dismissed has been referred to the ministry, and the model must support either answer. The owning context and the resolution rule are set by ADR-005, which also corrects the rationale NOTE-005 gave: an overpayment is not "always an error" (a supersession yields a recoverable overpayment with no error by anyone); what is always true is that an overpayment arises from a retroactive recalculation between determination records and carries a classification.
E Payments and financial control 10
FR-042 Must M0 High
Every payment goes through one issuance service
Every payment of public money starts as a payment instruction created from a determination. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (specification and criteria 1–3), M6
Description
Every payment of public money starts as a payment instruction created from a determination. Once accepted, an instruction cannot be changed. It carries an identifier the system can recalculate, the determinations it pays, the payee and the capacity they are paid in, the gross amount with each deduction listed, the value date, the benefit period, the channel, a purpose code, a funding code, and the requester and approver. Every instruction passes through one Issuance Service. No other component holds a credential for a payment rail, a cheque print stream or the corporate financial system's posting interface.
Amended 2026-09-30 (ADR-001): Financial Components is the sole writer of the PaymentInstruction aggregate: it creates, cancels and supersedes instructions, and a reissue is a new instruction it writes. Payments & Benefit Issuance is the sole writer of the Disbursement aggregate: it accepts an instruction at the chokepoint, includes it in a run, disburses, stops, handles returns and requests reissue. The two aggregates reference each other by identifier.
Relates To

Parameters

Acceptance Criteria

Given an instruction identifier that already exists, when it is submitted again, then no second payment is created, whether or not the details match; if the details differ, the submission is rejected with a reason.
Given an instruction with no determination reference, when it is submitted, then it is flagged as an exception and needs the exception approval.
Given an accepted instruction, when a change is needed, then it is cancelled and replaced, or stopped and reissued. It is never edited.

FR-043 Must M6 High
Issuance runs
Payments are issued in runs. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
Payments are issued in runs. A run is scheduled, can be resumed, can be audited, and follows a published calendar. Its stages are: cycle open, cutoff, assembly and pre-flight checks, control totals set before approval, approval, release, settlement and returns, reconciliation, and close. A run can be released more than once without paying twice. Supplementary and off-cycle payments are a run of one, with the same controls.
Relates To
BR-004, UC-6
Parameters
N17, N09
Acceptance Criteria
Given a release interrupted part-way, when it resumes, then it finishes instruction by instruction without paying anything twice, and the control totals match those set before approval TA-C17.
Given pre-flight exceptions above the published threshold, when assembly finishes, then the run does not proceed.
Given a closed run, when an adjustment is needed, then it is made with new instructions, and the run cannot be reopened.
Added v1.5 (TA §C.6.2): Given a run at assembly, when the control totals are set, then they give the count, gross, deductions and net, each broken down by channel and by program, and the same figures are carried unchanged to reconciliation.
Added v1.5 (TA §C.6.2): Given an instruction that arrives after the published cutoff, when the run is assembled, then the instruction is not in it; it goes to the next cycle or to a supplementary run.
Added v1.5 (TA §C.6.2): Given a cycle, when it opens, then the instructions in it are selected by a stored, versioned query and nobody can add or remove one by hand.
Added v1.5 (TA §C.6.2): Given each stage of a run (open, cutoff, assembly, totals, approval, release, settlement, reconciliation, close), when the run record is read, then the stage shows as a distinct state with its named owner.
Added v1.5 (TA §C.6.2): Given the whole platform, when it is tested, then no operation can release money except the release of an approved run TA-C17.
Data
Inputs: the set of instructions selected by query, and the cycle definition version. Outputs: a run record with frozen totals. Validations: thresholds are policy settings, not values written into code.
Dependencies
FR-042, FR-045, FR-009
Rationale
The dangerous failure is a run that stops halfway. An operator under pressure then runs it again and pays a live caseload twice (TA §C.6.2).
Added v1.6 (CL-D8-077). Given a payment or a run whose value is over the threshold policy sets for notice to Provincial Treasury's cash management branch (R-FI1-08), when it is assembled, then the system raises the notice with the lead time policy sets (CK-FI1-06) and records that it was given before release.

FR-047 Must M0 High

FR-100 Must M0 High
The Issuance Service's published contract and reconciliation feed

Description
The Issuance Service publishes one contract through the Open Host Service, and every context uses it. The contract has four operations: submit a run, approve a run, release a run, and read the state of an instruction. Submit and approve each answer with an acceptance or with a rejection that lists its reasons. The service publishes twelve events: run accepted, run approved, instruction released, instruction settled, instruction returned, instruction rejected, stop requested, stop confirmed, stop failed, recall requested, recall outcome recorded, and reissue linked. The service is also the only producer of the reconciliation feed. The contract and the feed are versioned and governed like every other published contract.

Given a run, when it is assembled, then the feed holds one control-total record for it, and that record never changes.

F Overpayment, compliance and investigation 6
FR-051 Must M6 High
Overpayments calculated and classified from the evidence that changed
An overpayment is the difference between two determination records for the same period. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
An overpayment is the difference between two determination records for the same period. The system splits it into one component for each change in evidence. It classifies each component by the operation and fault recorded on that change:
a supersession, or a correction where the client was at fault, is recoverable;
a correction where the ministry was at fault is administrative error;
where a third party was at fault, a person decides, and the default is administrative error;
where fault cannot be determined, it is administrative error unless a person reclassifies it.
Relates To
BR-005, UC-5
Parameters
N01, N06, N08
Acceptance Criteria
Given a recalculation with components in more than one class, when the overpayment is raised, then each component has its own classification and recovery terms, and the notice states each one separately.
Given a migrated fact where nobody knows when the ministry learned it, when a component depends on it, then the knowledge-state answer is INDETERMINATE and the component defaults to administrative error, not recovered unless a person reclassifies it on recorded evidence TA-C19 (ADR-002; DR-013).
Given the classification mapping above, when it runs, then it is executed as a versioned, released rules artefact that reads the operation (Supersede or Correct) and the error attribution from the evidence record, under the same release governance as eligibility rules (FR-090). It is not hard-coded in the service, and the artefact version is recorded on each component (drift B15; TA §B.2.1 Overpayment & Recovery).
Given any overpayment component, when its origin is inspected, then it arises from a retroactive recalculation between two determination records and carries a classification, or it is a resolved repayable issuance whose classification policy sets (FR-041; ADR-005).
Data
Inputs: two determination records, the evidence events, and the released classification rules artefact. Outputs: classified components. Validations: classification is required; an unclassified component cannot be acted on.
Dependencies
FR-012, DR-013
Rationale
The same arithmetic can be a recoverable debt in one case and an administrative error in another. What decides it is what changed in the evidence (TA §C.7.2). Legal counsel owns the question of how each class is treated under the statute.
FR-052 Must M0 High
A person decides every debt; raising is capped, grouped by cause and reversible
No overpayment is raised and no recovery starts unless a person decides each component. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (reversal mechanism), M6
Description
No overpayment is raised and no recovery starts unless a person decides each component. Automated raising has a cap per cycle on count and on value. When a single cause produces overpayments for more clients than the published threshold, the whole group is held for review before any notice goes out. A batch of debts can be reversed in one operation. The reversal also undoes recovery already taken and issues corrected notices.
Relates To
BR-005, UC-5
Parameters
N17, N18, N14
Acceptance Criteria
Given a calculated component, when no person has recorded a decision, then no debt, notice or recovery exists TA-C6.
Given automated raising that exceeds its cap in a cycle, when the cap is reached, then raising stops and escalates rather than queuing.
Given a batch identifier, when reversal is invoked, then every debt, deduction, set-off and collections referral from that batch is reversed, and corrected notices are issued.
Added v1.5 (TA §C.7.6): Given a context that has gone live, when each of its first four cycles closes, then the overpayments raised are reported to the steering committee by classification and by cause.
Data
Inputs: components and the group-review thresholds. Outputs: debts and reversal events. Validations: thresholds are set before the first live determination.
Dependencies
FR-051, FR-060
Rationale
A defect that produces a hundred thousand wrong records shows up as one pattern repeated. A process that looks only at one case at a time will never see it (TA §C.7.6).
FR-053 Must M6 Medium

Repayment agreements keep a version history. Where policy requires it, repayment continues after a recipient leaves assistance. FR-101 Must M6 Medium
Recovery rate, hardship and deferral
The rate at which a debt is recovered belongs to the repayment agreement. Show detail
First needed in: M6
Description
The rate at which a debt is recovered belongs to the repayment agreement. It lies between the statutory minimum protection and the maximum policy sets. It can be changed, and each rate has the period it applies to and the date it was recorded, so the system can say what rate was in force in any past month. A client can ask for recovery to be reduced or suspended because of hardship, or deferred. That is a discretionary decision. It is recorded with the decision-maker, their authority and their reasons, it has an end date, and it is reviewed.

Given a hardship or deferral decision, when it is recorded, then it carries the decision-maker, the authority, the reasons and an end date, and a review work item is raised before the end date.
Given a suspension that reaches its end date with no new decision, when the next payment is assembled, then recovery resumes at the agreement's rate, subject to the minimum checked at issuance (FR-048) TA-C47.
Data
