FR-217 Must M0 Medium
Continuing custody: guardianship, copies of orders and notices to the Public Guardian and Trustee
The system records the effect of a continuing custody order on guardianship: Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system records the effect of a continuing custody order on guardianship: the director as the child's sole personal guardian and the Public Guardian and Trustee as sole property guardian. It requires and records the copies of orders the Act says the director must send, and the notices the director must give the Public Guardian and Trustee. It prompts the notices policy asks for when an event affects the child's financial or legal interests. It ends the guardianship record when the order terminates.
Relates To
BR-018
Service lines
Guardianship; adoption and permanency; child protection and family services
Parameters
N01, N13, N17, N19
Authority
CFCSA ss. 50(1) and (4), 52, 53, 54.2(4) and 58; Permanency Policies, Permanency Plan After a Continuing Custody Order (CFD-300); Aboriginal Operational and Practice Standards and Indicators, 2005 (CFD-278), Guardianship Standard 21; Reportable Circumstances Policy (CFD-234) (tier 1)
Provisions
CL-D2-035, CL-D2-036, CL-D2-037, CL-D2-038, CL-D7-218, OB-LG1-106, OB-LG1-108 (5 reconciled provisions and 2 further rows; 20 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a continuing custody order, when it is recorded, then the system records the director as sole personal guardian and the Public Guardian and Trustee as sole property guardian from the date of the order, and requires a copy sent to each recipient the Act names for the child (OB-LG1-92), with the date sent.
Given an order appointing the Public Guardian and Trustee property guardian during temporary custody, or an order transferring custody to a person other than a parent in the cases the Act names (OB-LG1-106), when it is recorded, then a copy to the Public Guardian and Trustee is required and its sending recorded.
Given a child in continuing custody, or for whom a director is personal guardian under another Act, when the director consents to the child's adoption or to the child living outside British Columbia, then the system requires and records notice to the Public Guardian and Trustee.
Given an event policy lists as affecting the child's financial or legal interests (OB-IN1-16, CK-IN1-22), when it is recorded for a child whose property guardian is the Public Guardian and Trustee, then the system opens a work item to notify the Public Guardian and Trustee and records the notice.
Given an event that terminates a continuing custody order under the Act (R-LG1-98), when it is recorded, then the director's personal guardianship ends on that date, and the property guardianship ends unless an agreement under the Act continues it.
Edge case: an Indigenous child who is not a First Nation child, a Nisga'a child or a Treaty First Nation child. The copy goes to the designated representative of another Indigenous community identified by the child or by the parent, as the Act sets by the child's age (OB-LG1-92).
Data
Inputs: Orders and their dates; the child's First Nation, Treaty First Nation, Nisga'a or other Indigenous community and its designated representative; consents and events affecting the child's interests; Outputs: Guardianship periods for personal and property guardian; the record of each copy and notice sent, to whom and when; Validations: A continuing custody order is not complete on the record until each required copy is recorded as sent or the reason it is outstanding is stated.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-064, FR-067, FR-077, FR-084, INT-017
Open
The Act sets no time limit for sending a copy of an order. Policy says to send it when a signed copy is received (CFD-300 L351 and L352). The requirement sets none.
The wider list of events is in the 2005 agency standard only, and it refers to the repealed Family Relations Act (R-IN1-07, R-GU1-46: not current). No current ministry-wide policy held states the list or a time limit for the notice.
No policy held implements the copy of a permanent transfer order (s. 54.2(4)) or the notice of an application under s. 58 and the copy of its order. The Act alone is the authority. Service of the s. 58 notice within the Act's time limit (OB-LG1-108) is a hearing notice; the editor should check it against pack P10.
The incident notification form is not to be used for an incident that is a reportable circumstance (R-GU1-45, practice only). The Reportable Circumstances Policy sends those reports to the Public Guardian and Trustee where it is property guardian (pack P46).
The standard has the worker contact the federal department's lands and trust service to confirm whether it is trustee of some of the child's money. The body's current name and role need a ministry answer.
An agreement that continues property guardianship after the order ends (CFCSA s. 51.1) was read only in the cross-reference in s. 53(2).

The Act splits guardianship of a child in continuing custody between the director and the Public Guardian and Trustee and requires the director to send the order and to give stated notices (CFCSA ss. 50, 52, 54.2 and 58). The system holds the record of a child in care with the content policy sets at opening and at each review. Acceptance Criteria
Given a child admitted to care, when the record is opened, then the system requires the opening content policy lists (RC-IN1-07), including the date of admission, the child's status and Band membership or affiliation and registration number, reasons for service, placement and medical history, and a photograph.

Data

FR-220 Must M9 Medium
Youth agreement: conditions to be met before it is made and signed
The system records the director's decision to make a written agreement with a youth as a decision with a finding on each condition the Act and the Regulation set. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records the director's decision to make a written agreement with a youth as a decision with a finding on each condition the Act and the Regulation set. Before the agreement is made, it records that the director considered whether the agreement is in the youth's best interests and recommended that the youth seek advice from an independent third party. It treats the agreement as made only when the youth and a representative of the director who holds the delegation for these agreements have both signed. It makes information about the right to request an administrative review available to the youth.
Relates To
BR-018
Service lines
Youth transitions
Parameters
N08, N17, N20
Authority
CFCSA ss. 1 (definition of youth), 12.2(1), (4), (7) and (9); CFCS Regulation ss. 8.1 and 15(3); Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual, procedure on youth agreements (CFD-308); Youth Agreement form and its completion instructions (CFD-282, practice only) (tier 1)
Provisions
CL-D2-047, CL-D2-056, CL-D2-064, AU-LG1-15, R-LG1-28, R-LG1-31, R-LG2-89 (3 reconciled provisions and 4 further rows; 14 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a youth for whom an agreement is proposed, when the worker records the decision to make it, then the system requires a finding with its evidence on each condition in the Act and the Regulation (R-LG1-28, R-LG2-89), accepts any one alternative where a condition lists alternatives, and does not treat the agreement as made while a finding is missing or is not met.
Edge case: a person younger than the lower age in the Act's definition of youth (R-LG1-02) who is married, a parent or an expectant parent. The system accepts the person as a youth for this agreement and records which of those facts applies.
Given an agreement that is not yet signed, when the worker presents it for signature, then the system requires a record that the director considered whether the agreement is in the youth's best interests, and a record that the director recommended that the youth seek advice from an independent third party, made before any signature is taken.
Given a person who signs for the director, when the signature is recorded, then the system checks that the person holds, on that date, delegation of the director's power to make agreements with youth, and refuses the signature if the person does not. A youth probation officer who holds that delegation may sign only where the officer provides no youth justice services to the same youth.
Given a youth, when the agreement is signed, then the youth signs in their own right as a party and the system does not require a parent's or guardian's signature, because the Act makes the agreement enforceable against the youth (R-LG1-31).
Given a youth who asks for or is provided services under an agreement, when the agreement is produced for signature, then information about the right to request an administrative review and about the review process is made available to the youth with it.
Given the youth's signature, when it is recorded, then the system also records the youth's acknowledgement that the terms and the plan for independence were reviewed with them and that they were given information about their rights, about how to make a complaint and about the advocacy services of the Representative for Children and Youth (practice only, to confirm).
Data
Inputs: The youth's date of birth and circumstances; a finding and its evidence for each condition; the record of the best-interests consideration and of the recommendation to seek independent advice; the register of delegations; Outputs: A decision record for the agreement; the signed agreement with each signer's identity, authority and date; Validations: Every condition has a finding; the recommendation is recorded before any signature; the signer for the director holds the delegation on the signing date.
Dependencies
FR-001, FR-004, FR-026, FR-074, FR-094
Open
The rows for the conditions sit in other packs: R-LG1-28 (CFCSA s. 12.2(1)) in P08a, R-LG2-89 (CFCS Regulation s. 8.1) in P08b and R-LG1-02 (the definition of youth) in P02a. This requirement applies them.
The Standards for Youth Support Services and Agreements are not held. The child and family service standards, Chapter 2 and the youth justice manual all point to them for youth agreement practice. They may add conditions or steps before signing, and they would say who signs for the director.
Practice has the worker's supervisor sign for the director, and the form also carries an expense authority's signature (CF-D2-40, checked: not a conflict). No policy held sets the level of delegation needed. The level is data in the delegation register (P01); the delegation matrix in this pack is dated 2006 and is not current.
The agreement form says the recommendation to seek independent advice is required by s. 12.2(7) and is what makes the agreement legal. The Act places the duty in s. 12.2(4)(b) and says only that the director must recommend it.
For an Indigenous youth, Policy 1.1 requires the best-interests consideration to cover the factors the federal Act lists and to be documented. Those rows are held by P02a and P04.
The Act does not say whether the steps in s. 12.2(4) are repeated when an agreement is renewed. The modification form repeats the youth's acknowledgement for a youth agreement.
Chapter 2 (Policy 2.5) has a maintenance agreement with the parents completed before a youth agreement is entered, or the contribution waived with a team leader's approval where it is not in the youth's best interests (rows R-CP2-73 and R-CP2-75, held by P45). This requirement does not repeat that step.
Youth justice waits on a scope decision. The check on a youth probation officer needs to know whether that officer provides youth justice services to the youth.
Rationale
The Act lets a director make an agreement with a youth only on stated conditions, and it requires the director to consider the youth's best interests and to recommend independent advice before the agreement is made (CFCSA s. 12.2(1) and (4); CFCS Regulation s. 8.1). The agreement is enforceable against the youth, so the record must show that each condition was met and that the person who signed for the director had the authority to sign. LEG001-C63
FR-221 Must M9 Medium
Youth agreement: services, term, renewal and end
The system holds each youth agreement with the kinds of service it provides, its start and end dates, and each renewal as a new term. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system holds each youth agreement with the kinds of service it provides, its start and end dates, and each renewal as a new term. It refuses an initial term or a renewal term longer than the Act allows, and it lets no term run past the birthday on which the Act ends every agreement. On that birthday it ends the agreement and the assistance paid under it without a worker acting. It records how an agreement ends or is changed before then, and it keeps payments to the youth running when an agreement is modified or replaced. An agreement in force never stops the system from recording a court application or order about the youth.
Relates To
BR-018
Service lines
Youth transitions
Parameters
N01, N04, N19
Authority
CFCSA ss. 12 and 12.2(2), (5), (6) and (8); Child and Family Services File Transfer policies, transfer of agreements (CFD-262); Youth Agreement form (CFD-282, practice only, for the grounds and notice on early ending) (tier 1)
Provisions
CL-D2-053, CL-D2-054, CL-D2-055, CL-D7-118, CK-LG1-06 (4 reconciled provisions and 1 further rows; 10 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given an agreement or a renewal, when its term is entered, then the system refuses a term longer than the limit the Act sets for an initial term or for a renewal term (CK-LG1-06), and it records each renewal as a new term linked to the agreement.
Given a term whose end date would fall after the birthday on which the Act ends every agreement (CK-LG1-07), when the date is entered, then the system refuses it and offers that birthday as the latest end date.
Given an agreement still in force on that birthday, when the day ends, then the system ends the agreement, records the reason and creates no payment instruction under it for any later period.
Given an agreement, when it is recorded, then it states which of the kinds of service the Act lists it provides (residential, educational or other support services, or financial assistance), and at least one is chosen.
Edge case: a court application or order about the youth while an agreement is in force. The system records it; the agreement does not block or limit it (R-LG1-27).
Given an agreement that ends before its end date, when the end is recorded, then the system records who ended it, the date, the reason and the notice given, and shows whether the notice met the notice terms written into the agreement. The grounds for ending and the written confirmation with reasons come from the agreement form (practice only, to confirm).
Given an agreement whose terms are modified, or that is ended and replaced by a new agreement when the youth moves to another service area, when the change is made, then the system keeps payments to the youth running without a gap and records the new agreement as replacing the old (OB-CP1-76).
Data
Inputs: The youth's date of birth; the start and end date of each term; the kinds of service; the notice terms in the agreement; the term limits held in the register of time limits (CK-LG1-06, CK-LG1-07); Outputs: The agreement with its terms, renewals and changes; the end event with its reason and notice; the stop of assistance under the agreement; Validations: Each term is within its limit; no end date falls after the birthday in CK-LG1-07; at least one kind of service is recorded; a replacement agreement is linked to the agreement it replaces.
Dependencies
FR-001, FR-042, FR-061, FR-067
Open
The Act counts the terms in months and does not say how a month is counted when a term starts part way through a calendar month.
The Act says no agreement continues beyond the birthday. This requirement reads the birthday itself as the last day of the agreement. Legal advice should confirm.
Neither the Act nor the Regulation says how a youth agreement ends early. The File Transfer policies say a worker who ends an agreement must comply with notice requirements, without stating them (rows OB-CP1-76 and R-CP1-56, held by P41 and P08a). The grounds, the notice periods and the written confirmation are set by the agreement form alone (CL-D2-057, CL-D2-058). The Standards for Youth Support Services and Agreements are not held.
CF-D2-39 (the youth's notice to end the agreement) was checked and is not a conflict.
The form says the agreement also ends when the youth comes into the director's care. No legislation or policy held says so.
When an agreement is ended and replaced on a move to another service area, the Act does not say whether the first term of the new agreement counts as an initial term.
Rates, maximum amounts and approval levels for financial assistance under a youth agreement are not in any held document.
Rationale
The Act limits the first term and each renewal of a youth agreement and ends every agreement on a fixed birthday (CFCSA s. 12.2(5) and (6)). These are legal time limits, so they run in the system. The Act also says an agreement does not limit the court's power to make an order about the youth (s. 12.2(8)). Policy requires notice requirements to be met when an agreement is ended and payment to continue when it is modified or replaced (File Transfer policies). The dates of each term are counted later, when the person asks for an agreement as a specified adult. LEG001-C64

CL-D2-048, CL-D2-049, CL-D2-050, CL-D2-051, OB-LG1-17 (4 reconciled provisions and 1 further rows; 14 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a youth who is an Indigenous child, when a party is added to the agreement, then the system accepts only the body the Act names for that youth: the First Nation for a First Nation child; the Nisga'a Nation or the youth's Nisga'a Village for a Nisga'a child; the Treaty First Nation for a Treaty First Nation child; and otherwise the legal entity representing the youth's Indigenous community. The party is recorded as a participant outside the Crown.
Given such a party, when it is added, then the system requires the youth's recorded consent to the Indigenous community being a party, and it does not add the party without that consent.
Given an agreement that includes such a party, when it is presented for signature, then it holds a description of the party's role and the conditions on the use, disclosure and security of information provided under the agreement to the party. The system refuses the signature step if either is missing, and it records those conditions as limits on any information it provides to the party.
Given a party that withdraws from the agreement, when the withdrawal is recorded, then the system records its date and keeps the agreement in force between the youth and the director.
Given a youth who is an Indigenous child, when a youth agreement is about to be made or renewed, then the system does not record it as made or renewed until, for each parent, the care provider and the Indigenous governing body that has told the director it acts for the youth's community, it holds either a record that notice of the measure was given or a recorded decision not to give notice on a ground policy allows, with the supervisor's approval and the reasons.
Given an agreement for an Indigenous youth that has an end date, when renewal is to be considered, then the system raises the work item to give notice early enough for the notice period policy sets (CK-IN1-26) to run before the renewal.
Edge case: the youth does not consent to the Indigenous community being a party. Notice to the Indigenous governing body is still required, because the notice does not depend on consent. The system keeps the consent record and the notice record separate.
Data
Inputs: Whether the youth is an Indigenous child and of which kind the Act lists; the youth's Indigenous community; the youth's consent; the party's role and the information conditions; the Indigenous governing body that has told the director it acts for the community; the notice given or the decision not to give it; Outputs: The party on the agreement; limits on use recorded on information provided to the party; the withdrawal record; the notice record or the recorded decision with approval and reasons; Validations: The party matches the kind the Act allows for that youth; consent is on record before the party is added; role and conditions are present before signing; a notice record or a decision not to give notice comes before the agreement is made or renewed.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-067, FR-075, FR-080, FR-084, FR-085
Open
CF-D2-09: both passages were read. The agreement form tells the youth that their Indigenous community may be informed that the agreement has been made, under an agreement with the community (CFCSA s. 92.1). The federal Act and Policy 1.1 require notice to the Indigenous governing body before the agreement is made or renewed. The two statements concern different bodies and different moments, so they do not contradict each other, but the form (dated 2019) does not tell the youth about the prior notice. The requirement follows the federal Act and Policy 1.1.
The agreement form sets out the community's duties for information twice, with different wording (clauses 3 and 4). Which wording is the standard condition is not settled.
The Act names the party by the youth's status. Policy 1.1 and the Framework for Community Agreements speak of the Indigenous community being a party. The Framework adds that a Community Agreement may name who the director approaches.
The general capability for notice of a significant measure (the form of notice, the notice period, shorter or verbal notice, a parent or care provider who cannot be found, and what a notice may contain under federal Act s. 12(2)) is held by P04 (CL-D7-056 to CL-D7-068). This requirement states only what a youth agreement needs from it.
Policy 1.1 calls the notice period required for most notices in its procedures and a default guideline in its notice schedule. P04 holds the clock (CK-IN1-26).
CF-D1-13 and CF-D7-15 (MQ-094) concern agreements under ss. 5 to 8 and do not touch youth agreements. CF-D1-25 concerns another form. CF-D7-01 sets the 2005 agency standards against the federal Act; this requirement follows the federal Act.
Neither the Act nor policy says how the youth's consent is recorded or withdrawn, or whether information may still be provided to a party after it withdraws.
Rationale
The Act lets the First Nation, the Nisga'a Nation or Village, the Treaty First Nation or the legal entity representing the youth's Indigenous community be a party to a youth agreement, and it requires the agreement to state that party's role and the conditions on information provided to it (CFCSA s. 12.2(2.1) and (2.2)). The federal Act requires notice to the parent, the care provider and the Indigenous governing body before a significant measure, and policy names entering or renewing an agreement with a youth as one (federal Act s. 12; Policy 1.1). FR-224 Must M0 High
Agreements with specified adults: who qualifies, purposes and limits
The system supports the director's decision on whether a person qualifies for an agreement with a specified adult. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (no implementing policy held)
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system supports the director's decision on whether a person qualifies for an agreement with a specified adult. From the record of the person's time as a child it works out which of the Regulation's criteria the person meets, including the count of days under the listed agreements, orders and guardianships. Where a criterion rests on an arrangement under an Indigenous law, it requires a record of the consultation with the relevant Indigenous authorities before the arrangement is treated as comparable. It records the purpose of each support in the agreement and refuses a term or a support the Regulation does not allow.
Relates To
BR-018
Service lines
Youth transitions
Parameters
N01, N07, N12, N13
Authority
CFCSA ss. 1 (definition of specified adult), 12.3 and 12.4; CFCS Regulation ss. 8.3, 8.31, 8.32, 8.4, 8.5 and 15(3) (tier 1)
Provisions
CK-LG2-20, OB-LG2-69, R-LG1-08, R-LG2-90, R-LG2-91, R-LG2-92 (0 reconciled provisions and 6 further rows; 6 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a person who asks for an agreement, when eligibility is assessed, then the system first establishes that the person is a specified adult as the Act defines it, and then shows for each criterion in the Regulation (R-LG2-90) whether the record supports it, with the orders, agreements, guardianships, adoption or transfers of custody relied on, their dates and their sources. The decision record names each criterion met.
Given the criterion that counts days (R-LG2-91), when it is assessed, then the system counts each day on which the person, while an eligible child as the Regulation defines it, was under any of the listed agreements, orders, guardianships or comparable arrangements, counts a day once however many of them applied, leaves out an interim order that the person be returned to or remain with a parent, and compares the total with the minimum the Regulation sets (CK-LG2-20).
Given an arrangement under an Indigenous law that a criterion relies on, when a worker records it as comparable, then the system requires a record that the director consulted the relevant Indigenous authorities and considered both the nature and the purpose of the arrangement (OB-LG2-69). It accepts only an Indigenous law of a First Nation in British Columbia, the Nisga'a Nation or a Treaty First Nation, and it records what an Indigenous authority confirms with that authority as its source.
Given an agreement being drafted, when a support is entered, then it is recorded against a purpose the Act lists: financial assistance the person may use for any purpose; securing housing and remaining housed; taking part in a prescribed program or activity; or other needs while receiving housing or program support. A program or activity is recorded with its kind, and the list of kinds includes those the Regulation names and stays open to other educational, health and cultural programs (R-LG2-92).
Given a proposed term or support that would pass a limit the Regulation sets by the person's age or by total months of support (R-LG2-94), when it is entered, then the system refuses it and shows the limit. The exceptions the Regulation makes for housing assistance, and any period during which the Regulation suspends a limit (CK-LG2-26), are applied by rule.
Given an agreement for the benefit of a specified adult made with a person who provided residential services for that adult as a child and agrees to provide housing, when it is drafted, then the system checks that the adult meets a criterion and that the person provided residential services immediately before the birthday the Regulation names (R-LG2-93), refuses a term past the limit for this kind of agreement (R-LG2-95), and requires the term that lets the director end the agreement when the adult no longer needs that assistance (OB-LG1-20).
Given a person found not to qualify, when the decision is recorded, then its reasons name the criteria not met and the facts relied on, and information about the right to request an administrative review is made available to the person with the decision.
Data
Inputs: The person's date of birth; the record of services, orders, agreements, guardianships, adoption and transfers of custody during childhood, with dates and sources; what Indigenous authorities confirm; the record of consultation; the Regulation's criteria and limits as rules (R-LG2-90, R-LG2-91, R-LG2-94, CK-LG2-20); Outputs: An eligibility decision naming the criteria met and the day count; the agreement with the purpose of each support, its term and the running total of months of program support; Validations: The day count comes from recorded periods, never from a typed total; a comparable arrangement has a consultation record; no term or support passes a limit in R-LG2-94 or R-LG2-95.
Dependencies
FR-001, FR-002, FR-010, FR-084, DR-001, DR-004
Open
This requirement applies rows that sit in other packs: R-LG1-32 and R-LG1-33 (CFCSA ss. 12.3 and 12.4) in P08a; OB-LG1-20 (s. 12.4(2)(b)) in P05; R-LG2-93 to R-LG2-95 and CK-LG2-21 to CK-LG2-26 (CFCS Regulation ss. 8.32 to 8.5) in P09. The editor should join them here.
No policy on agreements with specified adults is held. The File Transfer policies point to a policy on agreements with young adults, the earlier name for these agreements, which is not held. Rates, amounts, approval levels and the way a person applies are not in any held document.
The Regulation counts the days on which the person was under a listed arrangement. This requirement reads a day under more than one arrangement as a single day. The Regulation does not say whether the first and the last day of an order or agreement both count.
The Regulation does not say how the director consults the relevant Indigenous authorities, or what follows when an authority does not answer.
Section 8.5 of the Regulation suspends limits by reference to s. 8.4 (a) and (b). Section 8.4 was replaced in 2024 and now has subsections (1) and (2). Which current limits s. 8.5 suspends needs legal advice.
For administrative review, the Regulation defines a young adult as a person who has, or is eligible for, an agreement. Whether a person found not to qualify may ask for a review of that finding needs legal advice.
A person's time under the care of an Indigenous authority, in another province or before the current systems may not be in the ministry's records. No held document says how that evidence is obtained. Specified personal guardianship includes guardianship under a repealed Act, so some periods rest on legacy records.
Rationale
The Regulation lets a director make an agreement with a specified adult only if the person meets a criterion drawn from the person's time as a child, including a minimum number of days under listed agreements, orders and guardianships (CFCS Regulation s. 8.3(2)). Those facts are years old when the decision is made, so the record of each period must be kept with its dates and its source. The Regulation also requires the director to consult the relevant Indigenous authorities before treating an arrangement under an Indigenous law as comparable (s. 8.3(4)). LEG002-C5
FR-225 Must M9 Medium
Child comes into care or returns home: the assistance case and the parents' benefits
When a child is removed from parents who receive employment assistance, the system prepares the notice that tells the family's assistance case the child is living outside the family home. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (policy rows held by other packs)
First needed in: M9
Description
When a child is removed from parents who receive employment assistance, the system prepares the notice that tells the family's assistance case the child is living outside the family home. When a child comes into care by agreement, it records that the parents were advised that the child benefits stop. When the child returns home, it prepares the notice of return and records that the parents were told how to resume benefits for the child, including health care coverage. Each notice crosses to the assistance case as evidence with its source and purpose, and a worker confirms it before it is sent.

Provisions
CL-D2-027, CL-D2-029 (2 reconciled provisions and 0 further rows; 5 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a child removed from parents who receive employment assistance, when the removal is recorded, then the system prepares a notice to the family's assistance case that the child is living outside the family home and that the family's full shelter allowance needs to be kept while the family works toward the child's return, and it records when the worker sends it.
Given a notice to the assistance case, when it is sent, then it crosses as evidence that carries only that fact, its date, its source and its purpose.
Given a child who comes into care under a voluntary care agreement or a special needs agreement, when the agreement is made, then the system records that the parents were advised that they are not eligible for the federal and provincial child benefits for the child from the date policy sets (R-CP2-80), that benefits paid after that date may have to be returned, and that they can contact the Canada Revenue Agency with questions.
Given a child returned to the parents' care, when the return is recorded, then the system prepares a notice to the family's assistance case that the child has returned, where the parents have been receiving employment assistance, and it records that the parents were told the steps to resume benefits for the child, including health care coverage and the federal child benefit.
Given a child who comes into care by removal, when the child's record is opened, then a work item is raised to tell the parents, where required, to end the child benefit while the child is in care, with the notice to parents as a generated letter (practice only, to confirm).
Given a child still in care at the point the job aid gives (CK-GU1-11), or for whom a permanency decision is made earlier, when that point is reached, then a work item is raised to send the assistance case the confirmation that the child is cared for outside the parental home (practice only, to confirm).
Edge case: a child expected to be in care only briefly. The system does not end the child's health coverage through the family's assistance case, or raise the benefit notice to the parents, until the worker who removed the child confirms it is needed (practice only, to confirm).
Data

Given a decision that resulted in a serious sanction as policy defines it (R-GU1-01), when a foster caregiver's written request for review is received, then the system records the request with its date, links it to the investigation or review and the sanction decision, and tests it against the time limit for making a request (CK-GU1-01), counted from the date the caregiver received the decision.
Given a recorded request, when screening starts, then the system records that the caregiver was told about the process, its timeframe, the information to be collected, how the outcome will be communicated and that the review cannot overturn the decision, and starts the time limit for the caregiver's written concerns (CK-GU1-02).
Given a request confirmed eligible, when eligibility is recorded, then the system produces a letter to the caregiver naming the issues to be examined and the timeframe, due within the limit policy sets (CK-GU1-03), and shares it with the leadership of the Service Delivery Area or ICFS Agency involved.
Given a request that did not follow a serious sanction, when it is found ineligible, then the system produces a letter with the reasons and the options for external review, due within the limit policy sets (CK-GU1-04).
Edge case: the request needs no earlier attempt at local review or resolution by a responsible manager (R-GU1-03). The system does not require one before accepting the request.
Data
Inputs: The request and its date; the date the caregiver received the sanction decision; the investigation or review and the sanction; the caregiver's written concerns; Outputs: A screening decision with reasons; the acceptance or decline letter; running time limits; Validations: A request is accepted only where a serious sanction is on record and written concerns were received; each time limit is a registered clock in business days.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-062, FR-064, FR-067, FR-092
Open
The policy does not say in terms who decides eligibility; the Director of Quality Assurance receives the request (AU-GU1-02 is inferred).
The policy states no consequence for a request made after the time limit, or for written concerns received late, and no power to extend either.
The policy says a request is declined where there was no serious sanction. It does not say what happens where there was a sanction but the caregiver gives no written concerns.
Resource Work Policy 8.21 (dispute resolution for caregivers), the local route this review may bypass, is not held.
Rationale
Policy gives a foster caregiver a review after a serious sanction and sets time limits on both the caregiver and the ministry (CFD-162). The caregiver is entitled to prompt and clear information about what the review covers and its limits. CFD162-C1

The record of steps taken is kept either way, so the system behaves the same; whether a recorded attempt with no reply satisfies the Act is a legal question for the ministry.
Policy says the ministry is still working with Indigenous partners on how to decide who an applicable Indigenous governing body is under the Adoption Act (CFD-277 L316).
No source says whether the time limit for the written notice is counted in calendar or business days.
The schedules of designated representatives under Adoption Regulation s. 5 were not read; they are reference data.
Rationale
The CFCSA and the Adoption Act each make consultation and cooperation with the designated representative and any other applicable Indigenous governing body a condition that comes before a request to place, or a placement of, an Indigenous child (CFCSA s. 50.06; Adoption Act s. 7). The system must be able to show the condition was met for each community. LEG001-C67

Open
Policy lets the homestudy update be started, not finished, before the proposal package is given (CFD-277 L709). The check is therefore a prompt at the proposal and a condition at placement (Standard 10.4(1)).
The placement priorities themselves (CFCSA s. 71 and the federal Act) are specified in pack P04; this requirement records how the match was assessed against them.
Standard 10.3(8) also requires a review by the Provincial Exceptions Committee before an Indigenous child is placed with a non-Indigenous prospective adoptive parent who is not a relative (CFD-277 L1029). It sits with the proposal and placement packs.

CF-D2-22 read in the source: the adoption policy tells the prospective adoptive parent the access order ends when an adoption order is applied for (CFD-277 L1081), and elsewhere says when the court grants the order (L563). Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance Criteria
Given a child with an adoption plan, when a worker records a person as a significant individual, then the system accepts only a person in a class the Act allows (R-LG2-34), opens a separate agreement record for that person, and requires a finding on whether openness with them is in the child's best interests.

Open

Data
Inputs: search applications with supporting documents; fees received; veto and no-contact declaration status; the located person's wish about contact; information received from public bodies; Outputs: search records with outcome; notice of outcome to the applicant; record of assistance to meet or communicate; Validations: applicant class and documents complete; fee paid before the search begins; no identifying disclosure against the located person's wish.
Dependencies
FR-027, FR-077, FR-080, FR-004
Open
No ministry policy on the search service is held. The Act says the Provincial director 'may' provide the assistance, subject to the regulations: the system must allow and record a decision not to assist.
Disclosure vetoes and no-contact declarations are filed with the registrar general, who also applies the period a veto lasts after the filer's death (CK-LG2-07). The system needs their status from the vital statistics agency (see candidates). No source says how that status reaches the Provincial director today.
The Act does not say what an applicant is told when a search is refused because of a veto or declaration.
How search and application fees are received and accounted for is for the payments group (CF13).
Rationale
Adoption Act s. 71 sets who may ask the Provincial director for help to locate a person, bars help against a person who filed a disclosure veto or no-contact declaration, forbids disclosing the name or location of a located person who wishes no contact, and requires the applicant to be told the outcome. Given a placement agreement, when it is recorded, then it holds the request to place, the responsibilities each party takes, the date of placement and both signatures, and the child cannot be shown as placed before both signatures are recorded.
Given a planned placement, when the medical examination of the child is not recorded, or is older than policy allows before placement (CK-AD1-21), then the system warns the worker and records how the worker resolved the warning.
Given a signed placement agreement, when the date of placement arrives and the worker confirms the child was received, then the residency starts on that date and every time limit that runs from placement starts with it.
Edge case: given an agreement that authorises a caregiver, not a prospective adoptive parent, to carry out the director's rights and responsibilities, when it is recorded, then it holds the same particulars and starts no residency.
Data
Inputs: The continuing custody order, how it was made and its appeal status; the placement agreement; the pre-placement steps and their dates; Outputs: A placement record with its date; the start of the residency; the start events for time limits that run from placement; Validations: The request is refused unless a condition in the Act is met; the placement date is the date in the signed agreement.
Dependencies

Acceptance Criteria
Given an inquiry from prospective adoptive parents or an authority in another province about a named child in care, when it is recorded, then a reply is due within the limit policy sets (CK-AD3-05), and the other authority's reply and homestudy run as clocks the ministry does not own (CK-AD3-06, CK-AD3-07).
Given a proposed adoption plan for another province, when the worker prepares the written notice of it, then the system requires the recorded approval of the regional manager responsible for adoption (AU-AD3-04) and tracks the receiving province's written acceptance.
Given a placement in another province, when it is recorded, then the system creates work to request the notice of placement, to forward the listed records within the limit policy sets (CK-AD3-17) and to request progress reports on the schedule policy sets unless otherwise negotiated (CK-AD3-08, CK-AD3-09).
Edge case: the rule that ends the child's health coverage at the end of the month of placement (R-AD3-08, CK-AD3-03) does not apply to a child placed in another province. Coverage continues until the event policy sets (R-AD3-09, CK-AD3-10).
Edge case: prospective adoptive parents living in British Columbia plan to move to another province during the post-placement period and consent in writing. Notice to the receiving province and the documents that follow are due by the limits policy sets (CK-AD3-15, CK-AD3-16), and family information goes only under their recorded consent to disclosure.
Edge case: the placement is disrupted. The system records the receiving province's notice of an emergency placement against the limit the protocol sets (CK-AD3-18), and the worker's decision on whether the child stays or returns with the factors policy lists (R-AD3-15).
Given a final progress report that recommends completion and the worker's recorded decision to complete, when the Director of Adoption's consent is requested, then the request, the consent and the documents forwarded are recorded. When the order arrives the system records the closing statement on where the adoption records are held and closes the records.
Data

FR-278 Must M0 Medium
Assessing and supervising for another province's permanent ward under delegated authority
The system supports adoption work for a child who is a permanent ward of another province or territory and is to live with prospective adoptive parents in British Columbia. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (the directive calls itself an interim measure)
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system supports adoption work for a child who is a permanent ward of another province or territory and is to live with prospective adoptive parents in British Columbia. It records the originating province or territory as the child's guardian and as the decision-maker. It records the director's role as acting on authority that province or territory delegated for that child. It records the request for assessment, the applicants' application, the written assessment and the supervision agreement with its delegation of authority. It does not let supervision of the residency start without that agreement.
Relates To
BR-019
Service lines
Adoption and permanency; guardianship
Parameters
N13, N17, N21
Authority
Practice Directive 2021-01, Facilitating Extra-Provincial Ward Adoptions in British Columbia (CFD-219, interim); CFCSA ss. 92 and 93(2); Adoption Act s. 49(b); Practice Standards 68 to 70 (CFD-044), which now only point to the directive (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D2-219, CL-D2-220, CL-D2-221, CL-D2-222, CL-D2-223 (5 reconciled provisions and 0 further rows; 15 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a request for assessment from an originating province or territory, when it is recorded, then the system assigns it to an adoption worker with full adoption delegation, and records the application given to the applicants, the completed assessment and the date it was submitted to that province or territory for its decision.
Edge case: the assessment notes concerns. The system records the letter that restates them to the originating province or territory, any further discussion with its local office, and a referral to dispute resolution where agreement is not reached.
Given a child with no completed supervision agreement and delegation of authority on record, when a worker tries to record supervision of the residency, then the system refuses (OB-AD2-31).
Given a completed agreement, when supervision is under way, then the frequency of communication and reports comes from the agreement, each report sent is recorded, and decisions on the child's day-to-day care are recorded as referred to and made by the originating province or territory.
Edge case: a child protection concern arises during supervision. The system creates the referral to child protection and records that the originating province or territory was told.
Given a ward of another province or territory, when a worker opens a decision on approval of the applicants, residency, placement, adoption subsidy or the court application, then the system records it only as a decision of the originating province or territory (R-AD2-25, R-AD2-26).
Data
Inputs: The originating province or territory and its contacts; its request for assessment; the applicants' application; the assessment; the supervision agreement and delegation of authority; its instructions and decisions; Outputs: The assessment as submitted; letters of concern; supervision reports; a record of each decision with the originating province or territory as decision-maker; Validations: The worker holds full adoption delegation; the agreement and delegation are on record before supervision; information about the applicants is held with their record and information about the child with the child's record.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-084, FR-085, FR-070, FR-077
Open
The sample supervision agreement (Appendix A of the directive) is not held, so the reporting terms it sets are not known.
The dispute resolution process is one sentence in the directive. No escalation steps beyond the people directly involved are stated.
The directive says adoption workers act with delegation under section 93(3) of the CFCSA. The Act as held shows subsections (3) and (4) of section 93 repealed. The ministry should confirm the provision relied on.
The directive is interim and dated 2021. Whether it has been replaced is not known.
Rationale
The directive says British Columbia legislation gives the director no power to assess, establish residency, supervise or finalise the adoption of another jurisdiction's permanent ward, and no authority to collect, use or disclose personal information for it. The director acts only on authority the originating province or territory delegates child by child (CFCSA s. 93(2)), so the system must hold that delegation and keep the decisions with the guardian. Direct placement: notice of intent and the duties before the child is received
The system records a notice of intent to receive a child by direct placement and the date the notice is deemed given. Show detail

The system records a notice of intent to receive a child by direct placement and the date the notice is deemed given. BR-019

Provisions
CL-D2-234, CL-D2-235, CL-D2-236, CL-D2-237, CL-D2-238, CL-D2-241, CL-D2-246, CL-D2-251, AU-LG2-26, R-AD3-23, R-LG2-50, RC-AD3-19 (8 reconciled provisions and 4 further rows; 39 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a written notice of intent in the prescribed form, when a director accepts it as complete, then the system records that date as the date notice was given (R-LG2-53), records the written acknowledgement, and records that the case is a direct placement and not a placement with a relative or of a child who lives outside the province (R-AD3-18).
Given a pre-placement assessment, when it is prepared, then the system requires a written report by a social worker as the regulation defines one (R-LG2-50), covering the matters the regulation lists (OB-LG2-49), from the sources and interviews policy lists (OB-AD3-34).
Given the required documents are gathered, when the assessment is opened, then it is due within the limit policy sets (CK-AD3-19). Completion after the limit needs recorded reasons and the approval of the supervisor or team leader (AU-AD3-12). The fee the fees regulation sets is recorded as collected before the work starts (R-AD3-23).
Given the history and the assessment, when they are given out, then the system records the date the prospective adoptive parents received the history, the dates they and the placing parent or guardian received the assessment, and any concern the worker recorded about the history. It keeps a copy of the history for the child.
Given every pre-placement duty is recorded, when the worker asks for sign-off, then the supervisor's or team leader's signature is recorded (AU-AD3-11). The record is then held for the period policy sets (CK-AD3-25) and closed if no notice of placement arrives.
Edge case: a person other than the worker counsels the child. The system records that person's written confirmation that the Act's requirements were met (RC-AD3-19).
Given a consent to adoption by the placing parent or guardian, when it is recorded, then the prospective adoptive parent named in it is recorded as joint guardian with that parent or guardian. The joint guardianship ends on the adoption order, a revocation of the consent or a court declaration (R-LG2-22).
Data

FR-061, FR-067, FR-004, FR-071, FR-074
Open
The standards say the ministry's part in most direct placements is limited to giving information and pointing people to a licensed adoption agency. The volume of ministry-run direct placements is not known.

The Adoption Fees Regulation is not held, so the fees are not in the register.

Rationale
Section 8(2) of the Adoption Act makes a director do these things as soon as possible after notice, and section 9 lets the prospective adoptive parents receive the child only once the assessment and the history have been given. Receiving a child earlier is an offence, so the dates on which each duty was done are the evidence that the placement was lawful. Section 8(2)(b) requires the history to be preserved for the child. CF-D2-38, read in the source: the set wording for the report (CFD-044 L2997 and L3604) has the Director state that the notice of placement came at least the section 31 period before the hearing. CF10 Children and youth with support needs 15
This group covers services for children and youth with support needs: residency, eligibility for the At Home Program, Autism Funding and Family Support Services, consent, planning, service requests and paying a family member. Policy gives guidelines, not a rule, for when to arrange the later assessment on the under-age route, and asks for discretion to meet the age limit (CFD-047 L95 to L99). The system schedules to the limit and lets the Regional Contact set the date within it.

Policy does not say how the ministry learns that a Direct Admit child no longer meets a category.
Rationale
Policy sets three routes into the program, each with its own evidence, and makes continued eligibility on two of them depend on a later assessment (CFD-047, statements 14 to 21). The system must know the route to know what is owed next. CFD047-C1

Edge case: the service is delivered under the CFCSA mandate. The system allows sharing with child protection without the family's prior consent and records section 79 or section 96 as the basis (R-SN1-36).
Data
Inputs: The mandate each service falls under (reference data, R-RX1-06); the child's care arrangement and who holds custody; consents; section 96 requests; Outputs: Access decisions and refusals; a record of each sharing with its basis; the governing Act recorded on each support needs record; Validations: The basis is checked against the service's mandate and the child's care arrangement at the time of sharing.
Dependencies
NFR-SEC-002, NFR-SEC-004, FR-028, FR-075, FR-077, FR-080, DR-005
Open
A worker may deliver services in both mandates to the same family (contracted respite is inside, support planning is outside). Policy does not say how one record that serves both is to be treated; the requirement assumes the mandate is recorded for each service and each piece of information.
For a child under a voluntary care agreement, a special needs agreement or an Extended Family Program arrangement, Policy 2(b)(i) names 'the child/youth or parent' as the person who consents and Procedure 2(b)(i) names 'the parent/guardian' (CFD-127 L47, L96). Same document, same tier: not resolved here.
CF-D8-29 (settled by hierarchy): a practice guideline says consent forms are not needed inside the ministry; policy requires consent or a section 96 request. The requirement follows policy.
Table 1 survives only in a repair transcription of the policy (R-RX1-06); the ministry should confirm the list of services in and out of mandate.
Standard 1.6(23) lists cases where a child protection worker does not seek a parent's consent (risk of harm, a criminal investigation, a supervisor's approval). They belong to the protection response and are not restated here.
Rationale
Since the policy change that took most support needs services out of the CFCSA mandate, those services are governed by FOIPPA. Policy bars each group of workers from the other's records and allows sharing only on consent or a section 96 request (CFD-127, CFD-271). The rule depends on which Act governs the information, so it must be recorded on the information itself. CFD127-C1

FR-299 Must M0 Medium
Restricting access to a record that has heightened sensitivity and a risk of harm
The system lets any staff member propose that a record be restricted, with the reason, and sends the proposal to the Authorized Position. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system lets any staff member propose that a record be restricted, with the reason, and sends the proposal to the Authorized Position. The Authorized Position records an assessment against the two criteria policy sets: heightened sensitivity, and a reasonable expectation of harm to the individual the information is about. Where both are met the Authorized Position applies the restriction. A restriction covers every instance of the record in every medium the system holds or tracks, and leaves the record open only to the limited group policy names. The nature of each restriction is recorded as evidence of the action taken.
Relates To
BR-022
Service lines
All service lines
Parameters
N06, N17, N21
Authority
Managing Access to Records through Restriction Policy (CFD-240), policy statements A and procedures C.1 to C.4; Core Policy B9 Documentation Policy (CFD-201), which applies the same test to child and youth mental health records (tier 2)

CL-D8-001, CL-D8-002, CL-D8-003, CL-D8-004, CL-D8-005, CL-D8-006, CL-D8-010, OB-RP1-02 (7 reconciled provisions and 1 further rows; 27 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a staff member who believes a record should be restricted, when they propose it, then the system requires the reason and creates a work item for the Authorized Position (OB-RP1-02).
Given a proposal, when the Authorized Position assesses it, then the system records a finding on each of the two criteria and refuses to apply a restriction unless both are met (R-RP1-01, R-RP1-02, R-RP1-03).
Edge case: a historical record of a current ministry employee who was formerly in care, or in an out of care status, may be restricted without the assessment. The system records that this exception was used (R-RP1-04).
Given the Authorized Position is among the people the restriction is meant to keep out, when they try to apply it, then the system requires ownership of the record to be reassigned first (OB-RP1-05).

NFR-SEC-002, NFR-SEC-004, FR-067, FR-089
See also
FR-384 (rests on some of the same provisions).
Open
CF-D8-01 (read in both documents): the policy glossary defines the Authorized Position as Team Leader, Office Manager, or authorized Records Advisor or Technician (CFD-240 L101); the FAQ says Team Leader or above, or Office Manager (CFD-239 L13). Who holds the position is reference data, and the policy prevails over the FAQ. The ministry should confirm whether a Records Advisor or Technician may apply a restriction.
CF-D8-03 (read in all three documents): the policy speaks of 'a historical record' of an employee formerly in care or in an out of care status; the FAQ and the guideline name particular file types. Which records the exception reaches is not settled by policy.
The policy describes who may see a restricted record only by the effect in the current case system (CFD-240 L52): team leaders and above, the office manager, and users assigned to the record. The ministry should confirm that group as the rule, and whether it is measured within the local office (the FAQ says restriction is managed at the local office level; the policy does not).
The policy tells staff to remove from the mental health clinical system a record that system cannot restrict and to track it elsewhere (CFD-240 L53 to L58). That is a workaround. The duty underneath is that restriction reaches all media and instances; whether mental health records come into this system waits on the scope decision.
The policy does not say what happens to a restriction when responsibility for the record moves to another office (FR-301) or is shared between two (FR-304).
Rationale
Policy requires that restriction be applied to records in the control of the ministry where there is heightened sensitivity and a risk of harm, on all media and instances, and that only a limited group of persons have access (CFD-240, statements A). FR-300 Must M9 Medium
Reviewing and removing restrictions, and keeping restricted records onsite
The system keeps a register of every restriction with its nature and its review date. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system keeps a register of every restriction with its nature and its review date. It brings each restriction back to the Authorized Position for review at least as often as policy requires. At a review the Authorized Position can reassign ownership, remove people who no longer need access, and decide whether the restriction is still required. When a restriction no longer applies, the system removes it from every instance of the record. While a restriction is active, the system does not let the record be sent to offsite storage.

Acceptance Criteria
Given a restriction, when it is applied, then the system requires a review date no later than the maximum policy sets (CK-RP1-02) and creates a review work item for the Authorized Position who set it or their successor (CK-RP1-01).
Given a review, when the Authorized Position completes it, then the system records whether ownership was reassigned, who lost access, and whether the restriction continues, with a new review date if it does (OB-RP1-09).

Policy says the Deputy Minister delegates financial authority in writing to a position, and that a delegation is not recognised until it is in the official register (CFD-161, chapters 1 and 4). FR-004 and FR-046 refuse an approver without authority; this requirement states what that authority is and where it is read from. CFD161-C1

Acceptance Criteria
Given a purchase authorization being issued, when its total is above the ceiling policy sets (R-FI1-39), or it names a kind of goods policy excludes (R-FI1-40), then the system refuses to issue it.
Given a purchase authorization being issued, when the signer does not hold expense authority for the responsibility centre charged, then the system refuses the signature.
Given an issued authorization, when it is saved, then it names one supplier and one maximum amount, is filed on the client's record, and cannot be edited; a mistake is corrected by voiding it and issuing another, and the voided one is kept.
Given a supplier's invoice with the original authorization, when it arrives, then the system matches it to the issued authorization and refuses payment above the authorized amount, to a different supplier, or against a voided authorization.
Edge case: Given an authorization already matched to a paid invoice, when a second invoice cites it, then the system refuses the second payment.
Data
Inputs: Client, purchaser, supplier, items with maximum cost, account coding, expense authority, date of issue; supplier invoice; Outputs: The authorization as a document on the client's record; its state (issued, voided, invoiced, paid); a payment instruction for the matched invoice; Validations: Total within the ceiling (R-FI1-39); no excluded goods (R-FI1-40); signer holds expense authority for the charged responsibility centre on the date of issue.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-034, FR-042, FR-050, FR-071, FR-094
Open
Policy describes a pre-printed numbered paper form signed by the purchaser in front of the expense authority. Whether the authorization may be issued and signed electronically (FR-074) is a ministry decision; the limits and the record are the same either way.
Custody and monthly count of the paper form stock (CL-D8-112) are left to the office unless the form stays on paper.
Rationale
Policy limits a purchase authorization to client goods and services, to one supplier and amount, and to the signature of an expense authority for the centre charged. A copy must sit on the client's file and the supplier is paid on return of the original. CFD161-C11

P47 holds the rest of the administrative review procedure: the designation of the review authority, who may ask and about what, the time limits, the views to be sought and the outcome (CFCS Regulation ss. 14, 15(1), 17 to 19). The Regulation does not say how, or within what time, the person is told of a decision not to proceed.
The agreement forms tell a youth how to make a complaint. No held document says how the complaints process and the administrative review relate; the ministry's complaints policy is not held.
The Regulation says a request must be made to a director. Who receives a request for the director is a matter of delegation (P01).
Rationale
The Act requires a director to establish an administrative procedure for reviewing the exercise of a director's powers, duties and functions, and to make information about it available to any person on request (CFCSA s. 93.1). The Regulation lets a request be made by any means, limits the grounds on which a review authority may decide not to proceed, and requires the person who asked to be told the decision and the reasons (CFCS Regulation ss. 15(2), 15(3) and 16). FR-337 Must M0 Medium
Deciding whether an event is a reportable circumstance

First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system records a death, an injury or an incident involving a child or youth as an event of its own and helps the practitioner decide whether it is a reportable circumstance. CL-D8-183, AU-LG2-43, AU-LG2-44, AU-LG2-46, CK-LG2-28, CK-LG2-29, OB-LG2-78, OB-LG2-79, OB-LG2-80, OB-LG2-81 (1 reconciled provisions and 9 further rows; 16 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a recorded request, when the review authority takes it up, then the system records the date the review started and runs the completion limit (CK-LG2-28) from the date the request was made. It extends the limit only on a recorded agreement of the review authority and the person who asked (AU-LG2-43), and records a missed limit.
Given a review in progress, when the review authority records its decision, then the system requires a record of the efforts made to find out the views of the child or young adult who is the subject, the person who asked and the director concerned (OB-LG2-79), and holds the views and information of anyone else consulted (AU-LG2-44).
Given a decision, when it is recorded, then it shows that the review authority considered the factors the Regulation lists (OB-LG2-80), and each recommendation to the director is held as a recommendation. The matter under review changes only by a separate decision of the director (AU-LG2-45).
Given a completed review, when the decision is recorded, then the system produces a copy for the person who asked, the director and any other person the review authority names, records when and how each copy was given, and times this against the limit the Regulation sets (CK-LG2-29).
Edge case: a child who is the subject of the review and did not ask for it. The child is given a copy unless the review authority records its opinion that this is not in the child's best interests (AU-LG2-46). A young adult who is the subject is always given a copy.
Given a recommendation, when the decision is issued, then it is tracked as its own action with the person responsible, a due date and the response received (practice only, to confirm).
Data
Inputs: The request date, the start date, any agreement to extend, the views gathered and from whom, the decision and its recommendations, the list of people to receive a copy; Outputs: A running time limit and any breach; a decision record with its recommendations; a record of each copy given; an action for each recommendation; Validations: An extension needs the agreement of both the review authority and the person who asked; a review cannot be marked complete without a decision; withholding a copy from a child needs the review authority's recorded opinion.
Dependencies
FR-001, FR-061, FR-064, FR-067
Open
The Regulation does not say whether either time limit is counted in calendar or business days.
The Regulation sets no consequence for a missed limit and no limit on how long an agreed extension may run.
The Regulation does not require the director to respond to a recommendation. Tracking each recommendation as an action with a responsible executive director rests on a system user guide alone (CFD-172); the policy that would give the authority is not held.
The Regulation says 'as soon as possible' for starting the review. The requirement records the start date and sets no deadline.
Rationale
The Regulation sets how an administrative review is conducted: when it starts, when it must be complete, whose views are sought, what the review authority must consider, and who receives the decision and by when (CFCS Regulation ss. 17 to 19). The outcome is a recommendation to the director, not a new decision. LEG002-C9

Given a complaint received by an agency, when it is recorded, then the record holds the date received, the person who complained and their type, the type of complaint and the service area, and later the outcome on the same record (RC-IN2-10).

The conflict recorded as CF-D7-24 was checked and is not a conflict.
The ministry's own complaints policy is not held. Complaints made to the ministry are dispositioned practice only, so this requirement is limited to agencies.

The system shows an alert as required where policy makes one mandatory (R-MH2-05), supports ending an alert with a discontinuation note, and brings current alerts to the team leader for review.

Acceptance Criteria
Given a clinician placing a safety alert, when they save it, then it has one type from the registered list (R-MH2-09), the recommended actions, the date and location of related information, and a record that the team leader or clinical supervisor was advised or consulted.
Given an active alert of one type on a record, when a clinician tries to add a second active alert of the same type, then the system refuses and offers the existing alert for update.

Given current alerts on a team's records, when the review interval policy sets comes due (CK-MH2-02), then the team leader receives a work item listing them and the review is recorded.
Edge case: Given an alert is placed, when it is saved, then the system sends no notice to the child, youth or parent; the clinician may record that they chose to tell them, then or later.
Data

The system holds the intake record: the clinical interview recorded on the intake assessment, the standard screening interview or a comparable tool, and narrative and collateral information about the child or youth and their parent, caregiver or guardian. It records each component as done, deferred or contraindicated, with the reason and the consultation with the team leader or clinical supervisor. It lets intake run over more than one session, runs the completion period policy sets, and lets an earlier intake stand in place of a new one within the windows policy sets.

N01, N19, N06

CL-D5-031, CL-D5-032, CL-D5-033, CL-D5-039, CL-D5-042, CL-D5-043, CL-D5-044, CL-D8-238 (8 reconciled provisions and 0 further rows; 30 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given an intake, when a clinician records the screening interview as contraindicated or deferred, then the system requires the reason and the team leader or clinical supervisor consulted (R-MH2-17, AU-MH2-05), and accepts a comparable tool recorded in its place.
Given a child or youth with high-risk concerns who will move directly into active services, when the clinician records a comprehensive mental health assessment in place of the intake assessment, then the system requires the documented rationale (R-MH2-18, RC-MH2-08).
Given an intake in progress, when the period in CK-MH2-04 passes, then the system shows the intake as past the usual period and prompts consultation with the team leader or clinical supervisor. It does not close the intake or block further sessions.
Given a child or youth who returns within the windows in R-MH2-19 and CK-MH2-05, when the clinician records that there are no significant changes or new events, then the system links the request to the earlier intake and requires no new one.
Edge case: in an urgent case, other screening components may be deferred on clinical discretion with the same consultation, and the system shows them as outstanding until completed (AU-MH2-05).
Edge case: intake information gathered by a core member of an integrated child and youth team is accepted as part of the intake record and is not asked for again (R-MH2-13).
Data

Scope
Conditional on DEP-26: whether the replacement covers child and youth mental health work, which is recorded today in its own clinical system.
Open
Policy does not state the event that starts CK-MH2-04. It says intake 'should' be completed in the period and recommends consultation beyond it, so the clock is a service standard with no stated consequence.
Policy does not define 'significant changes or new events'. The clinician's recorded judgement is the test.
CF-D5-10, read in B-1: policy makes the screening interview part of intake unless contraindicated or deferred in consultation. The job aid's 'recommended' (R-MH1-05) is practice tier; policy prevails. CF-D5-11 is settled by hierarchy: the screening interview or a comparable tool.
ICY Policy 1.2 (2021) says all clinical team members use the named screening interview; B-1 (amended later) accepts comparable tools. The requirement holds the tool as data, so it is the same either way.
Screening results are held today in the screening instrument's own service (practice only). Whether this system holds the results or receives them is a design decision that follows the scope decision.
The practice guidelines for the screening interview with Indigenous children, youth and families (CFD-060) are practice tier; B-1 and ICY Policy 1.2 require clinicians to follow them. How the interview is held is clinical practice (CL-D5-034).
Rationale
Policy B-1 names what informs intake screening and the eligibility decision, allows named exceptions with consultation, and sets how long intake should take and when an earlier intake can be relied on. Each exception must leave a record or the eligibility decision cannot be explained later. CFD197-C4
FR-360 Must M9 Medium
Deciding eligibility and the serving office, and who may decide
The system records the eligibility decision for child and youth mental health services as a decision of the clinician overseeing intake, informed by the intake record. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records the eligibility decision for child and youth mental health services as a decision of the clinician overseeing intake, informed by the intake record. Acceptance Criteria
Given a request for a child or youth whose recorded birth date puts them at or over the age limit (CK-MH2-06) and who is not already receiving services, when intake is started, then the system shows that the age criterion is not met.
Given a youth receiving services who reaches the general age limit, when no determination to remain is recorded, then the system raises a work item to record a best-fit determination or a transition or discharge plan. It does not close the file by itself.
Given a determination that a youth remains past the general limit, when it is saved, then the system requires each condition in R-MH2-71 to be recorded: developmental level, the agreement of the treatment team, youth and family as appropriate, and treatment plan goals that prepare for adulthood and transition.
Given a youth in service who reaches the outer limit (CK-MH2-22), when that date arrives, then the system shows the service as past the limit and requires a transition or discharge to be recorded.
Given a youth in the transition years moving to adult mental health and substance use services, when the transition service plan is recorded, then the system holds the written plan, the roles and responsibilities it names, and the participants, who include at least the youth and family, a ministry practitioner and an adult services practitioner (OB-MH2-83).
Edge case: a youth in the age band of R-MH2-70 may be given access to adult services where the conditions in that rule are recorded. The system records the determination and does not treat it as a finding of ineligibility.
Data

Rationale

When an Authorized Position finds that a record has both heightened sensitivity and a reasonable expectation of harm to the person it is about, the system limits access to every electronic part of that record. It records the nature of the restriction, schedules its review and lifts it when it no longer applies.

FR-067, FR-071
Scope
Conditional on DEP-26: whether the replacement covers child and youth mental health work, which is recorded today in its own clinical system.
Open
The Act requires notice to 'a near relative', not to every near relative. A facility may send it to a parent and not to a director who is guardian. The requirement covers the notices the ministry does receive.
The prescribed manner and forms of these notices, and the prescribed times for a hearing, are in the Mental Health Regulation, which is not held.
No ministry source says who acts 'on the patient's behalf' for a child in care or a client of a mental health team (claim of absence in the pack, unchecked).
The Act puts no duty on a near relative to act on a notice. The system records and routes the notice; it sets no deadline for a response.
Rationale
The Act counts the legal guardian of a minor as a near relative and requires the director of the facility to send that person notice of the patient's rights, of discharge and of a hearing request (Mental Health Act ss. 1 and 34.2). A guardian who cannot find the notice cannot use the rights it sets out for the child: a review panel hearing, a second medical opinion and an application to the court (ss. 25(1), 31(2), 33(2)). Given a person who believes they should be receiving team services, or an advocate acting for a child, youth or family, when they complain, then the system accepts the complaint without an open service record (R-QA1-02).

Given a resolved direct complaint, when it is closed, then the system requires a record that the person was told the resolution and any further steps open to them (OB-QA1-05).
Edge case: Given a person who wants a formal complaint, when the team member redirects them to the employer organisation's process, then the system records the redirection and its reason and closes its own record (OB-QA1-06).
Data
Inputs: The complainant and any advocate; the matter; the team member or service concerned; consent to share; Outputs: A complaint record with its escalations, resolution, notification and any redirection; Validations: A complaint cannot close without a resolution notice or a redirection.

Open

Rationale
