FR-401 Should M9 Low
Brief services recorded without opening a case, with written or verbal consent
The system records brief services given by an integrated team member to a child, youth or family without opening a case and without an intake or formal assessment. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE (depends on the scope decision; practice material says ministry clinicians do not give brief services)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records brief services given by an integrated team member to a child, youth or family without opening a case and without an intake or formal assessment. The record holds the referral, notes on what was provided and progress, and the consent. Consent may be written or verbal. Where it is verbal, the record states why written consent was not obtained. The record is marked as brief services so it can be told apart from an open case.
Relates To
BR-025
Service lines
Child and youth mental health
Parameters
N01, N21, N12
Authority
Integrated Child and Youth Team Policies, Policy 2.1 Brief Services, version 2 (CFD-010) (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D5-188 (1 reconciled provisions and 0 further rows; 3 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a team member gives brief services, when they record it, then the system creates a referral record marked as brief services and does not require an intake, an assessment or an open case (OB-IC1-37).
Given a brief services record, when it is saved, then it holds either the written consent or a note of verbal consent with the reason written consent was not obtained (R-IC1-22, RC-IC1-09).
Given a brief services record with no consent recorded, when the team member tries to complete it, then the system asks for the consent or the reason and keeps the record flagged as incomplete.
Edge case: brief services lead to an open case or an integrated care plan. The system links the brief services record to the new case and requires the intake and assessment that an open case needs (CL-D5-173).
Data
Inputs: Referral details; service and progress notes; written consent document, or a note of verbal consent with the reason; Outputs: Brief services record marked as such; consent record; link to any later open case; Validations: Consent or a verbal consent note is present; verbal consent carries a reason.
Dependencies
FR-075, FR-071, FR-070
Scope
Conditional on DEP-27: whether the replacement holds or exchanges with the Integrated Child and Youth teams' shared record.
Open
The ministry's frequently asked questions say ministry mental health clinicians will not offer brief services under this policy (CFD-175 L259, practice material). If so, the duty falls on other employers' team members, and this requirement applies only if the shared team file is in scope.
Policy 3.1 (CFD-016 L45) still speaks of an operational reporting form for these contacts; version 2 of Policy 2.1 removed that form.
Rationale
Policy 2.1 requires team members to document brief services and the consent for them, so that these contacts are tracked and counted. Consent must be given before personal information is collected. CFD010-C1
FR-402 Must M0 Medium
The child's own team: supplemental members the child chooses, and what each may see
The system records the team for each child or youth: Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system records the team for each child or youth: the core members serving the child and any supplemental members the child or youth identifies and consents to include. For each supplemental member it records the consent, the date, and what information may be shared with that person. A supplemental member stays on the child's team only while the child receives integrated team services. The system keeps consent to share information apart from consent to receive a service, and records that taking part in an integrated care plan is voluntary.

Acceptance Criteria
Given a child or youth names a person to join their team, when the person is added as a supplemental member, then the system requires a recorded consent from the child or youth and gives that member access only to what the consent covers (R-IC1-30).
Given a supplemental member is added after intake, when the consent is updated, then the record shows the date and the information sharing allowed with that member (practice only, to confirm) (RC-IC1-23).
Given a child's team case closes, when closure is recorded, then every supplemental member's access to the child's team file ends (R-IC1-30).
Given a consent to share information within the team, when a service from a team member is to start, then the system does not treat that consent as consent to the service (practice only, to confirm) (R-IC1-58).
Edge case: a youth does not consent to their family taking part in care planning. The system records the youth's decision and does not add the family to the plan or share it with them (R-IC1-29).

Dependencies
FR-075, FR-077, FR-080, FR-083
Scope
Conditional on DEP-27: whether the replacement holds or exchanges with the Integrated Child and Youth teams' shared record.
Open
A supplemental member is a participant who is neither staff nor client and may work for no partner organisation (a caring adult, an Elder). How such a person is identified and given access is not stated in any source held.
The rule that consent to share is not consent to service, and the way a supplemental member is added to a consent, are stated only on the form and its guide (CFD-180, CFD-173).
Rationale
Policy 1.4 makes services voluntary and requires informed consent both to receive services and for information to be shared. Policy 2.3 lets the child or youth decide who else joins their team. Access by a person outside the core team must therefore follow a consent the child or youth gave for that person. CFD013-C2
FR-403 Must M9 Medium
Closing an integrated team case: closing record, closure summary and sharing it
The system treats a child's integrated team case as closed only when no team member is serving the child. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system treats a child's integrated team case as closed only when no team member is serving the child. Before the team file is closed it requires the closing record policy lists, with the Program Leader's oversight recorded. It times the closure summary from the agreed closure or the last contact attempt. It records who received the summary and the consent for each, and that the family was told how to start services again. It holds a copy of each member's closure documentation made under that member's employer's policy.

BR-025

Child and youth mental health

N19, N08, N21
Authority
Integrated Child and Youth Team Policies, Policy 3.5 Transitions and Case Closure, policy statement and Case Closure and Monitoring and Evaluation procedures (CFD-019) (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D5-189, CL-D5-190, CL-D5-191, CL-D8-248, CK-IC1-12, R-IC1-41 (4 reconciled provisions and 2 further rows; 10 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a child still served by at least one team member, when someone tries to close the team case, then the system refuses (R-IC1-39).
Given a team file is to be closed, when the most responsible team member completes the closing record, then it holds the reasons for closure as stated by the child, the family or the team, any diagnoses and the clinical status, a summary of care and progress with follow-up arrangements, and a transition plan where further services are needed (OB-IC1-70, RC-IC1-19).
Given an agreed closure or a last contact attempt, when that date is recorded, then the system sets the closure summary due within the time limit policy sets (CK-IC1-10) and shows it as overdue if the summary is not on file by then.
Given a closure summary, when it is shared, then the system records each recipient and releases it to a recipient only where consent covers that recipient (OB-IC1-71).
Edge case: the child or family ends services before any planning meeting. The system accepts the closure, records that they ended it and that no pre-closure meeting was held (R-IC1-41).
Edge case: contact after closure for program evaluation. The system allows it only where consent was recorded before services ended. The period the consent form states (CK-IC1-12) is practice only, to confirm.
Data
Inputs: Date of agreed closure or last contact attempt; reasons for closure and who stated them; diagnoses and clinical status; summary of care; transition plan; each employer's closure documentation; consents to share and to later contact; Outputs: Closing record; closure summary with its due date; list of recipients; record that re-start information was given; closed team case; Validations: No active team member remains; closing record complete; each recipient of the summary is covered by a consent in force.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-067, FR-075, FR-077, FR-004
Scope
Conditional on DEP-27: whether the replacement holds or exchanges with the Integrated Child and Youth teams' shared record.
Open
Policy does not say whether the closure summary time limit counts calendar or working days.
A ministry clinician's own file closes under the ministry's transition and discharge policy, which sets its own time limit (CL-D5-114). One child can therefore carry two closure time limits; no source says how they relate.
Policy says the Program Leader oversees the closing record. It does not say the Program Leader approves closure, so the system records oversight and does not block closure for want of approval.
Rationale
Policy 3.5 defines when a team case is closed, lists what the closing record must hold, sets a time limit for the closure summary, and makes sharing it depend on consent. A child or family may end services at any time, so the system must accept a closure the team did not plan. CFD019-C1
FR-404 Must M9 Medium
Loss of contact: attempts to re-engage, closure for no contact, and return to service
The system records each attempt to re-engage a child, youth or family who stops taking part without asking for closure. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records each attempt to re-engage a child, youth or family who stops taking part without asking for closure. It runs a time limit from the last contact with the team. When the limit is reached the team file is closed and the system issues notice of the closure. The Program Leader may approve a longer period, and the system records that approval. When a child or family returns after inactivity or closure, the system brings forward what is already held so that it is not collected again.

Acceptance Criteria
Given a child or family stops taking part without asking for closure, when the most responsible team member tries to reach them, then each attempt is recorded with its date, method and result, and the file is marked as monitored for closure (OB-IC1-72, RC-IC1-20).
Given no contact with the team for the period policy sets (CK-IC1-11), when the period ends, then the system raises closure of the team file and issues notice to the child or youth and their family, caregiver or guardian.
Given the Program Leader approves a longer period, when the approval is recorded, then the time limit runs to the extended limit policy allows (AU-IC1-14) and no person other than the Program Leader can record that approval.

Scope
Conditional on DEP-27: whether the replacement holds or exchanges with the Integrated Child and Youth teams' shared record.

Policy reads as closing the file when the period ends. It does not say whether closure is automatic or a team member's act. The requirement raises the closure for a person to complete.
Practice material says a file need not be held open for the full period where closure is agreed (CFD-175 L342). That is consistent with policy and is covered by FR-403.
'Indigenous community representative' is the policy's term and is not defined. It is not the same as a designated representative or an Indigenous governing body.
The ministry clinician's own file follows a different closure time limit under the ministry's transition and discharge policy (CL-D5-114).

Policy 3.5 sets a period of no contact after which the team file is closed, lets the Program Leader extend it, requires notice of the closure, and requires that return to service does not repeat assessment and information collection. FR-405 Should M9 Medium
Complaints and compliments about integrated team services, and where each one goes
The system records a complaint or compliment that a child, youth, family, caregiver or guardian gives directly to an integrated team member, and what was done with it. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE (policy sets the process; it does not prescribe a record)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records a complaint or compliment that a child, youth, family, caregiver or guardian gives directly to an integrated team member, and what was done with it. It records which route the complaint took: answered directly, passed to the Program Leader, or redirected to the formal process of the team member's employer. BR-025
Service lines
Child and youth mental health
Parameters
N20, N21, N02
Authority
Integrated Child and Youth Team Policies, Practice Guide 4.3 Compliments and Complaints (CFD-022); Policy 1.4 Rights of Children, Youth and Families and Informed Consent (CFD-005) (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D8-154, CL-D8-155, CL-D8-156, OB-QA1-02, OB-QA1-04, OB-QA1-07, OB-QA1-08, R-QA1-04 (3 reconciled provisions and 5 further rows; 14 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a team member receives a complaint directly, when they record it, then the record shows whether it was answered directly and that the person was offered the option of a formal complaint to the employer organization (OB-QA1-02).
Given a complaint about another team member that the person does not want to raise with that member or the employer, or a complaint or compliment about the team as a whole, when it is recorded, then the system routes it to the Program Leader (OB-QA1-03, AU-QA1-17).
Given a response needs the Program Leader, an employer supervisor or another party, when the complaint is escalated, then the record shows the person was told the steps and what personal information is shared with whom, and sharing beyond the supervisory arrangement needs a recorded consent (OB-QA1-04).
Given a complaint is resolved, when the resolution is recorded, then the system records that the person was told the outcome, any changes to be made, and what further steps they can take.
Edge case: a formal complaint against a team member. The system records only that the person was directed to the employer's process and, where the employer reports it, that a resolution was reached. It does not hold the employer's investigation (R-QA1-03, OB-QA1-07).
Edge case: recording a complaint changes nothing in the person's service. No closure, pause or change of priority follows from it (R-QA1-01).
Edge case: the Program Leader takes complaint information to a team meeting or a local governance table. The extract carries no name of the child, family or team member (R-QA1-04).
Data

Scope
Conditional on DEP-27: whether the replacement holds or exchanges with the Integrated Child and Youth teams' shared record.
See also
FR-392 (rests on some of the same provisions).
Open
Where the team member is a ministry employee, the employer's formal process is the ministry's own complaints process. Whether the direct complaint record and the ministry's formal complaint record are one record or two is not stated.
The policy sets no time limit for answering a direct complaint or telling the person the resolution.
The duty to tell the person the resolution (CFD-022 L67) has no register row.
Rationale
Practice Guide 4.3 gives a complaint three routes, makes the employer responsible for a formal complaint against a team member, and requires that the person is told the steps, what is shared and the resolution. Without a record the team cannot show the complaint was answered or that the person was told. CFD022-C2

FR-406 Must M0 Medium
One youth justice record per youth, opened only within the age the Act sets
The system opens a youth justice record only for a person who had reached the age the Act sets at the time of the alleged offence (R-LG3-51, R-LG3-52). Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system opens a youth justice record only for a person who had reached the age the Act sets at the time of the alleged offence (R-LG3-51, R-LG3-52). Before it opens a record, on a new order or on admission to custody, it searches for an earlier record of the same youth and reactivates that record instead of creating a second. It holds the status of the record (active, pending, inactive) and changes it only on the events policy names (R-YJ5-06). The record stays open when the young person becomes an adult while proceedings or a sentence continue.

Parameters
N01, N04, N12
Authority
Youth Justice Act ss. 1, 2 and 3; Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Chapter 1 preamble and Chapter 2 (File Documentation, Standards, and Management) policy statements 9, 10, 16 and 17 and the community file standards procedure (tier 1)
Provisions
CL-D3-092, CL-D4-001, CL-D4-021, CL-D4-022, CL-D4-026, R-LG3-53, RC-YJ5-06 (5 reconciled provisions and 2 further rows; 16 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a referral about a person who was below the age the Act sets (R-LG3-52) at the time of the alleged conduct, when a worker tries to open a youth justice record, then the system refuses and records that the referral was not accepted (OB-YJ5-01).
Given a youth admitted to custody or made subject to a new order requiring supervision, when a record is to be opened, then the system searches for an earlier record and, where one exists, reactivates it and makes its relevant content available on the active record.
Given a youth released from custody to supervision in the community before the final expiry date of the warrant, when the release is recorded, then the record becomes pending and cannot be made inactive or sent for archiving before that date (R-YJ5-06).
Given a record whose final warrant expiry date is reached, or a youth who has died, when the event is recorded, then the record becomes inactive.
Edge case: given a young person who becomes an adult during proceedings or a sentence, when that birthday passes, then the record stays open and youth justice services continue (R-LG3-53).
Data
Inputs: Date of birth, date of the alleged offence, orders and warrants, admission and release events; Outputs: One record per youth with a dated status history; a refused-referral entry; Validations: Age at the offence is tested against the registered thresholds; a duplicate record for the same youth is refused.
Dependencies
FR-028, FR-091, DR-004
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
See also
FR-450 (rests on some of the same provisions).
Open
The upper limit of service after a young person becomes an adult is stated in the service framework without its conditions (R-YJ6-01, CK-YJ6-01, both not current); the conditions sit in the custody rows of another pack and in the federal Act, which is not held.
Policy states the pending and inactive statuses for the custody file only; whether the community file follows the same statuses is not stated.
Scope condition YJ: the requirement stands only if youth justice is in scope.
Rationale
The Act gives no jurisdiction over a person below the age it sets, and policy forbids accepting such a referral. Policy requires a search for an earlier file on every admission and reopening of an inactive file on a new order, so that all relevant material is in front of staff. LEG007-C1
FR-407 Must M9 Medium
The running record of work with a youth: entries, attachments and removal
The system keeps a running record of work with each youth: Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system keeps a running record of work with each youth: information gathered, changes in circumstances, communications, consultations, the rationale for decisions and supervisor approvals. FR-419 Must M0 Medium
Opening community supervision: officer assignment, order record and initial interview
The system opens community supervision when an order of the youth justice court, an extrajudicial sanctions agreement or a release order with a condition to report is recorded, or when a youth with no prior involvement is admitted to custody. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (conditional on the youth justice scope decision)
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system opens community supervision when an order of the youth justice court, an extrajudicial sanctions agreement or a release order with a condition to report is recorded, or when a youth with no prior involvement is admitted to custody. It asks the youth justice team leader to assign a youth probation officer, times the initial interview by the type of order, and holds the record of that interview. It times the completion and the closing of the order record. Supervision ends when the youth is not in custody and every order or agreement with a reporting condition has expired.

Acceptance Criteria
Given an order or agreement with a reporting condition is recorded, when no youth probation officer is assigned, then the system raises an assignment item for the team leader due within the time limit policy sets (CK-YJ5-24), and proposes the officer already assigned to the youth's active order.
Edge case: given the youth has, or is alleged to have, committed a sexual offence, when the team leader selects an officer without the delegation and training policy requires (OB-YJ5-53), then the assignment is refused.
Given the assigned officer starts leave that is indeterminate or at least as long as policy sets (CK-YJ5-44), when the leave is recorded, then the system asks the team leader to reassign the youth at once and records the reassignment.

Edge case: given an order with no reporting condition, when the officer records that the court intended this, then the order is held as its own record without opening supervision, notified changes of address, employment or schooling are recorded on it, and it becomes eligible for destruction at the time policy sets (CK-YJ5-42).
Edge case: given an appeal of conviction or sentence is recorded, when no stay of the sentence is recorded, then the order stays in force and every time limit keeps running.

FR-420 Must M9 Medium
Structured risk assessment and the supervision level it sets
The system records the structured risk assessment a youth probation officer completes for a supervised youth. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (conditional on the youth justice scope decision)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records the structured risk assessment a youth probation officer completes for a supervised youth. It works out from the order type and length whether an assessment is required, times the first assessment and each update, and holds the rating for violent and for non-violent offending with the rationale for each domain. It derives the supervision level from the higher of the two ratings.

FR-421 Must M9 Medium
Contact standards by supervision level, and the record of contacts and home visits

First needed in: M9
Description
The system holds the minimum contacts policy sets for each supervision level as rule data, with the modes of contact that count toward them. FR-426 Must M9 Medium
Violations of supervised orders: classification, consultation, report to Crown Counsel and record
The system records every alleged violation of, or failure to comply with, a release order, a recognizance order or a community sentence that requires supervision, against the order and the condition concerned. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records every alleged violation of, or failure to comply with, a release order, a recognizance order or a community sentence that requires supervision, against the order and the condition concerned. It records which route the youth probation officer took: the minor violation route, with the consultation with the youth justice team leader and the restored or alternate plan, or a report to Crown Counsel for an apparent wilful failure to comply. It holds the reasons for reporting or not reporting, and any change to the manner or intensity of supervision. It runs the time limit policy sets for making the record (CK-YJ4-45, CK-YJ4-46), counted from the day the officer became aware.
Relates To
BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice
Parameters
N01, N08, N19
Authority
Youth Justice Act s. 10 and s. 17; Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Reviews, Variations and Enforcement policy, policy statements 5 to 8 and the enforcement procedures for release orders, recognizances and community sentences (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D4-125, CL-D4-126, CL-D4-127, AU-LG3-26, R-LG3-65, R-YJ4-37 (3 reconciled provisions and 3 further rows; 13 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given an alleged violation of a supervised order, when the youth probation officer records it, then the system holds the order and condition concerned, the date the officer became aware, the route taken and the rationale, and starts the recording time limit (CK-YJ4-45 or CK-YJ4-46).
Given a violation recorded on the minor route (R-YJ4-25), when the record is completed, then it holds the consultation with the youth justice team leader, the restored or alternate plan, and that the violation was discussed with the youth, the parent or guardian and any other caregiver.
Given an apparent wilful failure to comply, when the record is completed, then it holds the circumstances and nature of the violation, the reasons for reporting or not reporting it to Crown Counsel, and any change in supervision. Where a report was made, the record links the report and the copy of the order sent with it.
Given a victim's report of a violation of a protective condition, when the officer records it, then the system holds either the consultation with the youth justice team leader on why Crown Counsel need not be notified, or the notifications made to the police and Crown Counsel.
Edge case: given an alleged breach of a community sentence, when the officer decides between a sentence review and a report recommending a charge (R-YJ4-37), then the system records the matters policy requires the officer to consider and the option chosen.
Data
Inputs: The order and its conditions; the alleged violation; the date the officer became aware; consultation with the team leader; notifications made; Outputs: A violation record with route, rationale and supervision changes; a work item with the recording time limit; a link to any report to Crown Counsel; Validations: A violation record cannot be completed without a route and a rationale; the minor route requires a recorded consultation unless a documented plan for the non-compliance already exists (OB-YJ4-51).
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-032, FR-061, FR-067, FR-070
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
Policy says the report to Crown Counsel is submitted through the prosecution service's own system. Whether the replacement sends the report, or only records that it was sent, depends on the youth justice scope decision and on that interface.
Policy sets no time limit for the report itself: 'in a timely manner', and 'as soon as possible' where the youth poses a substantial risk to the public (CFD-308 L3328). The system must not invent one.
The recording time limit runs from the officer becoming aware (CK-YJ4-45, CK-YJ4-46); the general recording rule in another chapter runs from the date of occurrence. The source check found this is not a conflict (CF-D4-05).
For a conditional discharge or probation order under the provincial Act, 'wilful' is not part of the test (CFD-308 L3336). Whether such a violation is recorded on the same two routes is not stated.
Rationale
Policy requires the youth probation officer to document each violation and breach, with the reasons for reporting or not reporting it to Crown Counsel, within a set time of becoming aware (CFD-308, policy statements 6 to 8). The decision not to report is as much a decision as the report, and the record is the only evidence of it. CFD308-C17
FR-427 Must M0 High
Suspension of supervision in the community or conditional supervision, and the provincial director's review
The system records a violation or potential violation of supervision in the community or of conditional supervision, the consultation with the youth justice team leader, and the decision to apply or not to apply for a warrant of suspension. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system records a violation or potential violation of supervision in the community or of conditional supervision, the consultation with the youth justice team leader, and the decision to apply or not to apply for a warrant of suspension. It routes an application to a person delegated to issue the warrant, records the decision with reasons, and holds the warrant's life: issue, notices sent, arrest date, place held and execution. From detention it runs the time limit for the provincial director's review (CK-YJ1-35), routes the review to a delegated authority for decision, and records the outcome and the copies and notices that follow. It holds the dates that sentence calculation needs after a suspension.

BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice
Parameters
N08, N17, N19
Authority
Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Reviews, Variations and Enforcement policy, policy statements 9 and 10 and the enforcement of custody sentence procedure; Youth Custody Services, Admissions 3.13; Sentence Calculation 5.05 and 5.11. The policy cites Youth Criminal Justice Act ss. 102 to 109, which is federal and not held. (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D4-123, CL-D4-128, CL-D4-129, CL-D4-130, CL-D4-131, CL-D4-132, R-YJ4-23, R-YJ4-24 (6 reconciled provisions and 2 further rows; 28 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a violation of supervision in the community, when the youth probation officer decides not to apply for a warrant of suspension, then the system requires the content policy lists (RC-YJ4-26) within the time limit policy sets (CK-YJ4-47), including the result of the consultation with the youth justice team leader.
Given an application for a warrant of suspension, when it is submitted, then the system routes it to a person delegated to issue the warrant (AU-YJ4-13) and refuses a decision by the applicant. An approval records the notices sent and starts the time limit for the administrative hold (CK-YJ4-48). A refusal records the reasons given to the officer and the police.
Given a youth detained on a warrant of suspension, when the arrest date and place held are recorded, then the system starts the review time limit (CK-YJ1-35), and the review is complete only when a delegated authority (AU-YJ4-15) records the decision to cancel the suspension or refer the case to the youth justice court.
Given a completed review, when the decision is recorded, then the system lists the copies and notices policy requires for that outcome and records each as sent, including notice of the court date to the youth and the parent or guardian where the case is referred.
Edge case: given a team leader review instead of a suspension (CFD-308 L3355), when the team leader adds or deletes optional conditions or reissues the order, then the system records the varied conditions and the notice to the originating police agency.
Data
Inputs: The order; the violation; the warrant application and decision; warrant issue date, arrest date, place held, level of custody on remand, days held in police cells, release date; the review and its decision; Outputs: Decision records for the application and the review; clocks for the hold and the review; community days owing worked out by the rule policy sets (R-YJ3-29); the report for a court review; Validations: Applicant, issuer and reviewer hold the delegation recorded for that act on the date; the level of custody on remand follows R-YJ4-23 and R-YJ4-24; days owing cannot be worked out without the warrant issue date and the arrest date.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-061, FR-064, FR-067, FR-094
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
See also
FR-452, FR-454 (rests on some of the same provisions).
Open
The review time limit is stated in the admissions chapter (CFD-308 L6177), which starts it at the suspension. The enforcement chapter only implies it and speaks of detention (L3415). The start event needs a ministry ruling.
The enforcement chapter gives no consequence for a missed review limit. It says only that, where a weekend detention prevents a review in time, the on-call manager of the nearest centre is told (CFD-308 L3415).
The delegation tables that confirm who may apply, issue and review are attachments that are not held. The policy text delegates the issue of warrants to directors of one named custody centre.
The time limit for recording a decision not to apply (CK-YJ4-47) has no stated start event.
Notice of a court review of a suspension: the policy's footnote says the federal Act requires clear days' written notice and that hearings often occur sooner, so the court may dispense with notice (CFD-308 L3465, CK-YJ4-51). The system must record a dispensation and notice by telephone.
The sentence calculation pack (P36) holds the recording of apprehension and custody dates (CL-D3-107). The days owing rule (R-YJ3-29) is placed here because no other pack holds it; the editor may wish to move the calculation to P36.
Rationale
A suspension returns a youth to custody on an administrative decision. Policy separates who applies, who issues the warrant and who signs off the review, sets a time limit for the review, and requires the dates to be recorded accurately because release dates are calculated from them (CFD-308 L3392, L3412, L6177, L3479). FR-428 Must M9 High
Sentence and custody reviews: key dates, eligibility, applications, notice and outcome
The system works out, from the sentence date and the kind and length of sentence, the date of a mandatory court review of custody and the earliest date an optional review or a review under the provincial Act may be sought without leave of the court. Show detail
First needed in: M9
Description
The system works out, from the sentence date and the kind and length of sentence, the date of a mandatory court review of custody and the earliest date an optional review or a review under the provincial Act may be sought without leave of the court. It brings the file forward so that preparation for a mandatory review starts by the lead time policy sets (CK-YJ4-37). It records every application for review, who made it, whether leave is needed, the forwarding of a youth's own application within the time limit (CK-YJ4-43), the notices given and received, the progress report, and the court's outcome.

BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice
Parameters
N04, N09, N19, N20
Authority
Youth Justice Act ss. 9, 15 and 16(4); Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Reviews, Variations and Enforcement policy, policy statement 4 and the review of custody sentence procedure. The policy cites Youth Criminal Justice Act s. 94 and Young Offenders Act s. 28, which are federal and not held. (tier 1)
Provisions
CL-D4-120, CL-D4-121, CL-D4-122, CL-D4-123, CL-D4-124, CK-LG3-20, OB-LG3-44, R-LG3-63, R-LG3-64, R-LG3-69, R-LG3-72, R-LG3-75, RC-LG3-15, RC-LG3-16 (5 reconciled provisions and 9 further rows; 33 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a custody sentence long enough to need a mandatory court review (R-YJ4-30), when it is recorded or recalculated, then the system sets the review date, restarts it from any later review hearing, and opens preparation work by the lead time in CK-YJ4-37, including telling the youth of the right and the date.
Given a sentence, when a user asks whether a review may be sought, then the system shows the earliest date without leave (R-YJ4-31, R-LG3-70), counting a prior review as a sentence, and marks an earlier application as needing leave of the court (R-YJ4-32).
Given a youth in custody who states an intent to seek a review, when staff record it, then the system starts the forwarding time limit once the youth completes the form (CK-YJ4-43), keeps a copy on the youth's record, and does not allow the application to be closed on the ground that staff disagree (R-YJ4-34).
Given a review hearing date, when the provincial director is the applicant, then the system prompts written notice to the youth, the parent and Crown Counsel by the registered limit for that kind of review (CK-YJ4-38, CK-YJ4-36), with method and proof of service. Notice received from another applicant is recorded with its date (RC-LG3-15).
Edge case: given a community service or probation order under the provincial Act made while the young person is serving continuous custody, when it is recorded, then its effective date is the date custody expires (R-LG3-64). A sentence registered from a reciprocating province is reviewed as if made in the Provincial Court (R-LG3-75).
Data
Inputs: Sentence date, kind, length and effective date; earlier review hearings; the application, the applicant and any request for leave; hearing date; notices; the court's requirement for a progress report; Outputs: Mandatory review date and bring-forward work item; earliest optional review date; notice records with proof of service; the outcome of the review (confirmed, rescinded, varied or a new sentence) and the changed order; Validations: Review dates are recomputed whenever the sentence is recalculated or a review is heard; each notice period is a registered clock with its own unit; the applicant is one the governing Act permits.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-064, FR-067, FR-092
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
Notice periods for like hearings are stated four ways: days, business days, clear days, and the provincial Act's days with no unit (CF-D4-12, settled by hierarchy). Each is a separate clock in the register; the units of CK-YJ4-38 and CK-LG3-23 are unstated.
The mandatory and optional custody review rules come from the federal Acts as the policy restates them. The federal Acts are not held, so the tier is T2 for those rules and T1 only for reviews under the provincial Act.
The policy sentence that sets the custody youth probation officer's duty to give notice is missing its object (CFD-308 L3284). Read with L3285 it is notice of the review application; to confirm.
Youth Justice Act s. 15(10) bars review of a sentence under appeal. No policy held carries this, and the system has no stated source for knowing an appeal is outstanding.
No policy held implements Youth Justice Act s. 9(2) or s. 16. The edge case criterion rests on the statute alone.
The progress report for a review hearing, and its time limit, are held by pack P31 (CL-D4-054). This requirement only opens the work when a review is set or the court requires a report.
Rationale
A youth has a legal right to apply for review, and the provincial director must bring a youth before the court for a mandatory review at a time fixed by law (Youth Justice Act s. 15; CFD-308 L3236, L3259). Policy requires a system of key dates and bring-forward so that the review is not missed (CFD-308 L3242). LEG007-C5
FR-429 Should M9 Low
Variation and renewal of release orders, recognizances and protective orders
The system records the youth probation officer's assessment of whether the conditions of a release order should be varied, the ground relied on, and what was done: Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE (the lead time is stated as 'should'; the assessment duty is mandatory)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records the youth probation officer's assessment of whether the conditions of a release order should be varied, the ground relied on, and what was done: a report to Crown Counsel seeking variation, help given to the youth to apply, or advice that the youth may apply without the officer's support. For a recognizance order and for a protective intervention or restraining order under the child protection statute, it brings the order forward before expiry by the lead time policy sets (CK-YJ4-35) so that renewal can be raised with Crown Counsel or with the social worker. It records who may apply to vary each kind of order.

Acceptance Criteria
Given a release order under supervision, when the youth probation officer records an assessment that conditions should be varied, then the system holds the ground (R-YJ4-26) and the action taken, and links any report to Crown Counsel.

Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
The lead time is a floor ('at least') on a discretionary step ('should be discussed'). The system prompts; it does not record a breach.
For a protective order the social worker, not the youth probation officer, is the usual applicant. Whether the prompt also goes to the social worker's own work queue is a design question that spans child protection and youth justice.

Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
The service planning chapter allows a referral to intensive support and supervision for a youth on a recognizance (CFD-308 L2124); the programs chapter limits the service to youth with a court order for it (L3656). The limit on the length of a stay is implied by an exception and not stated as a limit (CK-YJ4-55). No clock is registered for it until the ministry confirms one.
The effective date of the programs chapter differs between its header and its table of changes (MQ-062).
Notice of an unauthorized absence is the program operator's and the liaison probation officer's arrangement. Whether operators record absences directly or the ministry records what they report is not decided.

Description

Acceptance Criteria
Given a court file where a person was harmed, when the youth probation officer has not recorded a suitability decision and rationale, then the file shows the assessment as outstanding.

FR-442 Must M0 High
Placement in or transfer to adult custody: applications, decisions and the transfer record
The system records where a youth held on a remand order or a youth sentence is placed, and the basis for it. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system records where a youth held on a remand order or a youth sentence is placed, and the basis for it. It tracks the ages at which policy calls for a placement decision, and for each application to the youth justice court to place or transfer a youth in an adult correctional centre it records who may submit it, the consultations held first, the court's authorisation and the placement direction issued. CL-D3-037, CL-D3-038, CL-D3-045, CK-YJ1-12, CK-YJ1-13, CK-YJ1-14, CK-YJ1-15, CK-YJ1-16, CK-YJ1-17, R-YJ1-29, R-YJ1-30, R-YJ1-31, R-YJ1-33 (3 reconciled provisions and 10 further rows; 20 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a record of an outcome the Act lists, when its start event is recorded, then the system sets the non-disclosure date from the period for that outcome (R-YJ5-31, CK-YJ5-43, CK-YJ1-12 to CK-YJ1-17) and records the rule version used.
Given an outcome whose period runs from the finding of guilt, when the date is worked out, then the system uses the recorded date of the finding of guilt and never the date of sentence, and holds the calculation open until that date is recorded (R-YJ1-34).
Given a youth with a record still in its period who is sentenced again, when the later sentence is recorded, then the system recalculates both records to the latest date the rule gives (R-YJ1-29) and keeps the earlier calculation as history.
Edge case: a prohibition order is never counted when a period is worked out (R-YJ1-31). A release order that lapsed with no charge gives no period of access at all (R-YJ1-33).
Edge case: given a record past its non-disclosure date, when the youth or their counsel asks for access, then access is allowed (R-YJ1-32); for anyone else it is refused.
Data

Dependencies
FR-061, FR-090, FR-080
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
The start event for an extrajudicial sanction record is worded as the youth's consent in the Act (s. 119(2)(a)) and in the sanctions chapter of the manual, and as the date the youth signs the agreement in the records chapter. The Act governs; the ministry should confirm the two dates are the same event.
The manual's gloss on the conditional discharge period (CK-YJ1-15) is unclear about a later finding of guilt. The Act sets no clean period for it.
The Act also sets periods for acquittal, dismissal, withdrawal and stay (s. 119(2)(b) to (d)). The manual points to a reference guide for these, which is not held.
On an adult conviction while a youth record is still in its period, the manual says the record is treated as an adult record and these rules stop applying (R-YJ1-30). How the ministry learns of the conviction is not stated.
Rationale
Section 119(2) of the Youth Criminal Justice Act fixes how long each kind of record may be disclosed, and disclosing outside that period is an offence. Policy makes the youth probation officer calculate and recalculate the date for every record and explain it to the youth and their parents. CFD308-C36

Given a request for a copy of all or part of a file, when no written request is on the record, then the system does not record the copy as released (RC-YJ1-16).
Given a release of copies, when it is prepared, then the system applies the kinds of information policy says must be removed (OB-YJ1-40), and removes records past their non-disclosure date unless the requester is the youth or their counsel.
Given anything withheld or severed, when the release is issued, then a written notice states the reason for each and where the information may be obtained (RC-YJ1-17), and that a court application for access is open to the requester.
Given a proposal to disclose to members of the public, when it is recorded, then the system records the consultations policy requires, the application and the court's decision (RC-YJ1-18), and allows no public disclosure without a recorded court order (R-YJ1-49).
Data
Inputs: Request, requester and their authority, written request document, vetting decisions, consultations, court order; Outputs: Routed work item, released copy with severing reasons, written notice to the requester, application record with outcome; Validations: A written request is required for copies; each withheld item carries a reason; a public disclosure needs a court order naming the persons and the information.

Given an infraction a youth correctional officer could not resolve, when the officer submits an incident report, then the system requires the alleged infraction, the circumstances and any action already taken, and routes the report to a senior youth supervisor.
Given an incident report, when the senior youth supervisor orders a consequence or recommends denial or revocation of leave, then the system requires a record that the youth was heard, the reasons, and that the youth was told of the right to complain, and sends the report to a youth custody director.
Given a decision the affected youth asks to have reviewed, when the request is recorded, then the system opens a review due within CK-YJ3-26, refuses the decision-maker as reviewer, and records the outcome: confirmed, or varied or reversed in whole or in part.
Given a completed review, when the reviewer records the written decision, then the system sends it to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice and to the youth.
Edge case: a consequence is recorded against one named youth for that youth's own infraction; the system does not accept a consequence ordered against a group. A consequence may later be reduced or suspended by a senior youth supervisor or a youth custody director, and the change is recorded.
Data
Inputs: Incident report; record of the youth being heard; finding; consequence or recommendation; reasons; review request; reviewer; review outcome; any damage assessment (guideline in R-YJ3-62); Outputs: Decision record with reasons; review record and written decision; notice to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice and the youth; a damage assessment that stays on the youth's record across release and re-admission; Validations: Reasons are required before a consequence or recommendation is saved. The reviewer differs from the decision-maker. A review the youth requests cannot be declined.
Dependencies
FR-001, FR-002, FR-004, FR-061, FR-067
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
The Youth Custody Regulation is not held. The list of infractions (s. 10) and of consequences (s. 12(1)) must come from the regulation before the record's code lists are set.
Policy says the person in charge conducts the review, then speaks of 'the SYS conducting the review'. Who may review a decision made by a senior youth supervisor, and whether the youth custody director's review of every report (C 9 c) is the same review, is not stated.
The review time limit runs from the decision, not from the youth's request. Policy does not say what happens when a youth asks for a review after the limit has passed.
Policy says the reviewer may also review at their own discretion. The system must allow a review with no request from the youth.
The monetary compensation guideline (R-YJ3-62) carries a damage assessment across release and re-admission and limits payment to money earned in centre programs. No source held says how the amount is collected or accounted for.
Rationale
The regulation, as policy quotes it, requires a written report, reasons for a consequence and a review by a different person when the youth asks. Policy sets the time limit for the review and requires a written decision to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice and the youth. CFD308-C50

It raises the notice to the youth's community probation officer and records that the notice was given.

Acceptance Criteria
Given any use of physical restraint or a mechanical restraint device, when the reporting staff member submits the written report, then it holds each item policy lists (the steps taken to de-escalate, the reason, the restraint or device used, how long it was used, the consequences including any harm, the names of everyone involved or witnessing, the contact made and by whom, the date, time, place, name and signature of the reporting staff member, the medical or other services provided, the life space interview or debriefing provided, and the dates and times of all authorisations and re-authorisations) and the system sends it to a youth custody director.
Given another staff member or other person who was involved in or witnessed the restraint, when that person documents it, then the system holds the account as a supplemental report linked to the same incident.
Given the application of a restraint, when it is recorded, then the system opens the health care professional's assessment of the youth, due within the time limit policy sets (CK-YJ2-01), and records when the assessment took place. Where a mechanical restraint continues past the threshold policy sets (CK-YJ2-02), the record holds the more frequent assessments policy requires.
Given a restraint incident, when it is recorded, then the system opens the senior youth supervisor's assessment, due within the time limit policy sets (CK-YJ2-03), and the assessment records the consultation with the youth and staff involved, their physical and emotional well-being and need for medical care, counselling or other services, and whether behaviour support practice or the individual crisis management plan should change.
Given the written results of that assessment, when they are sent to a youth custody director, then the director's administrative review is due within the time limit policy sets (CK-YJ2-04) counted from the use of restraint, and records how the incident was handled, any need for new or revised policy or training, and any external reporting requirements. Where injury to the youth or staff did or could have occurred, or property was damaged, the record also holds the decision whether a formal de-briefing is required.
Given any use of physical or mechanical restraint, when it is recorded, then the system raises the notice to the youth's community probation officer for the case management supervisor (or designate) in regular working hours, or for the senior youth supervisor at other times or in that supervisor's absence, and records who gave the notice and when.
Edge case: where a restraint produces adverse effects such as illness, injury or severe distress, the record shows that the restraint was discontinued and that a health care assessment took place, whatever time the limits would still allow.
Data
Inputs: The written report and supplemental accounts; the time of the health care assessment; the senior youth supervisor's assessment; the director's administrative review; the notice to the community probation officer; Outputs: Work items due under CK-YJ2-01, CK-YJ2-03 and CK-YJ2-04; the report, assessment and review on the youth's file; the record of the notice; Validations: Each item policy lists must be answered before the report is submitted; an explicit 'none' or 'not yet' counts as an answer. The dates and times of authorisations on the report agree with the restraint record. The director's review needs the written results of the senior youth supervisor's assessment.

Acceptance Criteria
Given reasonable grounds to believe that a youth, visitor or staff member has contraband or evidence of a contraband or trespassing offence, when a strip search is sought, then the system records the authorisation of a youth custody director before the search, and the senior youth supervisor completes the record of authorisation in each case and submits it to a youth custody director.
Given a search made on reasonable grounds of a youth, visitor or staff member, their possessions or a youth's room, when the senior youth supervisor completes the report, then it holds at least the date, time and duration of the search, the names of the staff who conducted and observed it, the reason for the search, the reason for and a description of any force used, a description of any contraband found and seized, the date and signature of the senior youth supervisor and the youth custody director who authorised the search, and the system sends it to a youth custody director.

Given a strip search of a staff member, when it is recorded, then the record holds the Director's authorisation, the written grounds given to the staff member and the staff member's signed consent.
Given a youth who refuses to co-operate with a search, when restraint is used to carry out the search, then the record holds the approval a youth custody director gave before the restraint was used, and the search report states the reason for the force and describes it.

The Act requires a strip search to be conducted by an authorised person of the same sex, with an exception for danger to life or safety. Description
The system records each use of the body scanner on a youth as an entry of its own kind on the youth's record, with the radiation level of the scan and its result. Acceptance Criteria
Given a use of the body scanner on a youth, when it is recorded, then the youth's record holds an entry of a kind reserved for body scans that states the radiation level of the scan and whether the result was negative, positive or suspicious.
Given a scan that shows an object permanently embedded in a youth's body, when the operator records it, then the system holds an alert on the youth with the location and a description of the object, and shows that alert whenever a later scan of the youth is recorded so that the object can be validated.

Given a youth suspected of having drugs in the body, or suspected or confirmed to have drug contraband, when the scan is recorded, then the system raises a referral to a health care professional for assessment and a referral to the substance use counsellor within the centre.

FR-474 Must M0 Medium
Seized items: record, receipt, return, forfeiture and continuity of evidence
The system keeps a record of every object or substance a staff member seizes in a youth custody centre as contraband or as evidence of a contraband or trespassing offence. Show detail
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system keeps a record of every object or substance a staff member seizes in a youth custody centre as contraband or as evidence of a contraband or trespassing offence. The record describes the item and the circumstances of the seizure and follows the item until it is returned to its owner, kept for the young person's release, transferred to the police or a court, disposed of or forfeited to the government. The system runs the time limits the Act sets for the owner's request for return and for forfeiture (CK-LG3-25, CK-LG3-26, CK-LG3-27). Service lines
Youth justice
Parameters

Provisions
CL-D3-172, CL-D3-178, CL-D3-179, CL-D3-180, CL-D3-181, AU-LG3-50, AU-LG3-51, CK-LG3-25 (5 reconciled provisions and 3 further rows; 25 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given contraband, or evidence of a contraband or trespassing offence, seized by a staff member, when the seizure is recorded, then the record describes the object or substance and the circumstances in which it was seized, shows that it was deposited in a secure place at the centre, and holds the centre Director's final determination where it is disputed whether the article is contraband.
Given a seized item that is contraband but not prohibited by law, when it is placed in safekeeping for a young person, or is to be returned to a visitor on leaving, then the system produces a receipt that identifies the item for the young person or the visitor. An item found in mail and returned to the sender is recorded with the explanation given.
Given a seized item whose owner has been notified of the seizure, when the owner asks for its return within the time limit the Act sets (CK-LG3-25), then the system records the return only if the item is not required as evidence in a proceeding, is still in the custody or control of the minister, has not been forfeited, may lawfully be possessed and, where the owner is a young person in custody, would not be contraband or an unauthorised object or substance in that young person's possession.
Given an item seized from a young person in custody that is contraband or unauthorised there but lawful to possess outside the centre, when the person in charge directs that it be kept and returned on release, or that the young person be given a reasonable opportunity to arrange its disposal or safekeeping outside the centre, then the system records the direction and, for an item kept, raises its return when the young person's release is recorded.
Given a seized item, when a ground for forfeiture in the Act is met, then the system records the item as forfeited to the government and the ground: the owner cannot be located and the period the Act sets has passed since the seizure (CK-LG3-26); the owner, once notified, did not apply for its return within the time limit (CK-LG3-27); possession would be unlawful; or, for a young person in custody, the item is contraband or unauthorised, no direction to keep it was made and the young person did not arrange its disposal or safekeeping after a reasonable opportunity.
Given a seized item held as evidence, when the person in charge transfers it to the police or a court, or a staff member passes it to anyone else, then the system records who gave it up, who received it and when, and holds the receipt from the person who received it. Once charges or an investigation no longer apply to an item prohibited by law, the system records how the centre Director determined the item be disposed of.
Given seized money whose rightful owner cannot be determined and that is not needed for an investigation, when it is remitted to the Minister of Finance, then the system records the remittance and the centre Director's written notice of the forfeiture to the young person concerned.
Data

An item required as evidence, or no longer in the minister's custody or control, is not recorded as returned. A person records that an owner cannot be located or that possession would be unlawful.

Scope

Open
The Act's time limits for return and forfeiture run from the owner being notified of the seizure. Neither the Act nor the policy held says how, when or by whom the owner is notified, or whether the receipt policy gives is that notice.
Policy remits seized money with no determinable owner to the Minister of Finance at an earlier point (CK-YJ2-12) than the Act forfeits an item whose owner cannot be located (CK-LG3-26). The requirement follows the Act (CF-D3-09). The ministry should confirm whether money may be remitted before it is forfeited.
The Act states its limits in days and months without saying how the days are counted.
The Act speaks of an 'unauthorized object or substance' without defining it in the provisions held.

Rationale

Edge case: contact with a person in an adult correctional centre who is not a parent or sibling. The system records the parent or guardian's consent, the exceptional circumstances, and the recommendations policy names (R-YJ2-23) before the contact is shown as approved.
