Inputs: Grounds; approving director or supervisor; notice to the youth; monitored call entries; mail interception, examination and reading entries; persons designated to read mail; information shared with police and why; recorded copies; reasons for retention; Outputs: Monitoring authorization on the youth's record; review and re-authorization work items; communication monitoring log; retention due dates and removal records; record of disclosure to police; Validations: The grounds must be one of those policy lists (R-YJ2-22, R-YJ2-24). No monitoring, examination or reading entry may name a privileged person. A recorded copy past its limit must carry a reason or be removed.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-061, FR-067, FR-077, FR-080, DR-004
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
MQ-044 (CF-D3-16): policy states the test for reading mail two ways, reasonable and probable grounds held by a youth custody director (14.28) and reasonable grounds held by an authorized person (14.30). Both are policy tier. The threshold and the decision-maker are held as data until the ministry answers.
CF-D3-17 was checked and is not a conflict: a youth custody director authorizes, a centre director reviews and re-authorizes.
The retention limit (CK-YJ2-22) is in days with no calendar basis stated. The regulation made under s. 44(2)(l.1) of the Youth Justice Act on handling, retention and disposal of recordings is not held.
Policy 14.27 lists two conditions for contact with a person in an adult correctional centre without joining them by 'and' or 'or'. The criterion reads them as cumulative; the ministry should confirm.
The Act allows interception and recording without individualized suspicion (s. 32.5(2)); policy sets grounds for monitoring. The requirement follows policy for monitoring and reading, which is the narrower rule the ministry has set for itself.
Rationale
The Youth Justice Act allows communication to be restricted, intercepted, monitored or recorded only in accordance with the regulations. Policy requires the grounds and approval in writing on the youth's file, a standing review, and a limit on how long recorded copies are kept. Communication with a privileged person may not be monitored or examined at all. LEG007-C11
FR-478 Must M9 Low
Police access to a youth in custody: interviews, escorted absence, identification and property
The system records each police request to interview a youth in custody, to take the youth out of the centre under escort for an investigation, to fingerprint or photograph the youth, or to execute a warrant for a bodily sample. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (conditional on the youth justice scope decision)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records each police request to interview a youth in custody, to take the youth out of the centre under escort for an investigation, to fingerprint or photograph the youth, or to execute a warrant for a bodily sample. It records the conditions policy sets for each and the director's authorization. It records who was told and who was given the chance to attend. It holds the itemized, signed record of any property of the youth that police or another agency removed.
Relates To
BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice
Parameters
N01, N08, N17
Authority
Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Operational Security and Control 15.02 to 15.07 and 15.10 (external law enforcement investigations); Reintegration Leave policy on when an authorization is not required (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D3-194, CL-D3-195, CL-D3-196, OB-YJ2-33 (3 reconciled provisions and 1 further rows; 11 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a police request to interview a youth alleged to have committed an offence, when a youth custody director authorizes it, then the system requires a record that police arranged the time in advance, the youth was forewarned, and the parent or guardian was informed where possible (R-YJ2-25).
Given a request to take a youth out under police escort, when the director authorizes it, then the system also requires the director's finding that removal is necessary and the police assurance of continuous supervision and a scheduled return (R-YJ2-26). No leave authorization document is required (R-YJ3-49).
Given a police request to fingerprint or photograph a youth on site, when the centre director permits it, then the system records the charge or conviction relied on, the date police gave notice against the minimum notice (CK-YJ2-23), and whether parents or counsel were informed.
Given police or another agency removing a youth's property, when staff record it, then the system holds an itemized list with the signatures of the staff member and the officer, and whether a warrant was produced or visual access had been given.
Edge case: the youth is a victim, witness or informant and not a suspect. The system does not require forewarning of the youth, and still prompts for notice to the parent or guardian.
Data
Inputs: Police agency and officer; purpose; youth's status in the matter; scheduled time; forewarning; parent or guardian notice; adult or counsel attending; director's authorization; police assurances; warrant; items removed; signatures; Outputs: Police access record on the youth's record; authorization record; absence and return times; itemized and signed property record; Validations: An interview of a suspect or an escorted absence cannot be shown as authorized until each condition is recorded. A property removal cannot be saved without both signatures.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-074, FR-077
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
Policy requires no record of a police interview, a fingerprinting or a warrant for a bodily sample in so many words; it sets conditions a director must be satisfied of. The requirement records them so the authorization can be shown to be lawful. The ministry should confirm this is wanted.
Policy 15.03 names a youth custody director for an escorted absence and 15.04 names the centre director for fingerprinting and for escorted leave for that purpose; see MQ-048 on whether these are one position.
For a series of absences of the same nature, policy asks for a notation in the shift report and the client log (L7689); the requirement records each absence on the youth's record.
Rationale
Policy says the ministry must support the criminal justice process while protecting the rights of youth in its custody. A director may authorize a police interview or an escorted absence only if stated conditions are met, and any property removed must be itemized and signed for. CFD308-C62
FR-479 Must M0 Medium
Health information on the custody record: information form, consent, health confinement and costs
The system holds, on a youth's custody record, the health information that custody staff may see: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (conditional on the youth justice scope decision)
First needed in: M0 (schema), M9
Description
The system holds, on a youth's custody record, the health information that custody staff may see: the Health Information Form, which states precautions and considerations for the use of restraint and carries no diagnosis. It records consent to treatment, including written consent and the contact with a legal guardian where the guardian's consent is needed. It records confinement or isolation on health grounds: the written opinion, the director's authorization and each visual inspection. It records who pays for dental care, corrective lenses and an elective prescription, with any signed cost agreement. The active health record itself stays apart from other custody records.
Relates To
BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice
Parameters
N02, N17, N19, N21
Authority
Infants Act s. 17; Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), General Health and Safety 2.05, 2.06 and 2.09; Health and Safety Services 1.02 to 1.04, 2.09, 2.13 to 2.15, 4.01 to 4.06, 5.01, 5.02, 6.02, 6.03 and 7.06; General Health and Safety 8.04 (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D3-201, CL-D3-202, CL-D3-209, CL-D3-211, CL-D3-212, CL-D3-213, AU-YJ2-25, R-YJ2-32, R-YJ2-41, R-YJ2-45 (6 reconciled provisions and 4 further rows; 27 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a youth in custody, when a health care professional prepares or updates the Health Information Form, then the system places it on the youth's unit and master record, refuses a diagnosis field, and prompts an update when pregnancy is confirmed.
Given a new prescription medication or a private clinician's treatment program, when it is recorded, then the system requires the written consent of the youth, or of the legal guardian where the youth cannot consent, unless an exception policy lists applies (R-YJ2-36).
Given a health care professional's written opinion that a youth needs isolation or is a medical danger, when a youth custody director authorizes confinement, then the system records the opinion, the authorization and advised review timing, and each visual inspection with demeanour and appearance within the interval (CK-YJ2-37).
Given dental care, corrective lenses or an elective prescription, when cost is recorded, then the system records who pays under the rule that applies (R-YJ2-40, R-YJ2-41, R-YJ2-45), any director's approval, and, where the youth's negligence or misconduct is the cause, an agreement signed before care starts or lenses are ordered.
Given an admission, when it is recorded, then the system sets the dental screening, first examination and periodic examination due dates (CK-YJ2-38, CK-YJ2-39).
Data
Inputs: Health Information Form; consent and who gave it; guardian contact; health care professional's written opinion; director's authorization; visual inspection entries; chaperon's name where an examination needs one; physician's recommendation for separate housing; payer; cost agreement; approvals; Outputs: Health Information Form on the unit and master record; consent records; health confinement record and inspection log; dental due dates; cost responsibility record and signed agreement; Validations: The Health Information Form holds no diagnosis. Health confinement cannot be saved without the written opinion and a director's authorization. A cost agreement must be dated before the care or the order it covers.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-061, FR-074, FR-075, FR-080
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
See also
FR-369 (rests on some of the same provisions).
Open
Scope: policy keeps the active health record at the health centre, separate from other custody records and open to authorized health care professionals only. Whether that record (consent forms, chaperon's name, prescriptions, dental examinations) is held in this system or in a health system is not settled. If it is held elsewhere, the consent and dental criteria reduce to what the custody record needs to know.
CF-D5-03 was checked and is not a conflict. The Infants Act makes a minor's consent effective only if the provider has explained, is satisfied the minor understands, and has concluded the care is in the minor's best interests. The Act requires no record of that conclusion and policy 1.02 does not mention it.
CF-D3-18 was checked and is not a conflict: the two chaperon passages (G 2.09 and H 2.15) differ only on an emergency where no adult of the same gender is present.
OI-YJ2-18: no rule says what happens if the youth or the parent or guardian will not sign a cost agreement.
The dental limits (CK-YJ2-38, CK-YJ2-39) and the inspection interval (CK-YJ2-37) state no calendar basis. The record location for the inspections is not named in policy.
Rationale
Policy keeps the health record confidential and apart from custody records, and lets custody staff see only what they need to supervise a youth safely. It requires informed consent to treatment, written consent before new prescription medication, a director's authorization and recorded checks when a youth is confined for health reasons, and a signed agreement before a youth or family is charged a cost. CFD308-C63
FR-480 Must M9 Medium
Serious illness, injury, pregnancy, sexual activity and death in custody: notices and reports
The system records a serious illness or serious injury of a youth in custody, a confirmed pregnancy, sexual activity between youth, and a suspected or certified death. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (conditional on the youth justice scope decision)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records a serious illness or serious injury of a youth in custody, a confirmed pregnancy, sexual activity between youth, and a suspected or certified death. For each it tracks the notices policy requires, to whom and by when, and records that they were made. It holds the reports policy requires: the incident report, the entry on the youth's medical file, the centre director's reports to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice, and the staff reports and interim report on a fatality.
Relates To
BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice; guardianship
Parameters
N01, N08, N19
Authority
Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Health and Safety Services 8.01 and 8.04 to 8.07 (injuries and illness), 9.01 and 9.02 (pregnancy and sexual activity), 10.02 and 10.03 (abuse investigations) and 12.02 to 12.09 (fatalities) (tier 2)
Provisions
CL-D3-215, CL-D3-216, CL-D3-217, CL-D3-218, CL-D3-221 (5 reconciled provisions and 0 further rows; 18 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a serious illness or injury as policy defines it (R-YJ2-47), when it is recorded, then the system tracks notice to a youth custody director, the parent or guardian, and the community probation officer within the limit (CK-YJ2-40), and records each notice made.
Given an infectious disease, or a serious injury with longer-term impairment, when it is recorded, then the system also tracks notice to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice and, for a youth in the care of the director under the child protection statute, to the director's designate (CK-YJ2-41).
Given any injury, serious illness or report of abuse involving a staff member, when it is recorded, then the system requires the incident report (CK-YJ2-42), a copy for the health file, and for the abuse report the investigation results sent to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice.
Given a confirmed pregnancy or sexual activity between youth, when it is recorded, then the system records the youth's consent before any pregnancy notice, the immediate review, the medical referral limit (CK-YJ2-43), the consultation before notices, and the centre director's report to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice.
Given a suspected fatality, when the person in charge records it, then the system tracks the immediate notices and, once death is certified, notice to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice, next of kin and the probation officer, and collects the staff reports and the interim report.
Data
Inputs: Kind of event; date and time; determination that it is serious; people notified, how and when; the youth's consent to pregnancy notices; incident report; review findings; centre director's investigation and report; staff written reports; certification of death; Outputs: Event record on the youth's record; notice log with due times; reports to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice; copy of the incident report for the health file; interim fatality report; Validations: A serious illness or injury cannot be closed until each required notice is recorded as made or as not possible with a reason. A pregnancy notice cannot be recorded without the youth's consent.
Dependencies
FR-061, FR-067, FR-070, FR-075, FR-077
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
CF-D3-19 was checked and is not a conflict: the list is headed 'notify immediately' and the probation officer item carries its own later limit (CK-YJ2-40). The clock for that item follows the item.
The pregnancy notice is given by the medical practitioner with the youth's consent. Whether that consent and notice are recorded on the custody record or only on the health record depends on the health record scope question in FR-479.
Policy 9.02 says the parent or guardian, the probation officer and the police 'as appropriate' are notified after consultation with the centre director and the Provincial Director, Youth Justice. It sets no time limit for those notices.
The Provincial Director's own onward notices on a death (communications, the deputy minister, the director under the child protection statute, external review bodies) are held by cluster CL-D3-056 in another pack.
Rationale
Policy requires the senior youth supervisor to notify named people at once when a youth is seriously ill or injured and to document the notices. It requires reports to the Provincial Director, Youth Justice on a pregnancy that began in custody, on suspected sexual intercourse, on abuse involving staff, and on a death. CFD308-C64
FR-481 Must M9 Medium
Mental illness in custody: referral, written opinion and transfer to a mental health facility
The system records a staff report that a youth in custody appears mentally ill, the referral to a medical practitioner and to youth forensic psychiatric services, and the practitioner's written opinion to the centre director. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (conditional on the youth justice scope decision)
First needed in: M9
Description
The system records a staff report that a youth in custody appears mentally ill, the referral to a medical practitioner and to youth forensic psychiatric services, and the practitioner's written opinion to the centre director. Where a youth is transferred to a mental health facility under the Mental Health Act, it records the medical certificates, the authorization by the person in charge, the copies sent to the director of the facility, the leave or release that moves the youth, and the notices. It shows that the centre director's authority is suspended while the youth is detained there, that a warrant of committal stays in force, and what happens on discharge.
Relates To
BR-025
Service lines
Youth justice; child and youth mental health
Parameters
N01, N13, N17, N19
Authority
Mental Health Act ss. 22 and 29; Youth Justice Services Policy and Procedures Manual (CFD-308), Health and Safety Services 3 (referrals for psychological or psychiatric services) and 11.02 to 11.12 (admissions and transfers to and from designated mental health facilities) (tier 1)
Provisions
CL-D3-219, CL-D3-220, R-LG4-120, RC-LG4-28 (2 reconciled provisions and 2 further rows; 13 register rows in all)
Acceptance Criteria
Given a staff member's report that a youth appears mentally ill, when it is recorded, then the system tracks notice to the senior youth supervisor and a youth custody director, the referral to a medical practitioner and to youth forensic psychiatric services, and the practitioner's written opinion to the centre director.
Given a sentenced youth to be transferred to a mental health facility, when the person in charge authorizes the transfer, then the system requires the medical certificates the Act calls for (AU-LG4-37), and records that copies went to the director of the facility.
Given a youth accepted for admission, when the youth leaves the centre, then the system records the medical leave for a sentenced youth or the release for a non-sentenced youth, and notice to the parent or guardian and the community probation officer.
Given a youth detained under the Mental Health Act, when the director of the facility discharges the youth, then the system shows a youth still under a warrant of committal as returned to custody and the leave permit as revoked (R-YJ2-50).
Edge case: a remanded youth found to need psychiatric care, or any youth involuntarily admitted. The system tracks notice to Crown Counsel. For a youth certified before admission to custody, it records placement in the designated facility and no admission to the centre (R-YJ2-51).
Data
Inputs: Staff report; referral; practitioner's written opinion; medical certificates; authorization by the person in charge; facility and its director; leave or release authority; notices; discharge decision; warrant status; any removal order; Outputs: Mental health referral record; transfer record with certificates sent; leave or release record; status showing detention under the Mental Health Act and suspended authority; return to custody record; notices to Crown Counsel and the Provincial Director, Youth Justice; Validations: A transfer cannot be shown as authorized without the certificates. A youth detained in a facility is not shown as under the centre director's authority. A return to custody requires a warrant still in force.
Dependencies
FR-004, FR-036, FR-067, FR-070, FR-077
Scope
Conditional on DEP-28: whether the replacement covers youth justice.
Open
MQ-048 (CF-D3-11): policy 11.07 has 'a youth custody director' authorize the medical leave, while the Reintegration Leave section gives leaves to the centre director. The approver is held as data until the ministry answers.
The reconciler's note says policy does not cite the s. 29 transfer. It does, at 11.05 (L12011), and requires certificates under s. 22. Policy then moves the youth on a medical leave (11.07). The requirement records both the statutory authorization and the leave.
Section 29(4) of the Act names 'the person in charge' of a youth custody centre; policy 11.05 and 11.06 name the centre director. The Act does not say who operates a youth custody centre (see MQ-055).
Section 29(8) applies ss. 23 to 25 of the Act (renewal, review and discharge) to a youth transferred from custody (R-LG4-120, sent here from P49). Those steps bind the facility's director; the system receives the outcome.
Mental health scope: a youth's clinical record at the facility or with youth forensic psychiatric services is outside this requirement.
Rationale
The Mental Health Act lets the person in charge of a youth custody centre authorize a transfer only on receiving medical certificates, and the facility's director may admit only on receiving copies of them. Policy suspends the centre director's authority while the youth is detained there and returns a youth still under warrant to custody on discharge. LEG010-C3

Requirements
These are the requirements for the system that replaces ICM and MIS. Each one says what the system must do, how to check it, and which law, policy or design parameter it comes from.
[aria-label] The requirements in numbers
643 requirements across five categories
270/270 policy obligations traced to a requirement
3,689 provisions of children and family law and policy read, each with a recorded outcome
21/21 design parameters carried by at least one requirement
13 trade-offs set out, 6 still waiting on a ministry ruling
Where the requirements come from
Sources are ranked, and the ranking settles any conflict between them. Where a procedure says one thing and policy says another, the requirement follows policy and the procedure is recorded as a defect for the ministry to fix.
Legislation The Employment and Assistance Acts and their regulations, privacy, records and human rights law. For children and families: the Child, Family and Community Service Act, the Adoption Act and the federal Act on Indigenous children, youth and families. Overrides everything else.
Policy The BCEA Policy and Procedure Manual: 126 pages, 270 obligations, 297 rules, 138 time limits. For children and families: the policy chapters, standards and practice directives of the Ministry of Children and Family Development. Overrides every procedure, job aid and spreadsheet.
Practice Procedures, job aids and spreadsheets that show how the work is done today. Evidence of current practice. Never the authority for a requirement.
What they cover
Each category has its own page. Every requirement opens to show its description, the checks that prove it is met, and the reasons it exists.
25 Business What the ministry needs the new system to achieve, and how success is measured. 24 must · 1 should
481 Functional What the system must do, from a first application to an appeal and from a report about a child to an adoption order, grouped by capability. 444 must · 34 should · 3 won't
64 Quality How well it must do it: availability, recovery, security, privacy, accessibility and more. 60 must · 4 should
42 Integrations Every outside system it must exchange information with, and on what terms. 28 must · 14 should
31 Data How facts are recorded, kept, destroyed and moved from the legacy systems. 30 must · 1 should
When they are needed
The architecture delivers the system in ten modules, each in use before the next is funded. This chart counts the functional requirements by the module in which each is first needed. The foundations module carries the most, because some things cannot be added once the first record, rule or payment exists.
115 M0 Foundations
10 M1 Read access and client index
4 M2 Notices and correspondence
9 M3 Documents and capture
8 M4 Work management
9 M5 Decisions and rules
14 M6 Payments and recovery
6 M7 Reconsideration and appeal
18 M8 Employment and disability assistance
284 M9 Child protection
Functional requirements by the module in which each is first needed. A requirement needed across several modules is counted in the first.
How each requirement is written
It can be checked. Every requirement carries acceptance criteria written as "given, when, then", so a tester can say whether it passes.
It says where it comes from. Each one lists the policy obligations it meets and the design parameters that test it, and links to them.
It holds no dollar amounts or day counts. Those change, so they live once in the rules register with their policy source and effective date. A requirement names the rule; the register holds the value.
It does not copy today's system. Where the current system calculates something other than what policy states, the requirement follows policy.
What is still open
Some requirements depend on decisions nobody has made yet: rulings on conflicts inside policy, the records schedules, and several architecture decisions. The trade-offs page sets out each conflict, how it was resolved or who must resolve it, and the dependencies and risks that go with them.
The requirements for children and family services were added in version 1.6. Each was written from the passage of law or policy it rests on. Nobody at the ministry has reviewed them yet. Those for mental health, integrated teams and youth justice are marked conditional, because nobody has decided whether the new system covers that work.
Source: requirements specification, version 1.6, a draft. Words with a special meaning link to the glossary.

Integrations
Every outside system the new system must exchange information with: what flows each way, how it is protected, and what happens when it fails.
Three rules apply to every integration below. They are not repeated in each entry.
1. An integration that is not in the Module 0 integration inventory is not authorised to exist TA-C42. Each entry here becomes one or more named rows in that inventory, using the columns in TA §C.13.2: system, counterparty and accountable role, direction, pattern, classification, legal basis, criticality and disposition. The Programme Chief Architect owns the inventory, and it is due by month 4 of Module 0. 2. Every integration has a legal basis recorded in the agreement registry (FR-085). An integration without one is unauthorised, whatever it does today. 3. No interactive path depends synchronously on more than one external participant (NFR-A-004). Where an entry says "asynchronous", this rule is why. Where no source states a service level, the entry says "not stated". The design then assumes the exchange is not on a path a worker waits on, until the counterparty commits to a figure in writing.
Details marked [U] are unverified in the architecture's own register. They are settled in the inventory, not here.

INT-001 Must
Corporate Accounting System
Post payments, reversals, amounts owed to the ministry, recoveries and write-offs to the book of record, and reconcile daily and at month-end. Show detail
Purpose
Post payments, reversals, amounts owed to the ministry, recoveries and write-offs to the book of record, and reconcile daily and at month-end.
Integration Type
Batch posting and reconciliation query
Data Exchanged
From this system to CAS: postings with coding block, determination reference and run identifier; supplier records for provider payments.
From CAS to this system: the posted position, rejections, the month-end calendar and blackout periods.
Integration Pattern
Only through the Issuance Service (FR-042). No other component holds a posting credential.
Authentication
A service credential held only by the Issuance Service, over mutual TLS.
Error Handling
CAS rejects some batches as a whole when supplier key fields are missing (APP-R8). Supplier keys are therefore checked before submission. A rejection becomes a reconciliation break with an owner and an age. It is never retried silently.
SLA
Daily reconciliation. Postings are queued during blackouts (NFR-A-005). Today CAS offers only file-availability windows. The cutoff calendar is still to be confirmed by the Executive Financial Officer.
Owner
Provincial corporate financial function; ministry Executive Financial Officer.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
The corporate financial system remains the book of record (TA §C.6.4). CAS is outside the replacement scope, so the new system must connect to it (APP §1.1).
INT-002 Must
Bank and electronic funds transfer
Pay by direct deposit; Show detail
Purpose
Pay by direct deposit; receive settlement, return and reject files; run payment traces; receive client debt repayments.
Integration Type
Batch file transfer
Data Exchanged
Outbound: payment files in the format the bank requires; trace requests.
Inbound: settlement confirmations, returns, rejects, trace results and repayment files.
Integration Pattern
Through the Issuance Service only. A missing inbound file raises an alarm.
Authentication
Mutual TLS and file signing, as the bank requires.
Error Handling
A returned payment reopens the entitlement and queues a work item (FR-044). A missing file raises an alarm.
SLA
Settlement within the bank's stated window. The maximum reconciliation lag is stated for each payment channel.
Owner
The settlement institution; ministry payment operations lead.
Classification
Protected B
Rationale
Payment is the most critical integration (TA §C.13.3).
INT-003 Must
Provincial print-and-mail and cheque printing
Print and mail notices, letters and booklets; Show detail
Purpose
Print and mail notices, letters and booklets; print cheques; receive returned mail and delivery confirmations.
Integration Type
Batch file transfer (assumed, because no public API specification has been found [U])
Data Exchanged
Outbound: rendered documents with delivery details; cheque print files drawn from a controlled range of cheque numbers.
Inbound: confirmations that mail was lodged; returned mail.
Integration Pattern
Notices go through Notices & Correspondence. Cheques go through the Issuance Service.
Authentication
SFTP with service credentials, to be confirmed with the service.
Error Handling
Returned mail updates the delivery record and raises a work item. Deemed receipt is calculated by rule (FR-064), never typed in.
SLA
The file delivery windows the service sets.
Owner
Provincial print-and-mail service; ministry correspondence business owner.
Classification
Protected B/C
Rationale
Notices and cheques go through this service today, over 10 named interfaces (APP §4.2).
INT-004 Must
Provincial notification service
Send notices and messages electronically, and receive delivery confirmations. Show detail
Purpose
Send notices and messages electronically, and receive delivery confirmations.
Integration Type
API
Data Exchanged
Outbound: messages and notice references.
Inbound: delivery events.
Integration Pattern

INT-023 Must
Legacy platforms while old and new run side by side
Serve the published contract from the legacy platforms while capture proceeds; Show detail
Purpose
Serve the published contract from the legacy platforms while capture proceeds; write data back to legacy for captured cohorts; feed the shadow comparison.
Integration Type
Anti-corruption layer (facade, adapter and translator), runtime events, transactional outbox, change-data capture
Data Exchanged
From the legacy platforms: events and read models for cohorts not yet captured; the inputs each legacy decision used (FR-095).
To the legacy platforms: write-back for captured cohorts, using insert and update operations only (DR-014).
Integration Pattern
The layer holds no business rules and is set up to be retired. MIS is not a passive store: it holds payment issuance, debt and time limits, and it is the master copy when income data conflicts (APP §2). Both the coexistence design and the legacy side of the shadow comparison must therefore include MIS and every other legacy system that runs program logic (APP §7.1).
Authentication
Dedicated integration identities. Write-back uses its own identity, so the system can recognise its own writes and stop them looping back.
Error Handling
A late legacy change to a captured record goes to a queue for a person to reconcile (FR-098).
SLA
Sized from the measured point at which the legacy platform saturates (NFR-P-001).
Owner
The coexistence lead; the legacy platform's configuration authority, whose capacity is itself an open dependency (DEP-03).
Classification
Protected C
Rationale
Replacing the legacy platforms step by step is impossible without this (commitment 3). A comparison against only part of the legacy calculation is not a real check (TA §C.2.7).

Inbound: the authority's confirmation, verbal and then written, in the prescribed form or a form the authority determines; its confirmation of receipt of a referral; its notice that it is or will be providing services or will have custody; its written confirmation of the date and time of transition; its requests for information under the CFCSA; its answer before a permanent transfer of custody is sought.

Authentication
Not stated. The agreement registry holds the agreement and its information conditions where one exists (FR-085, FR-117).

INT-028 Must
Indigenous governing bodies, Indigenous communities and designated representatives

Integration Type

Data Exchanged

Inbound: views on a significant measure; the record of consultation and cooperation; advice that confirms a child belongs to an Indigenous community; a report of any incident affecting the privacy or security of information given under an agreement.
Reference sources read: the federal public list of Indigenous groups that gave notice, coordination agreements and Indigenous laws with their dates; the provincial and national repositories of Indigenous governing bodies; the Regulation's schedules of prescribed organizations and designated representative positions, held with effective dates.
Published: each power or duty agreement and its amendments, which the minister must publish on a public government website.
Integration Pattern
Each notice is kept as issued with proof of how and when it was given. The recipient is found from the registers at each notice, not from memory. Conditions on information given to an Indigenous party are recorded on the information itself and outlast the agreement (DR-006).
Authentication
Not stated. Policy requires encryption and password protection when a notice is emailed (NFR-C-009).
Error Handling
Not stated. Policy requires a copy of each notice and its delivery receipt on the child's record, verbal notice to be recorded, and reasons for withholding to be documented (FR-136, FR-137).
SLA
Not stated for the exchange. Each notice runs on the notice period the Act or policy sets (FR-136, FR-188, FR-189).
Owner

Data Exchanged
Outbound: a request for what an agency holds about a child, youth or family during the initial record review; transfer requests and the transfer summary; the record itself on transfer; a request for a prior contact check.
Inbound: what the agency holds, recorded with its source; answers to transfer requests; entries by a secondary worker under joint file management; reportable circumstance reports written by an agency practitioner for the delegate of the director; prior contact check results.
Integration Pattern
What an agency supplies is recorded as evidence with the agency as its source. A transfer of records from one director to another rests on a written instrument that names the records and its effective date (FR-314).
Authentication
Through the exchange and the agreement registry, as for INT-013.
Error Handling
Not stated. Safety information passes at once when a move involves immediate risk to a child, whatever the state of the transfer (FR-303).
SLA
Not stated for the exchange. The initial record review and each transfer step run on the time limits policy sets (FR-144, FR-301, FR-302).
Owner
Each delegated agency, for its own system. Ministry business owner not stated.
Classification
not stated in the sources; treated as Protected C until classified, as INT-013 is
Rationale
An initial record review that cannot reach an agency's records is incomplete, and a transfer between systems must not lose the record (CL-D1-020, R-RP1-31, CL-D8-025, CL-D1-217, R-QA1-24, CL-D7-176). Needed by FR-144, FR-226, FR-301 to FR-306, FR-314, FR-338, FR-339 and FR-348. Whether the delegated-agency standards behind some of these remain in force waits on DEP-29.
INT-030 Must

Purpose
Tell police what policy requires them to be told, receive what police report, and check the Protection Order Registry. INT-014 covers one exchange only: confirming arrest warrants for assistance applicants who consent. This entry covers child protection work.
Integration Type
Request and response, manual today. Registry checks go by email and telephone through centralized screening. Proof of service goes to the registry by fax. Checks with local police are telephone calls.
Data Exchanged

Integration Pattern
A registry result is held as unverified until a verification with police or the courthouse is recorded, where a decision depends on it (FR-148). Each disclosure to police is recorded with its legal basis (FR-077). Screening results about a person who is not a client carry a limit on use (DR-030).
Authentication
Not stated.
Error Handling
Not stated. A request with no answer stays visible as outstanding. Local protocols set the threshold for police investigation.
SLA

Owner

Classification
not stated in the sources; treated as Protected C until classified, as INT-013 is
Rationale
A protection order or a police concern can change a safety decision, and an order police cannot see as served cannot be enforced (CL-D1-029, CL-D1-030, CL-D1-064, CL-D1-128, CL-D7-211, AU-LG1-21, CL-D1-150, CL-D1-308, CL-D2-013, OB-RP1-28). Needed by FR-148, FR-149, FR-168, FR-182, FR-183, FR-196, FR-228 and FR-303.

Not stated.

Not stated. Volumes for leave on an adult sentence are very low.
Owner
Adult corrections; the sheriff service; the Parole Board of Canada; Correctional Service of Canada; Justice Canada; each other jurisdiction's youth justice service; forensic psychiatric services; each designated facility. Ministry business owner not stated. Whether the forensic service's own records sit inside the replacement is a scope question.
Classification
not stated in the sources; treated as Protected C until classified, as INT-013 is
Rationale
Each move of a youth between bodies carries duties of notice and record the manual sets (CL-D3-011, CL-D3-015, CL-D3-022, CL-D3-024, CL-D3-023, CL-D3-019, CL-D3-004, CL-D3-005, CL-D3-007, CL-D3-009, CL-D3-062, CL-D3-063, CL-D3-060, CL-D3-068, CL-D4-039, CL-D3-061, CL-D4-081, CL-D4-082, CL-D4-083, CL-D3-040, CL-D3-071, CL-D3-094, CL-D3-096, R-YJ3-33, CL-D3-121, CL-D3-219, CL-D3-220). Needed by FR-413, FR-417, FR-418, FR-420, FR-423, FR-433, FR-442 to FR-444, FR-448, FR-450, FR-453, FR-454, FR-458 and FR-481.
DRAFT
A design proposal for the successor to British Columbia's integrated case management systems, covering employment assistance, disability assistance, child care subsidy, employment services and child protection.
Figures on this site are drawn from the architecture document, from 326 service-delivery procedures, and from 308 documents and 14 statutes and regulations on children and family services. Nothing here is a government commitment.

Quality requirements
How well the system must work: how fast, how available, how secure, how accessible and how easy to support. Targets come from the architecture or are measured from the running legacy systems.
The figures in this section come from two places: the architecture's own positions, and measurements in the Release 26.7 technical design documents. For the services that make decisions and pay benefits, the architecture does not set response-time, concurrency or availability figures. It requires them to be measured from the running legacy system and given an owner TA-C28, and this document does the same. No volume figure in the sources covers concurrency, response time or storage APP-C2, and the service-delivery procedures give none either BPCM-C3.

Performance 6
NFR-P-001 Must
The capacity and response table is complete, measured and owned
Before design freeze, every cell of the architecture's capacity table is filled in and has a named owner. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Before design freeze, every cell of the architecture's capacity table is filled in and has a named owner. The table covers peak and average transactions per second, concurrent workers, annual determination volume, p95 and p99 response times, availability, recovery time and recovery point. It covers the Open Host Service, the anti-corruption layer, the determination service, the event backbone, each domain store, work management and payments.
Figures come from the legacy system's own telemetry over a full monthly issuance cycle, not from workshop estimates.
Concurrent worker numbers come from directory and session data. Determination volumes come from legacy counts per program family.
Response targets start from observed legacy behaviour, plus the improvement the service standard commits to.
Measurement Method
The table is reviewed at the design-freeze gate. Every figure must trace to a telemetry extract.
Load Conditions
The only volumes recorded today are per-interface and batch figures from the technical design documents APP-C1. For example, the employment-assistance monthly rollover covers about 158,414 benefit plans, 414,225 benefit lines and 73,920 orders. MIS feedback runs to about 400,000 header and 400,000 detail records a month. A CPP request file holds about 250,000 records. The predecessor's audit counted about 9,400 user accounts (TA §C.16.4). That is the number of users, not the number working at once.
Rationale
Nobody can responsibly approve the combined caseworker read while the legacy platform's saturation point is unmeasured. The anti-corruption layer's rate limits, circuit breakers and bulkheads are sized from these numbers (TA §C.15.2).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N18
NFR-P-002 Must
Payment runs finish within the financial calendar
A full monthly issuance cycle at production volume completes within the window the corporate financial calendar allows. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
A full monthly issuance cycle at production volume completes within the window the corporate financial calendar allows. The cycle includes assembly, pre-flight checks, approval, release, settlement intake and three-way reconciliation. If release is interrupted, it resumes and still finishes within the same window.
Measurement Method
A full-scale synthetic run in a production-shaped environment, including a test that interrupts release part-way (TA §C.6.8 criterion 3).
Load Conditions
Monthly rollover volumes as in NFR-P-001. The peak follows the issuance run, not the working day.
Rationale
Load on the payments service peaks with the issuance run, not over the course of the day (TA §C.15.1).
Parameters
N17
NFR-P-003 Must
Determination capacity at measured volume and peak
The determination service handles the measured annual determination volume for each program family and the measured peak rate. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The determination service handles the measured annual determination volume for each program family and the measured peak rate. This includes recalculating every affected case in batch after a rate change. The capacity model records the headroom factor, set by its owner, the ministry CTO.
Measurement Method
A load test that replays a recorded month of determinations, and a rate-change simulation across the full affected population.
Rationale
The architecture calls annual determination volume "the single most important number" in its capacity table (TA §C.15.1).
Parameters
N07
NFR-P-004 Must
A limit on how stale the facts behind a decision can be
Before the first production determination, the system sets a limit on how far the evidence snapshot may lag behind the latest recorded facts. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Before the first production determination, the system sets a limit on how far the evidence snapshot may lag behind the latest recorded facts. There is one limit per determination class (interactive, batch issuance and retroactive recalculation), set from measured projection lag. The system monitors the lag against the limit.
Measurement Method
Projection-lag telemetry for each contributing stream, with an alarm as lag approaches the limit.
Rationale
The architecture's example limits (seconds for interactive decisions, about a minute for batch) are unverified. The real numbers must come from measurement (TA §B.4.3).
Parameters
N09
NFR-P-005 Must
Event backbone consumer lag
Each consumer publishes the most lag it can tolerate. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each consumer publishes the most lag it can tolerate. The system raises an alarm at half that figure. Past the maximum, captured cohorts move to manual verification before any payment issues.
Measurement Method
Lag metrics for each consumer against its own threshold.
Rationale
When the backbone degrades, messages pile up, and a pile-up is only safe if it has a limit (TA §E.8.3).
Parameters
N06, N18
NFR-P-006 Should
Analytics query profile
Interactive analytics queries must filter on a partition. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE ---
Requirement
Interactive analytics queries must filter on a partition. Service tiers are committed per data class, as decided under D5. Caching for the most sensitive class happens in memory only.
Measurement Method
The Module 0 object-store benchmark, and query-plan checks that reject interactive queries without a partition filter.
Rationale
The object store's documented profile is response times over 100 ms and 1,000 active connections per node. Partition pruning is the first lever, and local disk caching is forbidden for Protected C (TA §A.5, §C.14).
Parameters
N12
Availability and Resilience 11
NFR-A-001 Must
Availability targets and combined availability
Each component on the caseworker's interactive path is available 99.9% of the time. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each component on the caseworker's interactive path is available 99.9% of the time. The combined caseworker read has a design target of 99.5%. That read runs through the experience back end, the Open Host Service, three contexts and the determination service. Availability is stated per service, and the combined figure is recalculated whenever the chain of calls changes.
A 99.5% combined figure allows about 2¼ minutes of unplanned downtime per 7.5-hour working day [D].
Maintenance windows for payment services come from the financial calendar (NFR-M-007).
Measurement Method
Availability is measured at the contract boundary, as the consumer experiences it (NFR-M-002).
Rationale
Availability multiplies along a chain of dependencies, and nobody has yet done that arithmetic for this system's own chain of calls (TA §C.3.8).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-002 Must
Recovery point and recovery time
- RPO: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
RPO: zero for anything that affects an entitlement or a payment, meaning determinations, payment instructions and evidence assertions TA-C29. Other data may have a stated RPO.
RTO: stated for each service against the harm its failure causes. Shared infrastructure takes the strictest target of anything that depends on it.
Recovery objectives are proven by exercise for each release train, not just stated.
Measurement Method
Recovery exercise results for each tier-1 component. A figure nobody has measured is not a target.
Rationale
A lost payment instruction is a person without money TA-C13.
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-003 Must
Every dependency declares its timeout, circuit breaker and fallback
Every synchronous dependency has a declared timeout, a circuit breaker and a declared fallback behaviour. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Every synchronous dependency has a declared timeout, a circuit breaker and a declared fallback behaviour. Every screen that depends on the exchange states what the worker sees, what they can still do, and what is queued.
Circuit breaker for external dependencies
Timeout on all network calls
Retry with backoff only for idempotent operations
Bulkhead isolation, including per external provider
Degraded behaviour documented per screen
Measurement Method
An architecture fitness function that checks every outbound client has a timeout and a breaker, plus tests of each fallback mode.
Rationale
A dependency without a stated fallback takes the caseworker desktop down with it (TA §C.15.3).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N18
NFR-A-004 Must
Dependencies on other organisations in interactive work
No interactive path depends synchronously on more than one external participant . Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
No interactive path depends synchronously on more than one external participant TA-C30. Any exchange on a caseworker path that blocks the worker needs 99.9% availability, run active-active across multiple sites, with bulkheads for each provider. Where two or more participants are involved, the design is asynchronous and uses a work item.
Measurement Method
Call-graph analysis for each interactive journey. The exchange's availability commitment is obtained in writing (dependency DEP-06).
Rationale
Four participants at 99.5% each combine to 98.0%, which is too low for work a caseworker waits on (TA §C.3.8).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-005 Must
Payments continue during a corporate posting blackout
Payments keep issuing while the corporate financial system is closed for month-end or year-end posting. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Payments keep issuing while the corporate financial system is closed for month-end or year-end posting. Postings wait in a queue that has an owner and an age alarm, and they are released when posting reopens.
Measurement Method
A blackout simulation in the M6 test cycle, plus an age alarm on queued postings.
Rationale
A benefit payment must not depend on a finance system's maintenance window (TA §C.6.6).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N17
NFR-A-006 Must
Disaster recovery and business continuity are exercised
Disaster recovery exercises run twice a year, and at least one each year is unannounced to the operations team . Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Disaster recovery exercises run twice a year, and at least one each year is unannounced to the operations team TA-C31. They cover catalogue restore, event backbone recovery, read-model rebuild and determination replay from the decision record store.
The business owns a business continuity plan that is separate from rollback. It covers how an office serves a client with no system for a day and for a week, how staff record actions for later entry, and who authorises payment. It is exercised each year with the regional offices before the first capture.
Measurement Method
Exercise reports with measured recovery times, checked against NFR-A-002.
Rationale
A restore nobody has run is a hypothesis (TA §E.8.5).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N14
NFR-A-007 Must
The child protection reporting line has its own availability target
The 24/7 statutory child protection reporting line has the highest availability target in the platform, set by its business owner with the CIO. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (M9) ---
Requirement
The 24/7 statutory child protection reporting line has the highest availability target in the platform, set by its business owner with the CIO. Its intake path depends on no service whose combined availability falls below that target. A rehearsed fallback path receives and safely records a report when downstream services are down. The line has its own change window.
Measurement Method
The combined-availability arithmetic is run against this chain of calls specifically, and the fallback path is rehearsed.
Rationale
If the reporting line is down for two hours on a Sunday, a child protection report goes unreceived (TA §C.12.2).
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N15
NFR-A-008 Must
Platform fallback modes are specified, rehearsed and owned
Each failure below has a fallback mode that is rehearsed and has a named decision-maker: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Each failure below has a fallback mode that is rehearsed and has a named decision-maker:
The anti-corruption layer is unavailable. Read models keep serving and show a visible staleness indicator.
The event backbone is unavailable. The outbox accumulates messages.
The determination service is unavailable. Determinations queue, and a captured cohort never falls back to legacy.
The exchange is unavailable. Where policy permits, determinations proceed on the evidence held and are flagged for verification after issue TA-C32.
The legacy platform is unavailable. Cohorts not yet captured become read-only.
Amended v1.5 (TA §E.8.3), payments under each fallback:
The event backbone is unavailable. Each consumer has a published maximum lag, with an alarm at half of it. Past the maximum, captured cohorts are verified by a person before payment is issued.
The determination service is unavailable. Once determinations have queued for longer than the stated interval, the trigger for emergency issuance is met (FR-047).
The exchange is unavailable. No client's payment waits on another organisation's gateway.
Measurement Method
Rehearsal records for each fallback mode.
Rationale
A fallback mode first discovered during an incident is an outage (TA §E.8.3).
Parameters
N05, N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-A-009 Must
An on-premise continuity copy for any software-as-a-service product at the core
The ministry must be able to keep its mission-critical services running if the supplier of any core software-as-a-service (SaaS) product cuts off access to it, or the product is lost for a long time for any other reason. Show detail
Requirement
The ministry must be able to keep its mission-critical services running if the supplier of any core software-as-a-service (SaaS) product cuts off access to it, or the product is lost for a long time for any other reason. Any recovery that depends on reaching the SaaS product at that point, such as a batch data export, fails in this case. The fallback must not need it.
Restated 2026-09-30 under ADR-009 Part A (ACCEPTED). The programme direction of 2026-09-29 is unchanged: supplier cut-off is the contingency; the copy is retrieved continuously or on a cycle while the service is live; it serves mission-critical services only; monthly payment issuance comes first; the cut-off is rehearsed without warning. What changed is that the copy now preserves the architecture's evidence model (drift Δ2.4, Δ3.1–Δ3.7).
Scope by context, not by product. A SaaS product sits wholly inside one bounded context, behind that context's published contract, and exchanges only evidence and determinations with other contexts (N02, N03, N10). A product is core if losing it would stop a mission-critical service of the context it sits in. (v1.3 read: "if losing it would stop determinations, payment issuance, or caseworkers' access to case records". That wording presumed a SaaS product could hold the system of record or host determination; see Part B below.)
What the continuity copy is. For each core SaaS product, the ministry holds on-premise, on infrastructure it controls, a replica of records, not of state:
the owning context's covered event streams, with their evidence succession sets, all three time axes and the operation (Record, Supersede, Correct, Verify, Invalidate) preserved, verified against the hash chain and signed heads (NFR-SEC-009);
the decision-record store;
the rules artefacts and engine images;
projections rebuilt from those.
A vendor table snapshot, a CRUD change-data-capture feed or a CSV extract does not conform unless it is transformed, at capture, into the owning context's registered events with all three time axes and the operation preserved. (v1.3 read: "a copy of a defined core subset of the product's data".)
Kept current while the service is live. The copy is retrieved continuously or on a stated cycle while the service is available. Its maximum age may not exceed the batch watermark bound (FR-009, NFR-P-004); otherwise a separate fallback bound is recorded and stamped on every determination made in fallback.
What the copy is for. The copy supports the mission-critical services only, not every service. The ministry defines and owns the list of mission-critical services and the records each one needs.
Payments come first. The first mission-critical service is monthly payment issuance: determining, issuing and reconciling the monthly payment run. Its fallback is designed, built and rehearsed before any other.
Fallback runs the same function. Determinations made in fallback run the same Determine(), with the five bound artefacts and the watermark (FR-001, FR-008, FR-009). Payments made in fallback go through the same controls as normal payments (FR-042, FR-046).
One writer at every moment. Switching to fallback is a recorded single-writer handover per context and per cohort (N05). Events written in fallback are appended to the authoritative streams when service returns, never merged (FR-098). Payment instruction identifiers keep their FR-042 derivation, so an entitlement cannot be paid twice across the switch. (v1.3 read: "reconciled if and when service is restored or replaced", which is the both-write-then-reconcile pattern N05 forbids.)
The copy is a registered derivative. It is subject to correction propagation, use constraints, disposition and cryptographic erasure like any other copy (DR-004, DR-006, DR-007).
Plan details for each product. The continuity plan (NFR-A-006) states the copy's maximum age, when a loss of service counts as protracted, who decides to switch to the fallback, and who decides to switch back.
Products that cannot be core. A SaaS product cannot be a core element if the records above cannot be retrieved continuously or on a cycle while the service is running, or if its function cannot run outside the supplier's service. (Function portability restored from v1.2; v1.3 removed it without a changelog entry, drift Δ3.4.)
What this requirement does not authorise (ADR-009 Part B, PROPOSED). NFR-A-009 is a continuity requirement. It does not by itself authorise any SaaS product to store Protected C data, to hold the system of record, or to host determination. Each of those needs a recorded relaxation by its named authority: storing Protected C data or holding the system of record needs A.3 commitment 5, agreed jointly by the Ministry Privacy Officer, the provincial CISO and the Ministry Records Officer (a reclassification question under D12; TC-1, NFR-C-004); hosting determination needs A.3 commitment 2, agreed jointly by the Chief Architect and the ADM Policy and Program Design (FR-090; NFR-I-006). Until such a relaxation is recorded, a SaaS product may be core only where its data stays below Protected C, or it holds a projection whose system of record is on-premise, and it does not host determination.
Measurement Method
A rehearsal is recorded for each core SaaS product, as for NFR-A-008. In the rehearsal, access to the product is cut off without warning, and the mission-critical services run from the continuity copy alone. The rehearsal verifies the copy against the hash chain, runs fallback determinations through the same Determine(), and on return appends the fallback events without a merge. The monthly payment run is rehearsed first, at production volume, before that SaaS product goes live.
Rationale
If a supplier withdraws access, the source system is offline by construction, so nothing can be exported from it at that point. A client's monthly payment is still due on a set date. Programme direction, 2026-09-29, recorded as ADR-009 Part A. The copy must preserve the evidence model, because a state replica loses succession sets, the three time axes, the difference between Supersede and Correct, registered schemas and hash-chain continuity, and a fallback built on it could not produce a defensible determination.
Relates To
BR-004, BR-013, FR-001, FR-008, FR-009, FR-042, FR-043, FR-046, FR-047, FR-098, DR-004, DR-006, DR-007, NFR-A-005, NFR-A-006, NFR-A-008, NFR-C-004, TC-1, TC-11
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED], N05, N03, N01, N17
Decision
ADR-009 (Part A ACCEPTED; Part B PROPOSED)
NFR-A-010 Must
Child protection work done at any hour can be recorded and approved at any hour
NFR-A-007 covers receipt of a report on the reporting line. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (M9) ---
Requirement
NFR-A-007 covers receipt of a report on the reporting line. This requirement covers the work that follows it and runs on limits counted in hours or from the moment a person is informed. Outside office hours and away from the office, a worker can screen a report and a supervisor can approve the screening; contact an Indigenous authority, record its confirmation and refer a report; record a safety assessment, a verbal safety plan agreement and a withdrawal from one; record that a child was taken charge of or removed, with the start time, the efforts to reach a parent and the supervisor's approval; and write, approve and send a reportable circumstance report. When the system is unavailable, an entry made afterwards carries the time each act took place, and no start time is lost.
Measurement Method
The availability target for these functions is set by their business owner with the CIO and measured for evenings, weekends and holidays apart from office hours. A rehearsal takes the system down during a taking charge and shows that the start time and the approval are recorded afterwards with their true times.
Rationale
The Act requires a prompt report, policy requires an immediate screening assessment in a dangerous situation, taking charge runs on limits counted in hours, and the reportable circumstance limit runs from being informed with no stated allowance for weekends or holidays (CL-D1-022, CL-D1-023, CL-D7-160, CL-D1-018, CL-D1-019, CL-D1-042, CL-D1-051, CL-D1-059, CL-D1-060, CL-D1-131, CL-D7-211, CL-D1-118, CK-QA1-07, CK-QA1-08, CK-QA1-09). The standards for delegated agencies require an on-call service with access to a supervisor at all times, subject to DEP-29. Needed by FR-122, FR-123, FR-145, FR-160, FR-165, FR-166, FR-180, FR-182 and FR-338.
Parameters
N16, N19, N01
NFR-A-011 Should
Youth justice records are made at any hour
A custody centre runs day and night. Show detail
Priority: SHOULD_HAVE (conditional on DEP-28) ---
Requirement
A custody centre runs day and night. The system is available for custody records through nights, weekends and holidays, or takes entries made after the event with the time each act took place. This covers the restraint log and its intervals, the use of force notice, the health care assessment after a restraint, an emergency medical leave approved in the centre Director's absence, a serious complaint made after hours to the on-call youth custody director, a warrant of suspension sought by police out of hours, and the provincial director's review for a youth detained on a weekend.
Measurement Method
The availability target for custody functions is set by their business owner with the CIO and measured across all hours. A rehearsal records a restraint during an outage and shows each interval entered afterwards with its true time.
Rationale
The restraint intervals, the use of force notice and the health care assessment run in minutes and hours, and policy sends out-of-hours warrants, reviews and serious complaints to an on-call manager or director (CL-D3-157, CL-D3-161, CL-D3-163, CL-D3-166, CL-D4-129, CL-D4-130, AU-YJ3-12, OB-YJ2-78). Needed by FR-427, FR-458, FR-462 and FR-469 to FR-471.

N16, N19
Scalability 3
NFR-S-001 Must
Scale to caseload and payment-run peaks
Services scale horizontally, without code changes, to the measured peaks in NFR-P-001 to NFR-P-003. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Services scale horizontally, without code changes, to the measured peaks in NFR-P-001 to NFR-P-003. The capacity model records growth projections for caseload and determination volume, set by its owner.
Growth Projections
None of the sources give any. The capacity model's owner (the ministry CTO, with the operations directorate) records them before design freeze.
Measurement Method
A scale test to the recorded headroom factor.
Rationale
Scale depends on the number of people served, not on the legacy system, so today's volumes are a minimum.
Parameters
N16 [PROPOSED]
NFR-S-002 Must
Data volume across decades of retention
Stores can be partitioned by retention class from the first event, and are sized to keep records for decades. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Stores can be partitioned by retention class from the first event, and are sized to keep records for decades. The current system keeps child services records for up to 90 years after closure and investigation records for 15 years (APP §6). Records are disposed of by class when their schedule expires.
Data Archival Strategy
Set per fact class under DR-004. The default is disposal of a whole class on schedule. Large, loosely structured content uses reference-based indirection. Per-subject cryptographic erasure applies only to named classes. Archival transfer applies where required.
Rationale
Partitioning by retention class must be in place from the first event (TA §B.7.1).

N12
NFR-S-003 Must
Migration and backfill at cutover volumes
Migration, identity matching and backfill run, re-run and reconcile at cutover volumes within agreed windows. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Migration, identity matching and backfill run, re-run and reconcile at cutover volumes within agreed windows. The design documents record matching-key volumes of about 15 million contact aliases, 35 million service-provider keys in the corporate accounting system, 1 million service-provider keys and 8 million contact-matching keys.
Measurement Method
A full-volume migration rehearsal that passes the quality gates in DR-012.
Rationale
Migration is a product with its own quality gates, not a project task (TA §C.2.8).

N01, N14
Security 15
NFR-SEC-001 Must
Authentication
All users sign in through the provincial single sign-on service using OIDC. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
All users sign in through the provincial single sign-on service using OIDC.
Staff: the corporate directory, with its multi-factor authentication.
Citizens: the BC Services Card authentication service, at identity assurance level 3.
Businesses and providers: BCeID Basic and Business.
Browser security: each experience has a back end for front end that holds the confidential client. No access token, refresh token or identity assertion reaches storage the browser can read TA-C33.
Session and re-authentication rules follow the provincial service's policy and are recorded for each experience.
Measurement Method
A security architecture review at each module gate, plus an automated check that no token reaches the browser.
Rationale
Identity is a commodity and is reused as it is (TA §B.6.1; commitment 8).
Parameters
N11
NFR-SEC-002 Must
Access rules written as tested code
Program confidentiality rules and API access rules are versioned, tested policy artefacts. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Program confidentiality rules and API access rules are versioned, tested policy artefacts. A policy engine evaluates them, and they are released through the same pipeline as eligibility rules. Access is checked at every resolver and endpoint, on both the links and the records of the graph. A restricted client record is a separate type, not an empty field on a normal record. Every access decision is logged with who, what, the purpose and the legal basis.
Measurement Method
A policy test corpus in CI, where a policy change that reduces coverage fails the build. Graph tests confirm that a restricted record's existence cannot be inferred from empty fields.
Rationale
In child protection, the fact that a record exists is often the sensitive fact (TA §B.6.2).
Parameters
N21, N13, N18
NFR-SEC-003 Must
Access rights are generated, never granted by hand
Access rights come from role definitions and program assignments held in a system of record, and automation applies them. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Access rights come from role definitions and program assignments held in a system of record, and automation applies them. Manual grant is not a supported operation TA-C34. Every role definition has a named owner and an expiry date. The system publishes a count of accounts holding rights that the access model does not explain, with a target of zero. Access reviews run every quarter for standard roles and every month for elevated and restricted-record access.
Measurement Method
Accounts reconciled against the access model and published every cycle.
Rationale
The predecessor's audit found that more than a third of about 9,400 users had access outside the defined model, and that nobody was checking (TA §C.16.4).
Parameters
N17, N18
NFR-SEC-004 Must
Active access monitoring and restricted-record controls
The system watches access patterns for anomalies, such as records outside the assigned caseload, out-of-hours restricted access and unusual volumes. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The system watches access patterns for anomalies, such as records outside the assigned caseload, out-of-hours restricted access and unusual volumes. Alerts go to a monitored queue with an SLA. Staff must record a business reason before opening a restricted or active-protection record. Break-glass access exists, is logged, and is reviewed within one business day. Restricted-record access is logged separately and can raise its own alerts.
Measurement Method
SLA metrics for the monitoring queue, plus sampled reviews of break-glass events.
Rationale
In a social-services breach, the people most at risk are those under active protection (TA §C.16.2).
Parameters
N17, N18
NFR-SEC-005 Must
Encryption and key management
- Data in transit: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
Data in transit: TLS everywhere, with mutual TLS between exchange participants.
Data at rest: encrypted in every store, backup and document store. Per-subject payload encryption applies only to fact classes assigned cryptographic erasure.
One key inventory records, for each key, the custodian role, how it is held, how it is rotated, how it is destroyed, and what becomes unreadable if it is lost.
Per-subject data keys are wrapped by a master key in a hardware security module or the platform key service. They are never exported in plaintext and never held in escrow. The wrapping key rotates once a year.
Measurement Method
The key inventory is reviewed at each gate. Destruction is verified by showing that a known ciphertext can no longer be decrypted.
Rationale
A key whose loss makes twenty years of determinations unverifiable needs different handling from one whose loss only means reissuing a certificate (TA §C.16.3, §B.7.3).
Parameters
N12, N08
NFR-SEC-006 Must
Secrets management
No secret appears in code, configuration, design documents or logs. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
No secret appears in code, configuration, design documents or logs. Secrets are kept in the platform secrets service. No connection uses clear-text authentication.
Measurement Method
Secret scanning in CI and across document repositories, plus a credential inventory.
Rationale
The platform already provides secrets management, and the system reuses it (TA §C.18).
Parameters
N11, N18
NFR-SEC-007 Must
Vulnerability management and penetration testing
- SBOM generation, licence scanning and vulnerability scanning block builds in CI, across the whole platform. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
SBOM generation, licence scanning and vulnerability scanning block builds in CI, across the whole platform.
An independent tester runs a penetration test at each module gate. It covers what changed, plus a standing set of identity, access and exchange-edge tests.
Remediation: critical findings are fixed, or formally risk-accepted by a named executive, before the gate closes. High findings are fixed within 30 days with a tracked plan. Medium findings are fixed within 90 days. Low findings go into the backlog with an expiry date TA-C35. Risk acceptances expire after 90 days.
Measurement Method
Gate evidence. An open critical finding means the gate fails.
Rationale
A finding without a fix date is an open finding (TA §C.16.1).

Both are required artefacts at the release gate.
Rationale

N18
NFR-SEC-009 Must
Records that show if they have been tampered with
The decision record store, the event backbone and the access-decision stream are hash-chained. Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE ---
Requirement
The decision record store, the event backbone and the access-decision stream are hash-chained. Chain heads are signed and kept separately from the store, under different administrative control. An offline verifier can check integrity without the live systems.
Amended v1.5 (TA §B.5.5 item 6): the covered streams are named, and for money they are: the payment instruction and disbursement streams of Payments & Benefit Issuance; the double-entry event log of Financial Components; and the assessment, agreement and write-off streams of Overpayment & Recovery. None of these is left to a later judgement of where integrity matters.
Measurement Method
A job that verifies the chain, plus a tampering simulation in test.
Rationale
Records examined years later need integrity designed in, not assumed (TA §C.4.4, §B.5.5).

N08, N13
NFR-SEC-010 Must
Evidence of exchanges with other organisations
The system reaches four evidence tiers for cross-organisation exchange: Show detail
Priority: MUST_HAVE (E1, E2) · SHOULD_HAVE (E3) · COULD_HAVE (E4) ---
Requirement
The system reaches four evidence tiers for cross-organisation exchange:
E1, in place before the first production exchange: every request and response is logged with participant, agreement, legal basis, purpose, correlation identifier, timestamp and hashes of the message bodies.
E2, at launch: the log is hash-chained, and signed chain heads are kept independently.
E3, within the first year: chain heads get trusted timestamps.
E4: each message is signed, for a named class of disclosures agreed with legal counsel.
